interesting_fact: Casa dos Ventos calls data centers its main growth vector: it signed a ~US$500M renewable supply deal with Ascenty (Jan 2026) and is exclusive power supplier to a large data-center campus at the port of Pecém, Ceará, linked to ByteDance/TikTok.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Crato, Ceará, son of an engineer in Brazil's federal anti-drought works department; he trained as an aeronautical-mechanical engineer at ITA. The wind idea came from ITA classmate Odilon Camargo, who urged him to be first to map Brazil's wind potential; he then used the Troller sale cash to prospect the Northeast.
notes: Company accounts, not personal. Son Lucas Araripe is CEO and the public face for data-center strategy; Mário gives occasional interviews (Forbes Brasil, Diário do Nordeste). Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Contact form is commercially oriented; no published press email found.

name: Gao Guangrong
current_role: Chairman, Eoptolink Technology Inc. (新易盛, SZSE: 300502), Chengdu
profile: Sichuan-born (1969) optical-communications engineer who co-founded Eoptolink with five partners in 2008 and listed it on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Eoptolink makes high-speed optical transceivers (400G/800G/1.6T) for AI clusters and cloud data centers and has boomed with AI build-outs, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink, once focused on domestic telecom, only broke into overseas hyperscaler (e.g. Amazon) supply chains around 2019; with Innolight and TFC it is nicknamed one of China's 'Yi-Zhong-Tian' AI optical-module trio, and its market cap passed RMB 350B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A technical-school graduate (industrial electrical automation, Chengdu Radio Machinery School), he joined the optical-communications branch of Leshan Radio Factory at 20 as a technician and stayed 10 years, then rotated through tech, purchasing, sales and management jobs before founding Eoptolink at 39.

public_contacts.value: daniel.wang@eoptolink.com (Wang Cheng, board secretary); vivi.wei@eoptolink.com (securities affairs rep)

notes: Low public profile; route via board secretary/IR. Note: CSRC issued an administrative penalty in Feb 2025 over his 2023 share sales (avoid in outreach). Strong data-center/AI angle.

name: Lisa Su
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
profile: Taiwan-born, Bronx Science- and MIT-trained (BS/MS/PhD EE) semiconductor engineer who worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale before joining AMD in 2012 and becoming CEO in 2014. She led one of tech's great turnarounds; her wealth comes from AMD stock. Now she is pushing AMD's Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs into AI data centers, including a 2025 compute partnership with OpenAI, against Nvidia.
interesting_fact: At IBM she played a key role in developing the 'recipe' to replace aluminum interconnects with copper on chips without contaminating them, a technology launched in 1998 that yielded chips up to ~20% faster.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT freshman her UROP job was 'pure grunt work' making two-inch wafers in Hank Smith's semiconductor lab in Building 39 for x-ray lithography research; that plus summer jobs at Analog Devices hooked her on semiconductors. Her PhD was among the earliest work on silicon-on-insulator (SOI).
notes: Extremely high-demand speaker; formal route is AMD Corporate Communications (corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com). Active on X (@LisaSu). Natural fit for AI data-center compute/power topics. Distant relative of Nvidia's Jensen Huang (often raised; she downplays it).

name: Cristiano Crippa
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO), since 2017
profile: Cristiano Crippa co-founded Technoprobe with his father Giuseppe Crippa (an ex-SGS/STMicroelectronics manager, d. 2025), which makes probe cards that test microchips; it is now the world's No. 2 probe-card maker with ~2,700 staff. Technoprobe listed in Milan in 2022 and later joined the FTSE MIB; Cristiano owns about 18% and has chaired the board since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Technoprobe became the first company in Italy to open a COVID vaccination hub for the general public inside its premises: a 4,300 m2 space where 160,000 doses were given to local residents over six months.
deep_cut_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco), while his father was still working at SGS/ST; in 1997 it bought its first building in nearby Cernusco Lombardone and moved in with about 10 employees.
notes: Founding year differs by source (Forbes: 1989 with his father; company history: garage start 1993, incorporated 1996). Family-run, low media profile; press@technoprobe.com is the published route. Father Giuseppe died July 2025 - avoid leading with that.

name: Roberto Crippa
current_role: Vice President (and Vice Chairman of the Board), Technoprobe S.p.A.
profile: Roberto Crippa is the son of the late Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who founded probe-card maker Technoprobe in his garage in 1989. Roberto joined in 2002, ran Italian operations and has been Vice President since 2013; Technoprobe, whose probe cards test chips before packaging (including for AI processors), listed on Euronext Milan in 2022 and Roberto owns about 18%.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in 1989 in Giuseppe Crippa's garage and attic while he was still working at STMicroelectronics; it became a global top probe-card supplier and made the founder a billionaire in his late 80s.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Politecnico di Milano, he started in a technical product-development role and is author or co-author of numerous international patents; in 2018 he and brother Cristiano led the 100% acquisition of hydraulics-components engineer DA-TOR, starting a diversification into an Italian industrial hub.
notes: Forbes named him among Italy's top 100 managers in 2019. Gave a 2023 interview to Corriere della Sera's L'Economia (https://technoprobe.com/news-and-press/news-events-publications/leconomia-interview-with-roberto-crippa). Company is in Cernusco Lombardone (Lecco). info@ is a general company address.

name: Michael S. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Freeport LNG (Houston); director, Teledyne Technologies
profile: Made his first fortune with Basin Exploration, an E&P company he founded in Fort Collins in 1981 and sold to Stone Energy in 2001 for ~$428M. He founded Freeport LNG in 2002 as an import terminal, then flipped it to exports when shale arrived, raising $15B+ of debt to build three liquefaction trains in Freeport, Texas (~15 Mtpa). He still runs it and speaks publicly on U.S. LNG export economics.
interesting_fact: Freeport LNG was designed to import gas; when the shale boom hit he turned the strategy 180 degrees and built one of the largest U.S. LNG export terminals instead.
deep_cut_fact: Though he left CSU just shy of a chemistry degree, his 2016 $13M gift to Colorado State created 50 full-tuition business scholarships for the college's 50th anniversary and completed funding for the Michael Smith Natural Resources Building; he credited 'strong science and mathematics' at CSU for teaching him the oil business.
notes: Company is private. Freeport LNG press releases list media contact Heather Browne, Director Corporate Communications (phone 713-980-2888, office line), e.g. https://freeportlng.com/files/docs/FINAL-Restart-Press-Release-022123-2.pdf. Info@ email dates from a 2018 release. Speaks at CERAWeek/Milken - conference route possible.

name: Ravi Ruia
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Essar Group (senior family figure since brother Shashi's death in Nov 2024)
profile: Co-founded Essar with elder brother Shashi in 1969, growing it from a Chennai port construction contract into a conglomerate spanning steel, oil refining, power, ports and telecom. Essar bought the Stanlow refinery (Essar Oil UK, now EET Fuels) from Shell in 2011 and sold its Indian refiner to a Rosneft-led group for $12.9bn in 2017; it now pursues energy-transition projects at Stanlow.
interesting_fact: The name Essar comes from the brothers' initials, 'S' and 'R' (Shashi and Ravi); the group's first job was a 1969 contract worth about Rs 2.3 crore to build an outer breakwater for Chennai (Madras) Port.
deep_cut_fact: He is a mechanical engineer by training, a graduate of the College of Engineering, Guindy in Chennai - India's oldest engineering college (founded 1794) - and was singled out as one of its six most notable alumni when it turned 225 in 2018.
notes: Essar's corporate press contacts are on essar.com press releases (Essar Capital corporate affairs) and EET Fuels (Stanlow) releases, but those sites blocked automated fetching, so no email was verified. Forbes profile is joint with Shashi Ruia (died 2024). Best route: Essar corporate affairs office.

name: Walter Faria
current_role: Owner and controlling shareholder, Grupo Petrópolis (Itaipava, Crystal, Petra, Black Princess beers), Brazil
profile: Brazilian brewer (b. 1955, Pedranópolis, SP) who went from a cotton gin to Brazil's largest Schincariol distributor, then bought Cervejaria Petrópolis in 1998 at ~2% market share; by 2013 Itaipava made it Brazil's No. 2 brewer. The group also makes TNT energy drink - likely the source of the 'energy' tag, not the energy sector.
interesting_fact: Under Faria, Grupo Petrópolis grew from about 2% of Brazil's beer sales in 1998 to over 11% and the No. 2 national brand in 2013, largely through aggressive marketing and low prices.
deep_cut_fact: At 13, in the Macedônia district of Fernandópolis (SP), he sold eggs and piglets around town using a horse cart - a cart he kept as a keepsake. His savings then funded a coffee-processing business with a brother.

public_contacts.value: VCRP Brasil (press relations for Grupo Petrópolis, South/Southeast, appointed 2024)

notes: Very private, gives no interviews. Carries significant legal baggage (Lava Jato 2019 arrest; group filed for judicial recovery in 2023) - poor fit and sensitive; avoid these topics. Weak link to the energy theme (beverages only). Company site blocks automated access; press route is via the group's PR agencies.

name: Garibaldi Thohir
current_role: Vice President Commissioner, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (formerly Adaro Energy; stepped down as President Director at the June 2025 AGM)
profile: Garibaldi 'Boy' Thohir, son of Astra co-founder Teddy Thohir and brother of Erick Thohir, led the 2005 takeover of coal miner Adaro and ran it for ~2 decades, steering it toward aluminium smelting, minerals and renewables (now AlamTri; coal spun off as AADI in 2024). He is also a tech investor (ex-Gojek commissioner).
interesting_fact: He served as president commissioner of Gojek after founder Nadiem Makarim joined the cabinet in 2019, and has said he advised Nadiem informally for years before Gojek scaled.
deep_cut_fact: Back from his US MBA, he wanted a $2,000-a-month job at Citibank, but his father refused and told him to be an entrepreneur. His first venture (1991) was a plan to build a rental office on a 3,000 m2 plot along the new Saharjo-Kuningan road in Jakarta; it stalled because land clearances required at least 1 hectare.
notes: Widely known as 'Boy Thohir'. corsec@ is AlamTri's corporate secretary (company office, not personal). Some data sites still list him as President Director - outdated since June 2025. Energy-transition angle: AlamTri is building an aluminium smelter and hydro/renewables in North Kalimantan.

name: Semahat Arsel
current_role: Chair, Vehbi Koç Foundation board & executive committee; board member, Koç Holding; chair, Divan Group
profile: Semahat Sevim Arsel (b. 1928, Ankara) is the eldest child of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç and holds a stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate (energy via Tüpraş, Aygaz, autos, appliances, banking). On Koç's board since 1964, she built its tourism/hospitality arm and leads the family's main foundation.
interesting_fact: Turkey's only postgraduate nursing education center, SANERC (founded 1992 at the American Hospital, Istanbul), is named after her; she has chaired the Vehbi Koç Foundation's Nursing Committee since its nursing fund began in 1974.
deep_cut_fact: In 1972 she took charge of renovating Istanbul's Divan Hotel in Elmadağ and went on to turn 'Divan' into a luxury hospitality brand; she also co-founded TUGEV, a foundation for tourism training, and lived in Germany in 1959-60, studying at the Goethe Institute.
notes: Aged 98 and very private; no personal public channels. Best route is via the Vehbi Koç Foundation or Koç Holding corporate communications. Koç's energy link (Tüpraş refining, Aygaz, Entek power) is the podcast angle.

name: Lukas Henrik Lundin
profile: Swedish-Canadian resource financier who chaired the Lundin Group of mining and energy companies for 25+ years (Lundin Mining, Lucara Diamond, Filo Mining, NGEx etc.); family holdings were held via the Nemesia trust vehicle. He died on 26 July 2022 in Geneva, aged 64, after a two-year battle with brain cancer.
notes: Deceased 26 July 2022 (sources: https://www.mining.com/?p=1096241 ; https://filomining.mediaroom.com/2022-07-27-Filo-Minings-Founder-and-Former-Chairman-Lukas-H-Lundin-Passes-Away). Sons Adam and Jack Lundin now lead Lundin Group companies; the Lundin family remains long-term shareholders.

name: Guo Jianjun
current_role: Listed by Hurun under 'Huineng' (likely Inner Mongolia Huineng Group, Ordos coal/coal-to-gas); role not verified
profile: Hurun lists Guo Jianjun (郭建军) with wealth from 'Huineng', an energy business. The best-known match, Inner Mongolia Huineng Group (Ordos; coal, coal chemicals, coal-to-gas, new energy), is publicly led by chairman Guo Jinshu (郭金树); no public source found linking Guo Jianjun to the group.
notes: Identity unresolved: searches find Huineng Group chairman Guo Jinshu, not Guo Jianjun; possibly a relative, another executive, or a Hurun name variant. Do not conflate with Maj. Gen. Guo Jianjun (PLA, Ningxia). Verify via Hurun's Chinese list or company registry before outreach.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Sandra Irving
current_role: Philanthropist; co-owner of Irving Oil family interests; advisory board member, Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society (Dartmouth)
profile: Saint John, New Brunswick-born widow of Arthur L. Irving (d. May 2024), longtime chairman of Irving Oil, the private refiner/marketer that runs Canada's largest refinery in Saint John; their daughter Sarah Irving is now the family's leader at the company. Sandra is a major donor to education and medical research in Atlantic Canada and the US.
interesting_fact: With Arthur and Sarah, she co-funded the $80M lead gift that created Dartmouth's Arthur L. Irving Institute for Energy and Society, and she sits on its advisory board; she and Arthur were adopted as honorary members of Dartmouth's Class of 1972.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a BA with distinction from the University of New Brunswick and an MA in Political Science from the University of Toronto, and is an honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada; with Arthur she endowed chairs in cardiology and oncology at Massachusetts General Hospital.

public_contacts.value: https://irvingoil.com/en-CA/press-room (Irving Oil press room; media contact listed as Sam Robinson, Public Affairs)

notes: Very private; no personal public channels. Arthur Irving died May 13, 2024. Most plausible routes are Irving Oil Public Affairs or the Dartmouth Irving Institute (energy/society angle fits the podcast).

name: Ilya Sutskever
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), Palo Alto / Tel Aviv
profile: Soviet-born Israeli-Canadian AI scientist (b. 1986) who co-created AlexNet with Hinton and Krizhevsky, co-founded OpenAI and served as chief scientist through GPT/ChatGPT and o1-style reasoning. He left in 2024 to co-found SSI, which raised $3B+ at a ~$32B valuation; CEO since July 2025. In July 2026 SSI announced an NVIDIA partnership to scale its compute 10x.
interesting_fact: He won the NeurIPS Test of Time Award three years in a row (2022-2024) and received the National Academy of Sciences Award for the Industrial Application of Science in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Jerusalem he began taking Open University of Israel classes in eighth grade; after moving to Canada at 16 he spent only about a month in high school before the University of Toronto admitted him straight into third year.
notes: Very media-shy; rare interviews (e.g. Dwarkesh Podcast, Nov 2025). SSI is compute-heavy (NVIDIA deal, earlier Google Cloud TPUs) - relevant data-center angle. comms@ssi.inc is the only published inquiry address.

name: Andre Desmarais
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial Corporation
profile: André Desmarais (b. 1956, Ottawa) is the youngest son of Paul Desmarais Sr. He and his brother Paul Jr. were co-CEOs of Power Corporation, the Montreal financial holding company, for about 24 years until 2020. He remains deputy chairman and sits on group boards including Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial and Power Sustainable, the group's renewables arm.
interesting_fact: He is honorary chairman of the Canada China Business Council and served on the Hong Kong Chief Executive's Council of International Advisers from 1998 to 2007.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at Campeau Corporation in 1979 and was a special assistant to Canada's Minister of Justice in 1980-81 before joining Power Corp in 1983. He also started and owned an experimental farm in Canada.

public_contacts.value: Media requests: Stéphane Lemay, VP, General Counsel & Secretary, Power Corporation of Canada (phone listed on contact page; no email published)

notes: No personal social accounts were found. The best route is Power Corporation's media-requests contact. For the energy angle, Power Sustainable (renewables and energy infrastructure) is the relevant group company. The first contact entry is a named media contact with a published phone number only; no email is published.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr.
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada (and Power Financial); also long-time chairman of Groupe Bruxelles Lambert
profile: Eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr. (born Sudbury, 1954; McGill BComm, INSEAD MBA). He joined Power Corp in 1981, led the creation of Power Financial in 1984 and was co-CEO of Power Corp from 1996 until stepping back in 2020; he remains chairman. Power's holdings span Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial, GBL, Sagard and Power Sustainable.
interesting_fact: He sat on the boards of major European energy groups, serving as a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, via the family's stakes held through Pargesa/Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm in 1981 he cut his teeth at S.G. Warburg & Co. in London and at Standard Brands in New York; in 1984 he led the creation of Power Financial Corporation.
notes: Energy angle is Power Sustainable (renewables/infrastructure; media pr@powersustainable.com per its 2025 release, https://powersustainable.com/en/news/power-sustainable-announces-plan-to-invest-and-mobilize-more-than-10-billion-into-canadian-infrastructure-and-related-companies/). Power Corp releases name Stephane Lemay (VP, General Counsel) as contact. Not to be confused with son Paul Desmarais III.

name: Surender Pal Singh Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (Hyderabad solar cell & module maker; listed NSE/BSE 2024)
profile: Mechanical engineer who founded Premier Energies in Hyderabad in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. The company grew into one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module manufacturers and listed in Sept 2024, making him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Singh Saluja is MD; the firm is expanding cell, module and storage capacity.
interesting_fact: Premier Energies began in 1995 selling small solar products such as lanterns and streetlights, decades before India's solar-manufacturing boom; it is now among the country's largest makers of solar cells and modules.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in mechanical engineering from Karnatak University, Dharwad, in 1969 and ran small ventures before solar; he has said his one slight regret is never having worked as an employee at a corporation early in his career.

public_contacts.value: mohit.chawla@premierenergies.com (Mohit Chawla, Marketing & Communications, Premier Energies)

notes: Name also spelled Surendar Singh Saluja. Day-to-day public face of the company is son and MD Chiranjeev Saluja; route through company communications. Strong energy/solar-manufacturing fit.

name: Lee Bass
current_role: Private investor (Lee M. Bass, Inc., Fort Worth); rancher and conservationist; Chairman Emeritus, The Peregrine Fund
profile: Lee M. Bass is one of the four Fort Worth Bass brothers who turned an inheritance from oilman uncle Sid Richardson into multibillion-dollar fortunes through oil and investing; in 2017 the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil for $5.6B in stock. He runs his own investments, raises longhorns on South Texas ranches and is a leading Texas conservation philanthropist.
interesting_fact: He chaired the Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named chair by Gov. George W. Bush; chairman emeritus since 2001) and with wife Ramona funded the reintroduction of the endangered Aplomado falcon in South Texas; they entered the Texas Conservation Hall of Fame in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a founding member of the International Rhino Foundation, and he and Ramona helped found 'South Texas Natives' (now the Texas Native Seeds Program) at the Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute; he has also chaired the TPWD White-Tailed Deer Advisory Committee.
notes: Very private; no personal website or social accounts found. Plausible indirect routes: The Peregrine Fund (peregrinefund.org) or Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, where he holds honorary/emeritus roles - neither publishes a contact for him personally.

name: Wang Hui (David H. Wang)
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, ACM Research Inc. (Nasdaq: ACMR); chairman of its Shanghai-listed subsidiary ACM Research (Shanghai) / Shengmei Semiconductor (盛美上海)
profile: Tsinghua- and Osaka-trained engineer who founded ACM Research in Silicon Valley in 1998, then built it out in Shanghai as a maker of wafer-cleaning, electroplating, furnace and PECVD equipment for chip fabs. His wealth comes mainly from the Shanghai STAR-listed unit. He still runs the company, which is expanding into advanced-packaging tools.
interesting_fact: EY's 2023 World Entrepreneur Of The Year program (Chinese mainland) credits Wang with inventing stress-free copper polishing and holding more than 100 patents. It says his cleaning technologies can cut use of hazardous chemicals such as sulfuric acid by 50-80%.
deep_cut_fact: Wang entered Tsinghua's precision instruments department in 1978. He first went to Japan to study industrial robotics at the University of Tokyo but was referred to Osaka University because his assigned professor was retiring. After a postdoc at the University of Cincinnati, he worked at Quester Technology (1993-98) before founding ACM.
notes: Known in English as David H. Wang. The IR contacts are at The Blueshirt Group (Steven Pelayo, US; Gary Dvorchak, China). Media contact is Alyssa Lundeen at Bodewell Group. Relevant to AI/data-center chip supply chains.

name: Carl Icahn
current_role: Chairman and controlling holder, Icahn Enterprises L.P. (Nasdaq: IEP); large holder in CVR Energy, CVR Partners, Southwest Gas, Centuri, Monro
profile: Veteran activist investor from Far Rockaway, Queens, who went from Dreyfus stockbroker to buying an NYSE seat in 1968 and became one of Wall Street's most famous corporate raiders. He invests mainly through Icahn Enterprises, whose energy arm CVR Energy (refining, fertilizer) is a core holding; Ted Papapostolou became IEP CEO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: His mother pushed him into medical school; he dropped out of NYU med school after two years because he hated it, joined the Army Reserve, and ended up on Wall Street. He has given about $200M to what is now the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai.
deep_cut_fact: His Princeton philosophy thesis, 'The Problem of Formulating an Adequate Explication of the Empiricist Criterion of Meaning,' won the McCosh Prize; he called writing it 'exhilarating,' said it was the most rewarding part of Princeton, and still keeps a copy. He also worked on the business side of The Daily Princetonian.
notes: Age ~90, now based in Florida (IEP moved HQ to Sunny Isles Beach). IR@ielp.com was the IEP investor contact in Feb 2026 releases; after May 2026 releases list only phone for CEO Ted Papapostolou. X account rarely used recently. Energy angle: CVR Energy/CVR Partners, Southwest Gas.

name: Marina Budiman
current_role: Co-founder & President Commissioner, PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (DCII)
profile: Indonesian tech entrepreneur who co-founded DCI Indonesia in 2011 with Otto Toto Sugiri and Han Arming Hanafia; DCI runs Southeast Asia's first Tier IV data center and leads Indonesia's colocation market. Earlier: Bank Bali banker, CFO of Sigma Cipta Caraka (2000-08), Indonet co-founder (1994). DCI president director 2012-16, president commissioner since.
interesting_fact: Named one of Forbes Asia's 20 'Asia's Power Businesswomen' in 2021; by 2025 she was ranked among Indonesia's 10 richest people and the country's richest woman.
deep_cut_fact: She has no tech degree (University of Toronto, finance/economics) and planned to be a banker; a 1985 software-installation project at Bank Bali convinced her tech could power business. Her line: 'You will never get bored with the tech sector.'
notes: Rarely interviewed; little personal media presence. DCI is central to Indonesia's AI/hyperscale data-center build-out, a strong podcast angle. Best route via DCI corporate secretary. Net worth figures vary widely with DCII's volatile share price.

name: Fernando Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Vice Chairman, Ayala Corporation; Chairman, AC Health; director of Ayala Land and BPI (as of 2025)
profile: Fernando Zobel de Ayala (b. 1960), seventh generation of the family behind Ayala Corporation, the Philippine conglomerate spanning property, banking, telecoms and energy (ACEN). He was Ayala's President/COO for 15 years and CEO 2021-2022, stepped back in 2022, and has since returned to board roles, chairing AC Health and Ayala Foundation.
interesting_fact: Long active in Habitat for Humanity: he was Vice Chairman of Habitat for Humanity International and chaired its Asia-Pacific capital campaign steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: A serious arts patron: he helped the founders develop Art Fair Philippines in its early days, sits on international advisory committees of Tate Modern, the Met and Art SG, and in 2025 funded CIMAM travel grants for Philippine curators and museum professionals.
notes: Input middle name 'Augusto' looks like a mix-up with his brother Jaime Augusto; he is Fernando Miranda Zobel de Ayala. Ayala's energy arm is ACEN. Route via Ayala Corporation corporate communications (ayala.com contact page); I could not verify a published press email. He took a medical leave in 2022, so avoid the topic.

name: Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala
current_role: Chairman, Ayala Corporation (Philippines); also chairs BPI and ACEN (formerly AC Energy)
profile: Eldest son of the Zobel de Ayala family (b. 1959; Harvard AB '81, MBA '87); succeeded his father as Ayala Corp. CEO in 1994 and led the conglomerate (property, banking, telecom, energy) as chairman & CEO 2006-2021. Now non-executive chairman; Ayala's ACEN is a major SE Asian renewables platform.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he became the first Filipino to receive Harvard Business School's Alumni Achievement Award, its highest honour; in 2017 the UN Global Compact named him the first Southeast Asian SDG Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: A rugby devotee who played county-level rugby in Sussex as a teen at English boarding school, he flew to France for the 2007 World Cup to cheer the All Blacks; at Harvard he rowed lightweight crew briefly and calls quitting 'one of my big regrets.'
notes: Correct spelling is Jaime (not Jamie). Wikipedia links an official Facebook page for him. Best route is Ayala Corp. corporate communications; ACEN is the energy angle.

name: Peter Shu
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Transcend Information Inc. (TWSE: 2451), Taipei.
profile: Peter Shu (Shu Chung-won, b. 1954) is a National Cheng Kung University electrical-engineering graduate and ex-HP engineer who founded Transcend in 1988-89. He built it into a major global brand of memory modules, flash cards, SSDs and USB drives with thousands of niche SKUs. In 2026 he was again named among Harvard Business Review's Taiwan Top 100 CEOs as memory prices surged.
interesting_fact: Transcend has made more than 2,000 specialised memory and board products and served 5,000+ long-term customers; Shu said in 2026 the company had not borrowed from banks in 17 years.
deep_cut_fact: Transcend began with Chinese printing: as an HP engineer Shu had worked on Chinese support for HP's LaserJet; after leaving he wrote the Chinese printer software alone in 3-4 months working 13-14 hour days. It sold 12,000 sets in year one at NT$2,500 royalty each, funding the company.
notes: Taiwan-based (listed as China in input). IR email per Transcend's shareholder-services page and 2024 annual report (spokesperson listed as Chen Po-Shou); company sites were not reachable by curl from here, so verified via search snippets. Early product was the Key Pro software-protection dongle.

name: Safra Catz
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation (CEO 2014-Sept 2025); director, Paramount Skydance
profile: Israeli-born American executive who joined Oracle from investment bank DLJ in 1999 and rose to president, CFO and CEO (co-CEO with Mark Hurd from 2014, sole CEO from 2019). Her wealth is largely Oracle stock. In Sept 2025, amid Oracle's AI data-center build-out, she handed over to co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia and became executive vice chair.
interesting_fact: She is credited with driving Oracle's $10.3bn hostile takeover of PeopleSoft in 2005, and in 2011 was the highest-paid woman among Fortune 1000 companies.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Holon, Israel, she moved to Brookline, Massachusetts at age six and graduated from Brookline High School; alongside running Oracle she has been a lecturer in accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
notes: SEC insider data still lists her as CEO; she became Executive Vice Chair on 22 Sept 2025. Very press-shy; best route is Oracle corporate communications.

name: Adebayo Ogunlesi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Global Infrastructure Partners (a part of BlackRock); Senior Managing Director, BlackRock; OpenAI board member
profile: Nigerian-born lawyer turned banker and infrastructure investor. After Cravath and 23 years at Credit Suisse, he cofounded Global Infrastructure Partners in 2006, building it to $100B+ AUM across energy, transport, digital infrastructure and water before selling it to BlackRock for $12.5B in 2024. He joined OpenAI's board in January 2025.
interesting_fact: Early in his career he clerked for Justice Thurgood Marshall, the first Black U.S. Supreme Court justice; he holds degrees from Oxford (BA), Harvard Law (JD) and Harvard Business School (MBA).
deep_cut_fact: Alongside his dealmaking he has taught courses on transnational investment projects at Harvard Law School, Yale Law School and the Yale School of Management.
notes: Very strong energy + AI data-center angle (GIP owns energy/digital infra; OpenAI board; GIP part of the BlackRock/MGX/Microsoft AI Infrastructure Partnership). Also director of Kosmos Energy and Topgolf Callaway. Route via BlackRock Americas corporate communications.

name: Qian Peixin
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Wang Liping) of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic Co. (SSE: 601100)
profile: Qian Peixin (钱佩新) is co-actual controller, with husband and chairman Wang Liping, of Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic, a Changzhou maker of hydraulic cylinders, pumps and valves for excavators and machinery. The family controls ~64% of the Shanghai-listed firm. She is not a public-facing executive.
interesting_fact: Hurun lists her among the world's self-made women billionaires (2020-2025) on the strength of the family's stake in Hengli Hydraulic, a key supplier of hydraulic components to excavator makers.
notes: Very low public profile; virtually no interviews. Only route is Hengli's board-secretary office (hlzqb@hengli.net, from 2025 annual report). Note: in March 2026 Hengli disclosed a provincial supervisory commission action concerning chairman Wang Liping; on 13 Apr 2026 it said he had resumed duties. Weak fit for an energy podcast.

name: Shen Xiqiang
current_role: Vice chairman and major shareholder, Jiangsu Yoke Technology Co. (雅克科技, 002409.SZ)
profile: Shen Xiqiang (沈锡强, about 78) co-founded Jiangsu Yoke in Yixing, Jiangsu in 1997 as a flame-retardant chemicals maker; it listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Yoke now makes semiconductor precursors, photoresists and specialty gases, plus LNG cryogenic insulation panels. His elder son Shen Qi is chairman and his younger son Shen Fu is deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Yoke is both a chip-materials and an LNG-shipping supplier. Its insulation panels went into the world's first large Mark III Flex LNG carrier, and its LNG panel business grew 57% in 2025, while its high-k precursors go into DRAM, 3D NAND and AI advanced-packaging chips.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews found. The family business is now run by his sons, so Yoke's IR office (board secretary Qin Hongjian, per the 2025 annual report) is the realistic route. Bridges both of the podcast's themes: LNG energy shipping and semiconductor materials for AI chips.

name: Richard Rainwater
current_role: Deceased (died 27 September 2015, Fort Worth, Texas, aged 71)
notes: Died 27 Sep 2015 at his Fort Worth home (announced by the Rainwater Charitable Foundation). Sources: https://www.keranews.org/news/2015-09-28/fort-worth-billionaire-richard-rainwater-dies ; https://fortune.com/2015/09/28/richard-rainwater-obituary/ . Legacy continues via the Rainwater Charitable Foundation.

name: Nitin Sandesara
current_role: Promoter, Sandesara Group; owner of Sterling Oil Exploration & Energy Production Co. (SEEPCO), Nigeria
profile: Gujarat-born promoter of the Sandesara Group (Sterling Biotech, gelatin/pharma, energy). Since the mid-2000s the group's main asset has been Nigerian upstream producer SEEPCO, which holds OML 143 (Okwuibome field). Lived abroad from 2017 amid an Indian bank-fraud case; India's Supreme Court let criminal proceedings be closed in 2025-26 after a settlement with lenders.
interesting_fact: SEEPCO says it is the only Indian-owned crude producer operating in an OPEC member country; between March and May 2026 it shipped about 6M barrels of Okwuibome crude to IOC, BPCL and HPCL, avoiding the Strait of Hormuz.
deep_cut_fact: In July 2015 Africa Oil & Gas Report called the Sandesara venture Sterling Energy 'the busiest company on rig sites in Nigeria', with five rigs active at once. SEEPCO won OML 143 (then OPL 280) in Nigeria's 2005 bid round.

public_contacts.value: SEEPCO media contact: Deepak Sodhi, sendvisesolution@gmail.com

notes: Reputationally sensitive. He was declared a fugitive economic offender in India over the Sterling Biotech loan-fraud case. India's Supreme Court conditionally agreed in Nov 2025 to quash proceedings on payment of Rs 5,100 crore, and reports say the matter was closed in April 2026. Based in Nigeria. Hurun figure (2015) is dated. Only route found is SEEPCO's press-release media contact.

name: Xu Yanming (徐延铭)
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Zhuhai CosMX Battery Co. (珠海冠宇, SSE STAR 688772); deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Harbin Institute of Technology graduate who has worked on batteries for nearly 30 years. He led a team from Harbin's Guangyu group to Zhuhai in 2007 to found what became CosMX, a maker of polymer lithium-ion batteries for laptops, tablets and phones, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Per TSR data, CosMX ranked No.1 globally in laptop battery shipments in 2024.
interesting_fact: CosMX ranked first worldwide in notebook-PC lithium battery shipments and second in tablet batteries in 2024 (Techno Systems Research data), and held 2,400+ granted patents by mid-2025.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2026 Two Sessions he proposed that China's lithium-battery makers copy the solar industry's playbook: a cross-supply-chain patent pool led by top firms and a 'next-generation battery technology innovation alliance' to co-develop high-silicon anodes and solid-state batteries, replacing 'litigation instead of competition'.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable. Chaired CosMX board meeting March 30, 2026 per SSE filing. Founding story (Harbin Guangyu spin-out, HIT alumnus) from Chinese press profiles (cnstock); verify details before quoting. No personal social accounts found.

name: Li Xue
profile: Listed on the Hurun Global Self-Made Women list (2022) with US$2.8bn from 'Energy New Material' (packaging production). This most likely refers to Yunnan Energy New Material (SEMCORP), which began in packaging and is now a leading lithium-battery separator maker. I could not tie the name 李雪 to that company or any other in public sources.
notes: Identity unconfirmed. Searches in Chinese and English found no 李雪 linked to Yunnan Energy New Material (恩捷股份), where the known family executives are Paul Xiaoming Lee and Li Xiaohua/Sherry Lee. The Hurun entry may be a romanisation or name error. Verify against Hurun's original 2022 list before outreach.

name: Martin Viessmann
current_role: Non-executive member of the Board of Directors, Viessmann Generations Group (family investment holding, Battenberg/Allendorf, Germany)
profile: Grandson of founder Johann Viessmann (1917); led the heating-systems maker as managing partner/CEO from 1989 and pushed it into renewables and efficiency. After the 2024 sale of Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier, the family runs Viessmann Generations Group, an investment company 'co-creating living spaces for future generations', with son Max as co-CEO; Martin now sits on its board.
interesting_fact: A fitness buff and passionate skier, he holds a professional pilot's license and an honorary doctorate from the University of Wisconsin; Viessmann is a major winter-sports sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: In Dec 2012 he and wife Annette endowed UW Oshkosh's first-ever endowed chair, the Viessmann Endowed Chair in Sustainable Technology, capping a partnership that in 2011 opened the Western Hemisphere's first dry-fermentation anaerobic biodigester on that campus.

public_contacts.value: phiv@viessmann.com (Philine von Hardenberg, Director Corporate Communications, Viessmann Generations Group)

notes: Forbes bio calling him chairman of the executive board is outdated: group site lists him as non-executive board member; son Max Viessmann leads. Best route is Generations Group corporate communications. Strong US tie via UW Oshkosh partnership.

name: Susan Ocampo
current_role: Director, MACOM Technology Solutions (MTSI); co-founder, VP, Secretary & Treasurer of GaAs Labs LLC
profile: Filipino-American co-founder (with her late husband John Ocampo) of RF chipmaker Sirenza Microdevices in 1984 and of investment fund GaAs Labs in 2008, which bought MACOM in 2009. She is MACOM's largest individual shareholder (10%+ owner) and a board member; John died in November 2023. In 2026 she launched a $100M endowment fund in his memory for RF, microwave and photonics research.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 she announced the $100M John L. Ocampo Endowment Fund, one of the largest private funds ever for RF/microwave and photonics engineering research, with annual grants to universities (Tyndall National Institute in Cork was an early recipient).
deep_cut_fact: In 2021 she and John gave $25 million to Santa Clara University (John's alma mater, class of '79) to support STEM education and a new science and engineering facility.
notes: Extremely private; Gulf News noted almost no photos of her exist. Reportedly holds a BA from Maryknoll College, Manila (sources conflict). Best route likely MACOM IR or GaAs Labs (Los Altos, CA), which has no published contact found.

name: John Leigh
current_role: Retired; former Non-executive Director of CLP Holdings (1997-2024) and of The Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels; long-time director of Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons
profile: John Andrew Harry Leigh is a British-trained solicitor who joined Hong Kong utility CLP in 1986 and became a long-serving board member of Kadoorie-family companies (CLP Holdings, Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons). He retired from the CLP board in March 2024 and the HSH board at its May 2024 AGM.
interesting_fact: Leigh sat on the CLP Holdings board for 27 years (appointed February 1997, retired 2024), one of the longest tenures among the Kadoorie group's directors.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the board, he was CLP's in-house lawyer: Senior Legal Advisor, Company Secretary and General Manager - Corporate Affairs of the CLP Group from 1986 to 1996, after private practice as a solicitor in Hong Kong and the UK.
notes: Hurun attributes ~$2.75bn 'CLP' wealth to him, but filings show him as a Kadoorie-group director/adviser, not a named family member or major shareholder - the wealth attribution is unverified (possibly a family-trust/relative link). He is retired and very private; CLP contact is only an indirect route.

name: Shao Xiaomei
current_role: Shareholder / family co-owner of Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology (no executive title found)
profile: Shao Xiaomei is the wife of Liang Feng, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology (603659.SH), a maker of lithium-battery anode materials, separator coatings and coating equipment. Per Putailai's IPO prospectus she controlled a share block as representative of the Ningbo Shengyue holding partnership.
interesting_fact: Putailai's IPO prospectus records that Shao Xiaomei, via the Ningbo Shengyue partnership, controlled about 56.7 million shares alongside her husband's 35.5% direct stake; the company filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; virtually no English coverage. Wealth is tied to husband Liang Feng's Putailai stake. Best route is Putailai IR / board secretary office; consider Liang Feng as the more relevant interviewee.

name: Li Xiangping
current_role: Party Secretary and Chairman of the Board, Shandong Dongming Petrochemical Group (山东东明石化集团)
profile: Li Xiangping heads Shandong Dongming Petrochemical, one of China's largest private 'teapot' refiners, based in Heze, Shandong. He took over a near-bankrupt small refinery and grew it into a group with about RMB 50bn in assets and 8,000+ staff. He has since pushed it from fuels into downstream chemicals. Li has also served as a delegate to the National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Under Li, Dongming built the 20 Mt/yr Rizhao-Dongming crude pipeline, listed its subsidiary Hengchang Chemical in Singapore, and became the first private refiner in China to obtain crude-oil import qualification. In 2022 Shandong named him a 'provincial industry-leading entrepreneur'.
deep_cut_fact: Li set up an in-house 'brain trust' of 12 of China's top chemical experts to advise the group. His motto for fuel quality: '油品如同食品、滴滴都是承诺' (fuel is like food, and every drop is a promise).
notes: No verified official website or published press/IR email was found (the group is privately held). Coverage is mostly Chinese-language local and state media. The best route is probably through Heze or Shandong business media, or the company's general channels if an official site can be confirmed.

name: Liu Tin-Ren
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2025-2026) with wealth from MediaTek (semiconductors), but no public source links a person named Liu Tin-Ren / 刘丁仁 to MediaTek. MediaTek's founder-chairman is Ming-Kai Tsai; this may be a romanisation variant of another MediaTek founding executive or shareholder.
notes: Could not identify. Searches in English, simplified and traditional Chinese (刘丁仁/劉丁仁 + 联发科/聯發科, Hurun) found nothing. A MarketScreener insider page exists for a 'Ting Jen Liu', a former MediaTek executive deputy GM (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/TING-JEN-LIU-A058RJ/), who may be the same person, but this is unverified. Check the Hurun source entry before any outreach.

name: Surender Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (NSE: PREMIERENE), Hyderabad
profile: Surender Pal Singh Saluja, a mechanical engineer (Karnatak University), founded Hyderabad-based Premier Energies in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. It is now one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module makers; its 2024 IPO made him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Saluja is managing director.
interesting_fact: Premier makes solar cells, not just modules - rare in India, where most players import Chinese cells - and has benefited from India's domestic-content rules for solar.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he set up Premier Deep Well Hand Pumps in 1981 to sell pumps for rural drinking water; he has called Premier's early solar days 'a one-man show', selling lanterns before assembling modules by hand.
notes: Name also spelled Surendar / Surender Pal Singh Saluja. Son Chiranjeev (MD) is the public face and does most interviews - likely the better podcast route.

name: Li Xiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Li Auto Inc. (Nasdaq: LI; HKEX: 2015)
profile: Born in 1981, Li Xiang is a serial internet founder who started IT site PCPOP as a teenager, then founded auto portal Autohome (NYSE-listed) in 2005. In 2015 he founded Li Auto, which pioneered extended-range EVs in China and is known for family-oriented SUVs like the six-seat Li L9; it is dual-listed in New York and Hong Kong and has delivered over 1.8 million vehicles.
interesting_fact: Li Auto's Chinese name, Lixiang (理想, 'ideal'), is a homonym of his own name; he was also among China's first generation of Tesla owners.
deep_cut_fact: He started PCPOP.com to prove doubters wrong after poor grades, woke at 5 a.m. daily to grab early-morning traffic from rivals, and by 18 the site earned over RMB100,000 a year, more than 10x his parents' income (he wrote about this on Weibo in 2019).
notes: Input's sec_insider_companies field (JinkoSolar CEO) is a data mismatch: that is Li Xiande of JinkoSolar, a different person. Li Xiang is highly active on Weibo and has run online business courses; Li Auto is EV/automotive (energy-adjacent: proprietary Lianshan battery).

name: Irwin Jacobs
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman Emeritus, Qualcomm; philanthropist (San Diego)
profile: MIT/UCSD electrical-engineering professor who co-founded Linkabit (1968) and then Qualcomm (1985), commercialising CDMA, the technology underlying modern cellular networks; CEO until 2005 and chairman until 2009, he left the board in 2012. Now in his 90s, he remains a major San Diego philanthropist and still appears at events (TechCon Fellows Lifetime Achievement Award, April 2026).
interesting_fact: With John Wozencraft he co-wrote the 1965 textbook 'Principles of Communication Engineering', still in use decades later; UC San Diego's Jacobs School of Engineering is named for him and his late wife Joan.
deep_cut_fact: He nearly became a hotelier: a guidance counselor said there was 'no future' in engineering, so he enrolled in Cornell's School of Hotel Administration and worked a summer as a country-club cook before a roommate's teasing pushed him to switch to electrical engineering.
notes: Born 1933; confirmed active as of April 2026 (TechCon award, Cornell alumni fireside chat in La Jolla). No published personal/office contact found; most plausible routes are via UC San Diego (Jacobs School) or the Cornell Club of San Diego events. Not involved in Qualcomm operations.

name: Mikail Gutseriyev
current_role: Founder and owner of the SAFMAR group (Russneft, Neftisa, Russian Coal, A101 and media assets). He left the Russneft board after EU sanctions in 2021.
profile: Mikhail Gutseriev (born 1958 in Akmolinsk, Kazakh SSR) is an Ingush-Russian oil tycoon and former State Duma deputy. He founded Russneft in 2002 and built the SAFMAR conglomerate, which spans oil, coal, retail, real estate and media. He fled Russia in 2007 over tax charges, returned in 2010 and won Russneft back. Since 2021 he has been sanctioned by the EU, UK and others over ties to Belarus.
interesting_fact: He is also one of Russia's most prolific pop lyricists. Meduza called him 'the most poetic billionaire' and 'the country's main pop lyricist'. His Mikhail Gutseriev Production Center was named Record Label of the Year at the 2022 TopHit Music Awards.
deep_cut_fact: In 1994 he helped set up the Zone of Economic Well-being Ingushetia, described as the first free economic zone in the post-Soviet states. The Russian government created it by Resolution No. 740 and appointed him head of its financial sector.
notes: COMPLIANCE FLAG: he has been under EU, UK, Canadian, Swiss, Australian and NZ sanctions since 2021 (ties to Lukashenko's regime). The EU General Court annulled the 2024 listing in Oct 2025, but sanctions were renewed. Get legal advice before any engagement. He is very private, and the dataset spelling is 'Mikail Gutseriyev'. He no longer holds a formal Russneft post, so pr@russneft.ru is an indirect route.

name: Shouliang Miao
current_role: Chairman and President, Shenzhen Fuyuan Group (深圳市富源实业(集团)有限公司)
profile: Miao Shouliang (缪寿良, b. Dec 1955, Wuhua county, Meizhou, Guangdong) arrived in Bao'an, Shenzhen in 1987 with RMB 2,000 and ~30 fellow villagers to run a stone quarry, supplying aggregate for Shenzhen airport and the Guangzhou-Shenzhen expressway. Fuyuan Group (1993) grew into real estate, schools, hotels, hydropower stations and new-energy/sapphire-tech ventures. Former CPPCC national member.
interesting_fact: Nicknamed Shenzhen's 'Quarry King' (采石大王) after Fuyuan supplied stone for Shenzhen airport (bidding half the state quarries' price), the Beihuan Avenue and section B of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen expressway.
deep_cut_fact: At 23 he designed the first tobacco-shredding machine in Wuhua county; when rivals piled into shredding he switched to selling the machines, then exited at the peak. He also founded the Shenzhen Fuyuan martial-arts-and-academics school (文武学校) in 2000.
notes: Hurun lists him through 2026, so presumed alive (born 1955). No official Fuyuan Group website or press contact found; deep-cut source is a Chinese profile aggregator (cnpp.cn) - verify before use. Ifeng profile: https://finance.ifeng.com/people/detail/comchief/miushouliang.shtml. Honorary president of the Guangdong Hakka Chamber of Commerce.

name: Huang Sheng
current_role: Chairman & GM, Wuhan Guide Sensmart Tech (高德智感); director/VP at Wuhan Guide Infrared (002414.SZ) through Dec 2025
profile: Huang Sheng (黄晟, b. 1989) is the son of Huang Li, founder and controlling shareholder of Wuhan Guide Infrared, a Shenzhen-listed maker of infrared detector chips, thermal imagers and defence systems. He joined the group in 2016, became a director and vice-GM, and runs its consumer/industrial thermal-imaging arm Guide Sensmart. Hurun lists the family wealth jointly with his father.
interesting_fact: Huang Li and Huang Sheng have been ranked by Hurun as Hubei's richest (by residence); Guide Infrared is credited with breaking Western restrictions to achieve home-grown infrared chips in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a 2013 master's in control engineering from Huazhong University of Science and Technology, and in 2022 was elected a part-time vice-chairman of the Wuhan Federation of Industry and Commerce.
notes: Source of wealth listed as 'Guide Electrics' corresponds to Wuhan Guide Infrared (高德红外); wealth shared with father Huang Li. His Guide Infrared director term ended 22 Dec 2025 per lixinger; confirm current title. Defence-related company; mostly Chinese-language press.

name: Dewi Kam
current_role: Minority shareholder (~10%), PT Bayan Resources; power-plant investor (reported President Commissioner, PT Sumber Segara Primadaya)
profile: Indonesian investor whose fortune comes mainly from a roughly 10% stake in Bayan Resources, Indonesia's third-largest coal producer, controlled by Low Tuck Kwong. She also has interests in building and operating coal-fired power plants. Bayan's soaring shares in 2022-23 made her one of Indonesia's richest people; she keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: In 2023 Forbes ranked her the richest woman in Southeast Asia, after Bayan's share price roughly tripled during 2022 on high coal prices.
deep_cut_fact: Her power business reportedly includes PT Sumber Segara Primadaya, operator of the Cilacap coal power plant in Central Java (a 51/49 JV with PLN's Pembangkitan Jawa Bali), where she is listed as President Commissioner, and the 2x125 MW Jeneponto plant in South Sulawesi with Bosowa.
notes: Very private: no interviews, website or social media found. Bayan's corporate secretary is only an indirect route because she is a shareholder, not an executive. In 2026, Bayan's controlling shareholder was reported to be in sale talks (Haji Isam). Avoid the Katadata article's ICW/offshore-leaks material.

name: Sun Shoukuan
current_role: Chairman, Liaoning Jiachen Group (Yingkou, Liaoning)
profile: Self-made founder-chairman of Jiachen Group, a private metallurgy and coal-mining conglomerate in Yingkou, Liaoning, with interests in steel, refractories, coal chemicals, power generation, real estate and construction. Forbes puts him among the wealthiest entrepreneurs in northeast China; Hurun ranked him Liaoning's richest person in 2021 (RMB 45B).
interesting_fact: Hurun's 2021 list ranked him No. 137 in China with RMB 45 billion, making him Liaoning province's richest person for a second straight year.
deep_cut_fact: Born in October 1949 in Dashiqiao, Liaoning (China's magnesite/refractories hub), he studied silicate engineering at what is now the University of Science and Technology Liaoning.
notes: Chinese name usually written 孙寿宽 (Forbes romanizes as Sun Shoukuan). Very private; no official company website or press contact found. Energy angle: Jiachen has coal-chemical and power-generation businesses. Sources for bio are a Chinese list aggregator citing Hurun; verify before use.

name: Zhang Jianzhong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Moore Threads Technology (Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Zhang (James Zhang), born 1966 in Nanjing, spent about 14 years as Nvidia's global VP and China general manager before founding GPU designer Moore Threads in Beijing in October 2020. The firm makes full-function GPUs and AI training clusters. Its December 2025 STAR Market IPO jumped about 425% on day one, making his roughly 36% stake worth billions.
interesting_fact: After Moore Threads was put on the US Entity List in October 2023, Zhang told staff China's GPU industry was not in its 'darkest hour' and vowed to build 'China's highest-quality full-function GPU'. Two years later the company listed at a valuation near US$40bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before Nvidia, Zhang studied computer science at Nanjing University of Science and Technology. He was then a senior researcher at the national computer lab of the Automation Research and Design Institute of Metallurgical Industry (1990-92), followed by stints at HP China (from 1992) and Dell China (2001-06).
notes: mkt@mthreads.com is Moore Threads' published marketing and promotion contact; no dedicated press address was found. The company is on the US Entity List, which may matter for a US-based podcast. He gives few English-language interviews.

name: Huang Xiaolei
current_role: Director & general manager (CEO), Eoptolink Technology (Chengdu, 300502.SZ); co-actual controller with chairman Gao Guangrong
profile: Electronics engineer (born 1969) who co-founded Chengdu-based optical-module maker Eoptolink in 2008 with Gao Guangrong and others, serving as technical director then general manager; it listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Eoptolink now supplies high-speed (800G/1.6T) optical transceivers for AI data centres, reportedly to Google and Nvidia, with a Thailand plant online since 2023 and a Hong Kong listing in preparation.
interesting_fact: Most of Eoptolink's revenue comes from overseas hyperscale/AI customers; its Thailand plant (first overseas base) started in 2023 and phase two came online in 2025. Huang was named to Forbes China's Best CEO list.
deep_cut_fact: A 1991 Southeast University radio-engineering grad, he spent 1991-98 as an engineer at Chengdu Qianfeng Electronic Instrument Factory and in 1999 founded his own small firm, Huida Electronics, before joining the optical-module world as a test engineer and technical director.
notes: Highly relevant for AI data-center optics angle. Runs operations while chairman Gao Guangrong handles strategy (per 2025 annual report). Board secretary Wang Cheng (Daniel.wang@eoptolink.com) is listed in filings as the formal contact. Low English-language media presence.

name: F.C. Tseng
current_role: Director, TSMC (board member since 1997); Chairman, TSMC China and TSMC Education & Culture Foundation; Vice Chairman, Vanguard International Semiconductor
profile: Fan-Cheng Tseng is one of Morris Chang's longest-serving lieutenants: TSMC president 1998-2001, deputy CEO 2001-05 and vice chairman 2005-18. While Chang chased customers, Tseng consolidated TSMC internally. His TSMC shares made him a billionaire in 2024 amid the AI chip boom; he remains on the board and chairs TSMC China.
interesting_fact: Tseng has sat on TSMC's board since May 1997 and was its president from 1998 to 2001, before becoming vice chairman for 13 years (2005-2018).
deep_cut_fact: In 1976 ITRI sent him, with Shih Chin-tai and Robert Tsao, to RCA in the US for CMOS IC training: part of the first group of Taiwanese engineers to acquire integrated-circuit technology, seen as the spark of Taiwan's chip industry.
notes: Low public profile; appears at events in his role as chairman of the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation. TSMC corporate PR (press@tsmc.com) is the official route.

name: Bret Taylor
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sierra (AI customer-service agents); Chairman of the board, OpenAI
profile: Stanford-trained engineer who led the team that co-created Google Maps, co-founded FriendFeed (sold to Facebook, where he became CTO), built Quip (sold to Salesforce, where he rose to co-CEO) and chaired Twitter's board through the Musk sale. Co-founded Sierra with Clay Bavor in 2023; a roughly 25% stake at a $10B valuation made him a billionaire, and he has chaired OpenAI since Nov 2023.
interesting_fact: Facebook's 'Like' button came from FriendFeed, the startup Taylor co-founded and sold to Facebook in 2009; in Dec 2025 he bought a ~1% minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers.
deep_cut_fact: Recounting Google's pre-Maps local search, Taylor noted that a search for 'coffee near Menlo Park' returned only Sun Microsystems pages, because Sun's Java-themed site was full of coffee puns. His follow-up, Google Local, was a formative near-miss that led to Google Maps.
notes: Very accessible publicly (frequent podcast guest). He lists his personal Gmail on his own homepage backchannel.org, which is the best direct route. Strong fit for AI/data-centre themes given his OpenAI chairmanship.

current_role: Cofounder, Sierra (AI customer-service agents), San Francisco
profile: Clay Bavor cofounded Sierra with Bret Taylor in 2023 after 18 years at Google, where he rose from associate product manager to VP running Google Labs and its AR/VR work (Cardboard, Daydream, ARCore, Lens, Project Starline). name: Zadik Bino
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with family, via Bino Holdings) of FIBI Holdings / First International Bank of Israel
profile: Iraqi-born Israeli banker and investor (b. 1943/44). He was CEO of First International Bank of Israel (1978-86) and CEO of Bank Leumi (1987-89), then built a fortune controlling Paz Oil (from 1999, incl. the 2006 Ashdod refinery purchase and IPO) and later buying control of FIBI. name: Drew Houston
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO of Dropbox (transitioning to executive chairman after co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi was named in May 2026); Meta board member
profile: Drew Houston co-founded Dropbox with MIT classmate Arash Ferdowsi in 2007 at age 24, took it public on Nasdaq in 2018 and remains its largest individual shareholder (20%+). In May 2026 Dropbox named Ashraf Alkarmi co-CEO; Houston is to move to executive chairman after a transition. He has sat on Meta's board since 2020.
interesting_fact: Houston conceived Dropbox after repeatedly forgetting his USB flash drive as an MIT student; Dropbox became touted as Y Combinator's most successful early investment. At 15 he worked at an industrial robotics startup (Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: His first company, an online SAT-prep startup called 'The Accolade Group, LLC', was founded with Andrew Crick in a Chili's over onion strings when he was 21; while burned out on it he wrote a poker bot. His 2013 MIT commencement 'cheat sheet': a tennis ball, a circle and the number 30,000.
notes: Leadership transition in progress (co-CEO Alkarmi named May 26, 2026). Houston is an active public speaker on AI and 'Dropbox Dash'; route via Dropbox press team.

name: Guillermo Rauch
current_role: Founder and CEO, Vercel
profile: Self-taught engineer from Lanús, Argentina, who never finished high school; joined the MooTools core team as a teen and moved to San Francisco at 18. Created Socket.IO and Mongoose, sold Cloudup to Automattic, then founded ZEIT (2015), now Vercel, maker of Next.js and the v0 AI app builder; valued at $9B in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: His Socket.IO library's underlying engine powers Notion's real-time sync and powered Coinbase's first trading product; he also wrote one of the first books on Node.js, 'Smashing Node.js: JavaScript Everywhere'.
deep_cut_fact: He credits a now-defunct online hacking wargame, Izhal.com (level 1 was solved by finding a hidden HTML comment; later levels meant disassembling binaries and writing keygens), with teaching him reverse engineering and debugging more than any coding tutorial did.
notes: Very public and podcast-friendly; extremely active on X (@rauchg), which is the most direct route. Frequent guest on dev/startup podcasts.

name: Johnny Ho
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, Perplexity
profile: Former competitive programmer and Harvard math/CS student who worked as a Quora engineer and a quant trader at Tower Research before cofounding Perplexity in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Denis Yarats and Andy Konwinski. The AI answer engine, which cites its sources, hit a $20B valuation in 2025; Ho focuses on product strategy.

Forbes calls him a three-time IOI gold medalist; official IOI stats show gold 2011, gold (1st) 2012, silver 2013. No verified personal social/press email found; route via Perplexity communications.

current_role: Co-founder, chairman and board secretary, Enflame Technology (燧原科技, STAR Market 688801), Shanghai
