He bought 75% of Italian club Pisa in 2021 (promoted to Serie A in 2025) and has put the bulk of his assets into The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research.
interesting_fact: He named Pamplona Capital after the San Fermin festival in Pamplona, which he attended after graduating from Harvard Business School.
deep_cut_fact: Energy roots: in 1980, fresh out of Carnegie Mellon, he took a job as an engineer with Schlumberger working on oil platforms in the Gulf of Mexico. He later endowed the Alexander M. Knaster Scholarship Fund (1993) for CMU electrical & computer engineering undergrads.

public_contacts.value: ed.orlebar@tbcardew.com (Tavistock/TB Cardew - media enquiries for Pamplona)
info@themarkfoundation.org (The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research)

notes: Wikipedia article flagged for possible COI editing; facts used are biographical basics. Political donor (UK Conservatives) - avoid. Pamplona has moved away from energy; his podcast hooks are the Schlumberger start, Alfa-Bank era and Pisa football. Best route: Pamplona media contact at TB Cardew.

name: Sanjay Singal
current_role: Former chairman & managing director / promoter, Bhushan Power & Steel Ltd (company now owned by JSW Steel)
profile: Sanjay Singal, from the family behind the Bhushan steel businesses, built Bhushan Power & Steel into a large integrated steelmaker with operations in Odisha. The company went into insolvency in 2017, and JSW Steel took it over through a resolution plan (₹19,700 crore). He no longer controls the business and has spent recent years contesting the process in court.
interesting_fact: In September 2025 the Supreme Court of India upheld JSW Steel's ₹19,700 crore resolution plan for Bhushan Power & Steel, after briefly ordering liquidation in May 2025 at the former promoters' urging.
notes: He is a low-value and sensitive outreach target: he lost control of BPSL in insolvency, faced ED/CBI fraud proceedings, and the Supreme Court criticised the former promoters in 2025. No published contacts or public profile were found. No positive, sourced deep-cut fact was found.

name: Lin Zhiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Sanan Optoelectronics Co. (SSE: 600703), Xiamen; director at Fujian Sanan Group
profile: Eldest son of Sanan Group founder Lin Xiucheng (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Born 1974 in Anxi, Fujian, he joined the family group in 1996, became Sanan Optoelectronics' general manager in 2011 and chairman in July 2017. Sanan is China's largest LED chip maker and is expanding into SiC/GaN compound semiconductors for EVs, inverters and power electronics.
interesting_fact: Sanan reached the stock market via a 2008 backdoor listing into the suspended, loss-making Tianyi Technology, which was turned into China's LED chip leader after the family injected Sanan Electronics' LED wafer and chip assets.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economic management at the PLA Naval Command College and has served as a local people's congress deputy in Anxi County and in Xiamen's Siming District.
notes: IR email is the board-secretary contact in Sanan's 2025 annual report summary. Sensitive timing: in 2026 Sanan disclosed that founder Lin Xiucheng and vice-chairman Lin Kechuang were placed under investigation, and the company swung to losses. Deep-cut source is a secondary Chinese profile site; verify before use.

name: John B Hess
current_role: Director, Chevron Corp (since July 2025, after Chevron's $53B acquisition of Hess Corp); director, Goldman Sachs
profile: Son of Hess founder Leon Hess, he joined the family firm as a trainee in 1976 and was CEO from 1995 until 2025, turning Hess into an exploration-and-production company with a stake in Guyana's giant Stabroek oil discoveries and the Bakken. Chevron bought Hess for ~$53B (closed July 18, 2025) and he joined Chevron's board and its Public Policy & Sustainability Committee.
interesting_fact: Hess's 30% stake in Guyana's Stabroek block, one of the biggest oil finds of the past decade, was the main prize in Chevron's $53B takeover, which was delayed over a year by an arbitration with ExxonMobil.
deep_cut_fact: Despite growing up wealthy he pumped gas at the family's Hess stations, joined his father on foreign oil fields at age seven, and as a Harvard undergraduate studied in Beirut, becoming fluent in Arabic and Farsi.
notes: No personal or family-office contact published; Hess Corp no longer exists as a separate company, so Chevron (board) is the institutional route. Recent CEO talks frame oil and gas as needed alongside AI-driven power demand, a good podcast hook.

name: Thomas Kurian
current_role: CEO, Google Cloud (Alphabet), since January 2019
profile: Kerala-born, Princeton-trained engineer Thomas Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle, rising to president of product development over a ~35,000-person engineering org, which made him wealthy via Oracle equity. Since 2019 he has run Google Cloud, turning it into a profitable, fast-growing business at the centre of Google's AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: His identical twin George Kurian is CEO of NetApp; in 1996 the twins effectively swapped careers - George moved from Oracle to McKinsey while Thomas left McKinsey to join Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pampady, Kottayam, he and his twin boarded at Jesuit-run St Joseph's Boys' High School in Bangalore; both got into IIT Madras but took the SAT there and won partial scholarships to Princeton, moving to the US at 17. He graduated summa cum laude in electrical engineering.
notes: Wealth listed by Hurun is attributed to Oracle; he now runs Google Cloud - highly relevant for a data-center/AI podcast. Route via Google Cloud press team. X handle @ThomasOrTK ('CEO of @GoogleCloud') confirmed only via an aggregator; he is also active on LinkedIn.

name: Mahabir Prasad Agarwal
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (advisory), Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (NSE: SHYAMMETL); stepped down as chairman in May 2025
profile: Kolkata-based first-generation steel entrepreneur and co-promoter of Shyam Metalics and Energy, an integrated maker of ferro alloys, steel, aluminium foil and captive power, listed in 2021. He chaired the company until May 2025, when he resigned citing his age. Brij Bhushan Agarwal became chairman and MD, and Mahabir Prasad Agarwal stayed on as chairman emeritus.
interesting_fact: When he stepped down as chairman in May 2025, Shyam Metalics kept him on as chairman emeritus in an advisory role rather than letting him retire outright.
notes: Elderly and retired from the chair, so a low public profile. The company's Head of IR is Pankaj Harlalka, per the Nov 2026 earnings-call transcript. Unverified social posts say he started as a steel trader around 1970 and opened a sponge-iron plant in Sambalpur in 1990; these are not used as facts. The current chairman and MD, Brij Bhushan Agarwal, is the more active spokesman.

name: Stefan Fuchs
current_role: CEO (Chairman of the Executive Board), FUCHS SE, Mannheim (contract extended to June 2029)
profile: Third-generation family leader of FUCHS (formerly Fuchs Petrolub), founded in 1931 in Mannheim and now the world's largest independent lubricants supplier with ~6,000 staff in 50+ countries. He joined in 1996, entered the Executive Board in 1999 and has been CEO since 2004; the board extended his contract in Oct 2025 to 2029. (Input name 'Stefan Fuch' is a misspelling.)
interesting_fact: FUCHS has grown from a 1931 Mannheim family business into the world's largest independent supplier of lubrication solutions, independent of the oil majors; Stefan Fuchs has run it for more than 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent two years as an auditing assistant at Wollert-Elmendorff Deutsche Industrie-Treuhand in Mannheim, then was posted (1997-99) to Fuchs Lubricants Co. in Harvey, Illinois, responsible for Argentina, Brazil and Mexico. He also sits on the supervisory board of machine-tool maker TRUMPF.
notes: Input name misspelled ('Stefan Fuch'). Press contact Tina Vogel (FUCHS SE Public Relations) per July 2026 release. Born 1968; Mannheim University business graduate.

name: W Brett Welson
current_role: Chairman, Prairie Merchant Corporation (private merchant bank); co-founder (ret.) of FirstEnergy Capital
profile: W. Brett Wilson (input spelling 'Welson' is a typo) is a Saskatchewan-born investment banker who co-founded Calgary energy investment bank FirstEnergy Capital in 1993 (with Murray Edwards and others) and chaired it until 2008. He was a Dragons' Den panellist (seasons 3-5) and now invests via Prairie Merchant in energy, real estate, agriculture and sports (incl. a Nashville Predators stake).
interesting_fact: He bills himself as the all-time lead deal-making 'dragon' on CBC's Dragons' Den, and wrote the 2012 Penguin book 'Redefining Success: Still Making Mistakes'.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Wilson earned a civil engineering degree and spent three years working the oilfields of Western Canada for Imperial Oil, then did an MBA in entrepreneurship at the University of Calgary (1985) and started at McLeod Young Weir.
notes: Hurun $2B figure looks inflated (other estimates far lower). Very active and outspoken on social media; has had public controversies over posts (2018, 2020) - be aware. Prolific philanthropist (prostate cancer, domestic-abuse research, mental health) and regular podcast guest, so likely receptive.

name: Ronald Mc Aulay
current_role: Director, Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons Ltd (Kadoorie family office); former long-time director of CLP Holdings and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels
profile: Ronald McAulay (b. 1935/36), a Scottish-born Hong Kong businessman, married into the Kadoorie family. His wealth stems mainly from a roughly 10% stake, held through trusts, in CLP Holdings, Hong Kong's biggest power utility. He sat on CLP's board 1968-2016 and on Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels' board 1972-c.2017.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's main power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and served nearly half a century, leaving on 1 October 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the Kadoorie businesses he trained as an accountant: he is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland, holds a master's degree from the University of Glasgow, and was schooled at Gordonstoun.
notes: Very private and about 90 years old. I found no death report, and Wikipedia (edited 2026) lists him as living. No published personal contact; the only route is via the Kadoorie family office (Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons, Hong Kong) or CLP corporate communications. Input lists the country as China (Hong Kong); he is a British citizen.

name: Catherine Lozinck
profile: Catherine Lozick (correct spelling), daughter of Swagelok co-founder Fred A. Lennon, inherited a majority stake in the Solon, Ohio valve and fittings maker. Forbes reports she died in January 2025 at age 79. Swagelok is now led by Fred Lennon's grandson Thomas F. Lozick as chairman and CEO.
notes: Deceased January 2025 per Forbes profile (https://www.forbes.com/profile/catherine-lozick/). Input name is misspelled ('Lozinck'). Family remains very private; Swagelok is run by Thomas F. Lozick (https://swagelok.com/en/about/news/swagelok-announces-election-of-directors).

name: Maria del Carmen Sundblad Beccar Varela
current_role: Matriarch and shareholder of the Perez Companc Family Group (Argentina); founder of Munchi's ice cream and driving force behind Temaikèn.
profile: Born 1942, 'Munchi' Sundblad is the widow of Gregorio Pérez Companc (d. 2024), whose family controls Pecom (oil & gas services/production, expanding in Argentine upstream), Molinos Río de la Plata food and farmland. She built her own businesses: the Munchi's ice-cream chain, a Jersey dairy herd, and the Temaikèn bioparque in Escobar.
interesting_fact: She personally decided to build Temaikèn in Escobar, which opened in 2002 as Latin America's largest theme/bioparque, and she weighed in on the family's historic 2002 sale of Pecom Energía to Petrobras for about US$1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Her ice-cream brand Munchi's is named after her own childhood nickname; she also raises prize Jersey cattle at the family's San Isidro Labrador cabaña in Escobar, which she visited weekly, and La Nación wrote she only raises her voice when her bulls win at a rural show.
notes: Extremely private family ('extremists of anonymity'); no personal channels. Alive status presumed (on Hurun Global 2025-26 lists, no obituary found; would be 84). Contacts are company forms only (Munchi's, Pecom). Husband Gregorio died June 2024.

name: Giannis Vardinogiannis
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Motor Oil (Hellas) Corinth Refineries; Chairman & CEO, Avin Oil
profile: Eldest son of the late Vardis Vardinoyannis and head of the Vardinoyannis group, which controls Greek refiner Motor Oil Hellas. CEO since 2021 and chairman since Nov 2024, he has pushed the refiner into renewables (2.2 GW via the 2024 Anemos RES deal), waste/circular economy and banking (Optima Bank, listed 2023), with interests in shipping, upstream and hospitality.
interesting_fact: He ran Panathinaikos FC from 2000, taking the club to the Champions League quarter-finals in 2001-02, and was a founding member and later president of Greece's Super League.
deep_cut_fact: A Vassar economics graduate, he won the Greek Rally championship six straight times (1987-1992) in a Lancia Delta with co-driver Kostas Stefanis, and in 2024 founded the private team Cyclon Rally Sport.
notes: Also spelled Yannis/Ioannis Vardinoyannis. No published personal or press email verified (moh.gr blocked automated access); Motor Oil IR officer listed as Mary Psyllaki on market-data sites.

name: Robin Khuda
current_role: Founder and CEO, AirTrunk
profile: Dhaka-born accountant who moved to Sydney at 18, worked at Fujitsu, PIPE Networks and NEXTDC (as CFO), then founded hyperscale data-center operator AirTrunk in 2015. Blackstone and CPP Investments bought AirTrunk in 2024 in a A$24B (~US$16B) deal; he remains CEO and is expanding across APAC, the Middle East and India (a ~US$30B India plan announced in 2026).
interesting_fact: In AirTrunk's early days he dipped into his retirement savings to keep it afloat and came close to bankruptcy; in 2024 he was named AFR Business Person of the Year. In 2025 he gave A$100M to the University of Sydney for a 20-year women-in-STEM program.
deep_cut_fact: Right before founding AirTrunk he left NEXTDC to become CEO of Mint Wireless, a telecom payments company; he says he had been watching the cloud boom since 2010-11 and planning his own data-center business.
notes: Elected Fellow of ATSE in 2026. Runs the Khuda Family Foundation (women in tech, mental health). Also founded luxury developer Ondas. Excellent fit for the data-center podcast; route via AirTrunk media.

name: Amjad Masad
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Replit
profile: Jordan-raised son of refugees who moved to the US in 2012 as an early engineer at Codecademy, then worked on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure before cofounding Replit in 2016 with his wife Haya Odeh. Replit became a leader in AI 'vibe coding' agents and was valued at $9bn after a $400m round in March 2026.
interesting_fact: As a teenager in Jordan he made money building software management systems for local internet cafes; Replit's backers now include a16z, Coatue, Shaquille O'Neal, Jared Leto and Qatar's QIA.
deep_cut_fact: Before Replit he was tech lead on Facebook's JavaScript infrastructure team, which built or maintained the Babel compiler, Jest and the React Native packager; before that he was Codecademy's #1 employee, briefly at Yahoo, and worked in cybersecurity while in college.
notes: Very active and accessible on X (@amasad); has done many podcasts, so a direct X reply/DM plus press@replit.com is the best route. Strong AI/data-center angle (compute-hungry coding agents).

name: Zhu Gongshan
current_role: Founder, chairman and joint CEO of GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK); chairman of GCL Group (Golden Concord)
profile: Born 1958 in Funing, Yancheng, Jiangsu, Zhu founded GCL in Hong Kong in 1990, first building cogeneration power plants, then moving into solar-grade polysilicon from 2006. GCL Tech became one of the world's largest polysilicon makers and is now pushing low-energy FBR granular silicon. He also chairs the Asian Photovoltaic Industry Association and the Global Green Energy Industry Council.
interesting_fact: Zhu trained as a power engineer, graduating from Nanjing Electric Power College (now Nanjing Institute of Technology) in 1981. GCL's first business was thermal and cogeneration power plants, years before it became a solar-materials giant.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding GCL he worked ordinary jobs from 1978, including as a shop sales clerk. He later chaired the SNEC Hydrogen Energy Industry Alliance Council and was named one of the 'Ten Outstanding Contributors to New China's New Energy Industry' in its 70th year.
notes: ESG@gcl-power.com is the corporate contact printed in GCL Tech's 2025 annual/ESG report (Suzhou HQ, tel +86 512 6853 3900); no dedicated press email was found. He speaks often at SNEC and global solar forums, so a conference is a plausible route. The sales-clerk detail comes from an ifeng profile (https://finance.ifeng.com/people/comchief/zhugongshan.shtml); the award and hydrogen role from the HKEX annual report.

name: William Koch
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Oxbow Corporation / Oxbow Carbon (West Palm Beach, Florida)
profile: William 'Bill' Koch, one of the four sons of Koch Industries co-founder Fred Koch, founded Oxbow in 1983 after leaving the family business; it grew into a major trader and processor of petroleum coke, coal, sulphur and other carbon products. He remains chairman, and is also a big collector of art, wine and Old West memorabilia.
interesting_fact: He won the 1992 America's Cup with his America3 syndicate, then in 1995 entered 'Mighty Mary', a boat crewed mostly by women, in the next Cup.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2011 he paid about $2.3m at Brian Lebel's Old West auction in Denver for the 'Upham tintype', the only authenticated photo of Billy the Kid; it joined his Wild West collection that includes Custer's rifle and Remington bronzes.
notes: Born 1940; listed on Forbes real-time 2026, no death reports found. Oxbow is private; a 2015 Oxbow press release listed a Corporate Communications Office in West Palm Beach (phone 561-907-5422, Director Corporate Affairs Brad Goldstein) - may be outdated. oxbow.com did not respond to direct fetch. Avoid the Koch-brothers feud and Oxbow litigation topics.

name: Mariarosa Lavelli
current_role: Major shareholder (~11%) of Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan); co-founder of the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa
profile: Widow of Giuseppe Crippa (d. July 2025), an ex-STMicroelectronics engineer who founded Technoprobe, now a global leader in probe cards for chip testing used by Nvidia, Apple, TSMC and others. She handled the administration from the start and was still reported in 2022 to follow the family company's accounts. Owns ~11% since the 2022 IPO.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco). In 1993 the nucleus was Giuseppe, son Cristiano, Mariarosa on administration and two employees. It moved to its first building in 1996 with about 10 staff.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2023 she and Giuseppe set up the Fondazione Mariarosa e Giuseppe Crippa to give structure to the family's and Technoprobe's philanthropy. Il Giorno noted she 'still follows the accounts' of the family firm even after it made Giuseppe a billionaire at 87.
notes: Recently widowed (July 2025), so be sensitive. Never gives interviews; route via Technoprobe press office. The family (son Cristiano Crippa, CEO Stefano Felici) is the public face. The foundation's start date is given as May 2023 in Technoprobe materials.

name: Li Jianli (励建立)
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Kedali Industry Co. (科达利, SZSE 002850)
profile: Ningbo-born mould designer who co-founded Kedali in Shenzhen in 1996 with his brother using ~RMB 20,000 of savings. Kedali moved from stamping dies to phone-battery parts and, from 2007, to precision structural parts for EV batteries; it listed in Shenzhen in 2017 and supplies CATL, BYD, CALB, EVE, Panasonic and LG, with ~32% global share in 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2007, as iPhone-era pouch cells threatened his phone-battery parts business, he put more than half its profits into EV battery structural parts; R&D succeeded by 2010 and the segment grew from RMB 66m revenue (2013) to RMB 930m (2016).
deep_cut_fact: He studied mould design at a technical secondary school, graduated in 1991 and went to Shenzhen as a die designer at a Hong Kong-owned firm. Kedali's break came in 1999 when BYD asked it to co-develop phone-battery parts: after 20+ attempts in a year it matched Japanese imports at about a third of the price.
notes: Low media profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable. No published email found on company site; best route is Kedali's investor-interaction page (cninfo IRM, linked from its website) or the company contact page https://www.kedali.com.cn/contact.html. Brother Li Jianju (励建炬) is president.

name: Airat Shaimiev
current_role: Head (CEO) of JSC Tatavtodor, Tatarstan's state road-construction company; co-owner of TAIF shareholders' stake in Sibur
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president, Mintimer Shaimiev. He built his fortune as a co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan holding with refining and petrochemical assets that merged into Sibur in 2021; TAIF shareholders received 15% of Sibur. He still runs Tatavtodor, the regional road builder, which reported 2025 contracts worth billions of rubles.
interesting_fact: With his brother Radik and his son Timur he also owns MNKT, a small oil producer in Tatarstan (per Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: He practiced karate in Soviet times, when the sport was banned in the USSR. After it was legalised he won the Kazan championship, then took up motor racing; he and his brother raced in the first events at the Vysokaya Gora autodrome in 1996.
notes: He is under UK sanctions (OpenSanctions entry gb-hmt-15608), so outreach may raise compliance and reputational issues. The only published contact is Tatavtodor's general company email. He gives few interviews.

name: Wang Nan
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Puya Semiconductor (普冉股份, Shanghai STAR Market 688766)
profile: Born 1976; SJTU applied-physics graduate who spent 14 years (1998-2012) at Shanghai Hua Hong NEC rising from IC design engineer to senior director, then founded Wuxi Puya (2012) and Puya Semiconductor (2016) with ex-colleague Li Zhaogui. Puya makes NOR Flash, EEPROM and MCUs, listed in 2021, bought SLC-NAND maker SkyHigh Memory, and in H1 2026 profit jumped ~19x on AI-driven memory demand; it is now planning a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: He bet on an unfashionable process: Puya was the first to build general-purpose NOR Flash on the SONOS charge-trap process (instead of incumbents' ETOX), whose low power and tiny die size rode the TWS-earbud boom into Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO and vivo products.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a double bachelor's in physics and applied electronics from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and, while still at Hua Hong NEC, earned an EMBA (2011) from Washington University in St. Louis' Olin Business School.
notes: Low-profile; few personal interviews. Route via board secretary / IR (ir@puyasemi.com). Hurun lists name as Wang Nan (王楠). Company announced H-share HK listing plans in Nov 2026.

name: Yao Lijun
current_role: Founder, Chairman (and CTO), Konfoong Materials International Co. (SZSE: 300666), Yuyao/Ningbo, Zhejiang
profile: Materials scientist with doctorates from Harbin Institute of Technology and Hiroshima University who returned from abroad and in 2005 co-founded Konfoong Materials with six partners in Yuyao, Zhejiang. Konfoong makes ultra-high-purity metal sputtering targets used by 100+ chip fabs worldwide, a key domestic supplier in China's semiconductor supply chain; he aims for a 30% global share.
interesting_fact: Konfoong's sputtering targets are used by more than 100 chip factories worldwide, and Yao has said his goal is a 30% global market share in target materials.
deep_cut_fact: He launched Konfoong in April 2005 alongside returned Chinese scientists plus Japanese and American experts, shipping in 20 containers of imported equipment to Yuyao; he credits reform and opening-up with 'four opportunities' including his Japanese doctoral scholarship.
notes: Thousand Talents Program recipient; won Zhejiang provincial science & technology award (2018). No published IR email found; Konfoong's board secretary (Zou Junwei, appointed 2025) and securities dept. handle investor queries via SZSE Interactive (irm.cninfo.com.cn). Company site was not reachable from here; URL taken from public listings.

name: Farris Wilks
current_role: Co-owner, Wilks Brothers LLC (family investment office, Cisco, Texas); 10%+ shareholder in ProFrac Holding Corp. (ACDC)
profile: Texas stonemason-turned-fracking billionaire: with brother Dan he founded Wilks Masonry (1995) and Frac Tech (2002), selling to a Temasek-led group in 2011 for $3.5bn pretax. Via Wilks Brothers they invest in oilfield services (ProFrac, U.S. Well Services, Dawson Geophysical) and own ~672,000 acres in six states.
interesting_fact: Farris is pastor of his own church, the Assembly of Yahweh Seventh Day Church near Cisco, Texas - the congregation his father Voy led from 1952.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, the brothers were bricklayers like their father and ran Wilks Masonry; they launched Frac Tech in 2002 out of tiny Cisco, Texas (Eastland County), where both still live, and grew it into one of the largest US fracking firms in under a decade.
notes: Very private; Wilks Brothers site publishes no contact. ProFrac (chaired by Dan's son Matt Wilks) is an indirect route only - Farris is a shareholder, not an executive. Politically prominent (major conservative donor), so expect media caution.

name: Tseng Shin-yi
profile: Most likely Cheng Hsin-yi (鄭信義, b. 1928), one of three cofounders in 1949 of Taiwan's Chang Chun Group, the island's No. 2 petrochemical group after Formosa Plastics. Chinese Wikipedia records his death on 28 January 2016.
notes: Caproasia's 2017 Forbes-based list has 'Tseng Shin-yi', 90, Chang Chun Group; this matches cofounder 鄭信義, who died 28 Jan 2016 per https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%84%AD%E4%BF%A1%E7%BE%A9 and https://www.cmoney.tw/notes/note-detail.aspx?nid=49860. Romanization match not 100% confirmed; treat as deceased.

name: Vladimir Gridin
current_role: Retired co-founder of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo; exited the business from 2016 to 2019
profile: Vladimir Gridin co-founded Siberian Business Union (SDS) with Mikhail Fedyaev in the mid-1990s and built it into a large Kuzbass coal, chemicals and engineering holding (registered 2004). He was a State Duma deputy for Kemerovo region from 2011. He later stepped back, reportedly moved to Monaco, and from about 2016 to 2019 sold his stakes to Fedyaev and Roman Trotsenko.
interesting_fact: SDS grew into Russia's third-largest producer of thermal (power-station) coal, with interests in mining, rail transport, chemicals, machine building and radio stations.
deep_cut_fact: The partners' first major asset in the mid-1990s was the Chernigovets open-pit coal mine in Kuzbass. When SDS was formally registered in Kemerovo in 2004, it already brought together more than 20 businesses in coal, machinery, building materials and utilities.
notes: Out of public life since around 2015; last on the Forbes list in 2013. He has largely exited SDS and reportedly lives in Monaco (dataset says UK). No current public contact found; alive status is unconfirmed, with no death reports found. Russian coal ties carry sanctions sensitivity, so check before outreach.

name: Sanjeev Soosaipillai
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of Prax Group (UK oil refining/fuel group); key UK units in administration since June 2025
profile: Sanjeev Kumar (Winston) Soosaipillai cofounded Prax with his wife Arani in 1999, growing from petrol retailing into wholesale fuel (2002), then buying the Lindsey Oil Refinery on the Humber and a stake in South Africa's Natref refinery. Parent State Oil and the Lindsey refinery entered administration/liquidation in June 2025; retail, upstream and international arms continue to trade.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a two-person operation in 1999 into the owner of one of the UK's six major refineries (Lindsey), a rare case of a privately held, founder-owned UK refiner.
notes: Sensitive: Prax's UK refining collapse (June 2025) is subject to an Insolvency Service investigation, and a High Court asset freeze was reported. The only published press contact is the administrators' (Teneo) media desk, which does not represent him personally. Most bio coverage is sponsored/promotional content, so personal details (e.g. University of Kent, early filling-station job) are unverified. Probably not a suitable podcast guest at present.

name: Arani Soosaipillai
current_role: Co-owner (with husband Sanjeev Kumar/Winston Soosaipillai) of Prax Group, UK oil refining and trading group now in insolvency
profile: Arani Soosaipillai and her husband built London-based Prax Group (founded 1999), an oil trading, distribution and refining group that bought the Lindsey oil refinery. Reports name her as joint ultimate controlling party alongside her husband, who was sole director. Prax's main companies entered administration/liquidation in mid-2025 and Lindsey refinery ceased operations.
interesting_fact: Prax grew from a 1999 London fuel-trading start-up into an integrated group owning the Lindsey refinery in Lincolnshire, one of only a handful of UK refineries.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Prax collapsed in June 2025 (administration/liquidation, refinery closure, UK government demands for investigation, High Court asset freeze on her husband). Hurun $1.9bn figure is pre-collapse and stale. No public role or contact for her found.

name: Wang Junshi
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, Ginlong Technologies (Solis inverters); stepped down as director/deputy GM in 2021
profile: Wang Junshi (age ~77, Ningbo) co-founded Ginlong Technologies in 2005 with his wife Lin Yibei and son Wang Yiming; the company, sold under the Solis brand, became one of the world's largest string solar-inverter makers and listed in Shenzhen (300763) in 2019. He left the board in 2021; his son now chairs the firm, which has expanded into energy storage.
interesting_fact: Ginlong/Solis says it was only the second inverter company worldwide to obtain the UK's G83 grid-connection certification, in 2006, a year after its founding, an early bet on export markets.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding a multibillion-dollar solar-inverter business, Wang Junshi worked as a high school teacher.
notes: Very low public profile; elderly and retired from management. Best route is via Ginlong/Solis corporate (son Wang Yiming is chairman and the public face). No published press/IR email found on Solis site (only sales/service addresses).

name: Tan Dong
current_role: Director (non-independent), Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co. (科翔股份, SZSE: 300903); GM of subsidiary Huayu Huayuan
profile: Tan Dong (b. 1969, postgraduate degree) co-founded Huizhou-based PCB maker Kingshine (Dayawan Kexiang) in 2001 with Zheng Xiaorong, now chairwoman; the pair are its controlling shareholders and share the Hurun fortune. Kingshine listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in Nov 2020 and makes HDI, multilayer, flex and ceramic-substrate boards for autos, servers, optical modules and mmWave radar.
interesting_fact: Before Kingshine, Tan Dong was general manager (1996-2001) of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, where Zheng Xiaorong was executive director; they then moved together to found Dayawan Kexiang in July 2001, the origin of today's listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as an engineer in the technical department of Guangdong Macro (Wanjiale) Communication Equipment Co., before moving into PCB manufacturing.
notes: Hurun English name 'Kingshine' = 科翔股份 (not Kinwong/景旺). Low public profile; no interviews found. Company securities dept (board secretary Zheng Haitao) is the formal route; IR email published in company filings (shown via Eastmoney F10).

name: Zheng Xiaorong
current_role: Chairwoman, Guangdong Kingshine Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (科翔股份, SZ:300903), a Huizhou PCB maker
profile: Zheng Xiaorong (b. 1972) and her husband Tan Dong are the controlling shareholders of Kingshine Electronic (科翔股份). The company makes high-density PCBs, including HDI boards for AI servers and 800G optical modules, at plants in Huizhou and Jiangxi. She has run the business since 2001 and was general manager until October 2025. She holds about 15% directly.
interesting_fact: In 2009 she bought a near-bankrupt factory, turned it profitable within three months, and passed RMB 100M in output the next year. Around 2012 she set up an HDI division while most peers held back, and that bet now underpins Kingshine's AI-server boards.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career in 1992 as marketing department manager at Shenzhen Kerong Electronics' subsidiary factory. In 1997 she became executive director of Shenzhen Shunjiaxing Electronics, before founding Daya Bay Kexiang (Kingshine's predecessor) in 2001.
notes: The Hurun 'Kingshine' entry is Guangdong Kingshine Electronic (科翔股份), not Jingsheng/晶盛. The board secretary is Zheng Haitao, and the IR route is the securities affairs inbox. Her motto from a 2026 Shanghai Securities News interview: 'bend down to dig into technology, look up to see the direction clearly' (俯身深耕技术、抬头看清方向).

name: Zhang Yanxia
current_role: Co-founder and Deputy General Manager (joined 2013 as deputy GM and board secretary), Gpixel / Changchun Changguang Chenxin Microelectronics (長光辰芯), HKEX-listed
profile: Zhejiang University applied-electronics graduate with a PhD from TU Delft; co-founded Gpixel with her husband Wang Xinyang, an incubatee of the CAS Changchun Institute of Optics. Gpixel makes industrial and scientific CMOS image sensors (ranked ~3rd globally in both niches). The couple held ~49.5% pre-IPO; the company listed in Hong Kong in April 2026, jumping ~75% on day one.
interesting_fact: Gpixel avoided the smartphone-sensor market dominated by Sony and Samsung and targeted industrial/scientific imaging (<3% of the CIS market); in 2015 it launched what it calls the world's first back-illuminated scientific CMOS image sensor.
deep_cut_fact: She and her husband were classmates in Zhejiang University's applied electronics program; she did her master's at Concordia University in Canada (he went to Southampton) before both earned PhDs at TU Delft. She gave up a job abroad to join Gpixel in its second year.
notes: Fortune shared with husband Wang Xinyang (chairman/GM). Her exact current board title post-IPO not verified; check the HKEX prospectus. Media contact form is the best press route.

name: Zhou Xunwei
current_role: Founder & Chairman, JoulWatt Technology (杰华特, SSE STAR: 688141), Hangzhou
profile: Zhou Xunwei (周逊伟) is a Zhejiang University and Virginia Tech-trained power-electronics engineer who spent years at US analog-chip firms before co-founding JoulWatt in Hangzhou in March 2013. JoulWatt designs analog/power-management ICs, including power chips for servers and data centers, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Dec 2022; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: JoulWatt was founded on 18 March 2013 by Zhou and co-founder Huang Biliang and IPO'd on the STAR Market in December 2022, part of China's push for domestic analog/power-management chips.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding JoulWatt he was a senior design engineer at Linear Technology in the US (2001-2007) and then VP of engineering at Helix Micro; he earned his PhD at Virginia Tech after bachelor's and master's degrees at Zhejiang University.
notes: Deep-cut career details come from a single Chinese profile site (maigoo); verify against the STAR Market prospectus director bios before use. IR contact is board secretary Ma Wenwen's office. Reported US nationality.

name: Dou Baibing

notes: Unverified lead: 'Jinjiang' plus energy/chemicals and the rare surname Dou (钭) suggests Hangzhou Jinjiang Group (杭州锦江集团: aluminium/alumina, waste-to-energy, chemicals), founded by Dou Zhenggang (钭正刚), but no source links her to it. Confirm on Qichacha/Tianyancha or the Hurun list before using.

name: Fan Caiping

notes: Could not confirm identity (English and Chinese 范彩平 searches returned nothing). Possibly a family member/shareholder linked to the Jin family; check JA Solar annual report shareholder list before outreach. Company IR route: JA Solar investor relations at jasolar.com.

name: Jin Junmiao
current_role: Shareholder (25%) of Jingtaifu, the controlling shareholder of JA Solar Technology; former JA Solar assistant president and procurement head. Current title unconfirmed.
profile: Younger daughter of JA Solar founder Jin Baofang. Her wealth comes from a 25% stake in Jingtaifu, the holding company that owns about 48% of JA Solar, one of the world's largest PV module makers. She was assistant president and ran procurement, and has a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: In June 2021 her father transferred 25% of Jingtaifu, the vehicle controlling about 47.77% of JA Solar, to her. That makes her the only one of his daughters with a direct stake in the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2019 she was 'godmother' at the naming ceremony for a new COSCO Shipping vessel, the 'COSCO Shipping Aquarius'. She named the ship, cut the rope and broke the champagne bottle in the traditional launch rite.
notes: Hurun calls her 'self-made', but her stake came from her founder father. She is very private and I found no personal channels; go through JA Solar IR. Her husband Tao Ran is a JA Solar director.

name: Alexander Isaev
current_role: CEO of Elga coal managing company (Elgaugol / UK Elga) and minority co-owner (~20%) of the Elga coal project via Energogroup
profile: Russian coal executive, formerly co-owner and CEO of VostokCoal, who in 2020 became CEO of Elgaugol, the operator of the Elga coking-coal deposit in Yakutia (Russia's largest, ~2.2bn t reserves) bought by Albert Avdolyan's A-Property. He holds roughly a 20% stake alongside Avdolyan; the pair also bought and later sold Sibanthracite. Forbes added him to its billionaire list as a newcomer in 2025.
interesting_fact: Elga sits in remote, frozen southern Yakutia; its owners set out to lift output from ~4m tonnes in 2019 to tens of millions of tonnes, mostly exported to China, building a private railway to reach the Pacific coast.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2022 Isaev's Energogroup and Avdolyan's AP Holding registered a new company, A-Steel, to produce pig iron, steel and ferroalloys (Avdolyan 75%, Isaev 25%) - a first sign of interest in moving downstream from coal.
notes: Very low public profile; no official site, press contact or social accounts found for him or Elgaugol. Russian coal sector — check Western sanctions status of Elga/A-Property entities before any outreach. Common name: confirm identity via Elga link.

name: Brad Keywell
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Gigawatt AI (AI-native operating system for utilities, founded Aug 2025); Director, TKO Group Holdings
profile: Detroit-born serial founder who co-founded Groupon, Echo Global Logistics and Mediaocean with Eric Lefkofsky, plus VC firm Lightbank. His fortune rests largely on being a founding investor in Tempus AI. He founded industrial-AI firm Uptake (2014; sold to Bosch in 2026) and now runs Gigawatt AI, building AI software for energy and water utilities.
interesting_fact: Named overall 2019 EY World Entrepreneur of the Year (chosen from 44 country winners); he also founded Chicago Ideas and the immersive WNDR Museum, and signed the Giving Pledge in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first business at age 7, a greeting-card company called Key Creations. As a University of Michigan freshman he met Sam Zell and spent summers interning at Zell's Equity Group Investments; Zell mentored him for 35 years. He is also an adjunct professor of entrepreneurship at Chicago Booth.
notes: Strong podcast fit: Gigawatt AI targets utilities (energy/grid). Personal site has a press kit (bradkeywell.com/files/Brad-Keywell-Bio-2026.pdf). Gigawatt's published media route is marketing@gigawatt.ai. Avoid divorce topic.

name: Deng Weiming
current_role: Chairman and President, CNGR Advanced Material Co. (中伟股份; Shenzhen 300919 / HKEX-listed)
profile: Born 1968 in Shaoyang, Hunan, Deng founded the Zhongwei group in 1995 around coal chemicals and trading, pivoted to new energy by buying a lithium-battery precursor maker in 2013, and spun out CNGR in 2014 in Tongren, Guizhou. CNGR makes nickel/cobalt precursor materials for cathodes supplied to Tesla, LG Chem and CATL; it listed in Shenzhen in 2020 and Hong Kong in 2025.
interesting_fact: After its 2020 Shenzhen ChiNext listing, CNGR at one point became the second-most valuable listed company in Guizhou province, behind only Kweichow Moutai.
deep_cut_fact: Deng studied organic chemistry at Taiyuan University of Science and Technology and began his career as a technician at a state-owned coking plant in Shaodong, Hunan, before quitting to try property trading in Hainan during the early-1990s boom.
notes: Chinese-language outreach recommended. He and his wife Wu Xiaoge jointly control ~56% of CNGR. Early-career details come from a Chinese media summary (Touzijie, reposted on Bilibili) of the HK IPO prospectus.

name: Said Gutseriev
current_role: Russian-British investor; founder of Larnabel Ventures; shareholder in SFI holding (Europlan leasing, VSK insurance) - reportedly exited M.Video board in 2025
profile: Said Gutseriev (b. 1988, Moscow) is the son of oligarch Mikhail Gutseriev and was educated in the UK from age 8. After an analyst stint at Glencore he took board roles in family oil, refining and coal businesses from 2014, then built holdings in retailer M.Video and investment group SFI. Reports say he left M.Video's board in 2025 after signalling plans to sell.
interesting_fact: He holds an Oxford master's degree in geology and an MA in oil & gas management from the University of Plymouth.
deep_cut_fact: He started out (2012-2014) as an analyst in Glencore's London structured-financing department for oil projects, later moving to the trader's finance office.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (28 June 2022) and EU over his SFI directorship - check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach or featuring. No published personal contact or official social accounts found. M.Video ownership in flux in 2025 (interfax.ru/business/860507).

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Private investor; former chairman/CEO of Saras (Italian oil refiner) and former owner/president of Inter Milan
profile: Son of Angelo Moratti, who founded Sardinian refiner Saras in 1962, Massimo ran the company with brother Gian Marco and took it public in 2006. In 2024 the Moratti family sold about 35% of Saras to trader Vitol at EUR 1.75/share, triggering a takeover and delisting. He is best known for owning Inter Milan for ~two decades, selling his last shares in 2016.
interesting_fact: His Inter Milan tenure included five straight Serie A titles and the 2010 treble (Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League), plus that year's Club World Cup.
deep_cut_fact: As Inter president he conceived Inter Campus, the club's social project that since 1997 has used youth football to help children in need, starting in Recife, Brazil; it now reaches thousands of kids worldwide.
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: family sold its Saras control to Vitol (closed June 2024; Vitol press release https://www.vitol.com/members-of-the-moratti-family-enter-into-an-agreement-to-sell-approx-35-of-saras-to-vitol/). No personal channels; reachable mainly via Italian press/football world. Brother Gian Marco died 2018.

name: Huo Qinghua
current_role: Founder and chairman, China Kingho Energy Group (中国庆华能源集团) / Inner Mongolia Qinghua Group (last reported)
profile: Huo Qinghua (霍庆华) built China Kingho (Qinghua) Group, once called China's largest private coal miner, from a 1996 start in Alashan, Inner Mongolia, expanding into coal chemicals, logistics and overseas projects (assets RMB 68.6B in 2014). He was on Forbes' billionaire list 2013-2018, but the group struggled after the coal downturn.
interesting_fact: In 2011 Kingho announced plans to build a coal terminal at Mozambique's Beira port and upgrade the Sena railway to the Moatize coal mines, and had proposed a $19B coal development in Pakistan's Thar field.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a coal magnate he served in the army and then worked as a physician at the hospital of Ningxia's Shitanjing Mining Bureau, studying economic management at the Ningxia Coal Workers' University.
notes: No recent (post-2018) news on him found; no death reports found. Per NBD (2018) the group fell into financial distress after 2013 with creditor lawsuits and court enforcement lists, so approach with care; likely not a current billionaire. No published personal/press contacts.

name: Evangelos Mytilineos
current_role: Chairman and CEO, METLEN Energy & Metals (Athens/London-listed)
profile: Greek industrialist (b. 1954, Athens) who in 1990 founded the modern Mytilineos group from his grandfather's 1908 metallurgy business, listed it in Athens in 1995, renamed it METLEN in 2024 and added a London listing in 2025. METLEN runs aluminium plants and bauxite mines, builds solar and storage projects worldwide and is Greece's largest independent electricity supplier.
interesting_fact: METLEN's roots go back to a metallurgy business founded in 1908 by his grandfather, also named Evangelos; he turned it into one of Greece's largest industrial and energy groups and moved its primary listing to London in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A Moraitis School alumnus, he holds an economics BSc from the University of Athens and an MSc from the London School of Economics; the University of Piraeus gave him an honorary doctorate in 2019, and his family hails from Koroni in the Peloponnese.
notes: No personal social media found. Route via METLEN media/contact-us page (info@metlen.com). Strong energy fit: solar/storage EPC, power supply and energy-intensive aluminium. Deep-cut fact is light (from Wikipedia); my web-search quota ran out before I could look further.

name: Farkhad Akhmedov
current_role: Private investor; chairman/shareholder of AZNAR (Azerbaijani natural-juice and agriculture company); former Russian senator
profile: Baku-born (1955) Azerbaijani-Russian businessman who started trading furs in London, founded Tansley Trading to supply equipment to Soviet gas producers, and built a stake in Siberian gas producer Northgas, selling his 49% to Novatek in 2012 for ~$1.4B. Sat in Russia's Federation Council 2004-2009. Now invests privately, incl. AZNAR juice and agriculture in Azerbaijan.
interesting_fact: He invested $55 million in a pomegranate juice factory in his native Azerbaijan, in the region where his father worked during the Soviet era.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and gas, he served in the Soviet Navy (1975-77) as a senior sergeant and platoon commander, then earned a degree in the technology and merchandising of fur products from the Moscow Veterinary Academy (1983), the expertise behind his first business selling furs in London.
notes: Sensitive: under UK sanctions since April 2022 (EU lifted its sanctions in Sept 2023) and subject of a long, heavily covered divorce case; avoid both. He has also been the first ethnic Azerbaijani in Russia's upper house. No published personal/office contact found; web-search budget ran out before checking AZNAR's site.

name: Lu Feng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Wind Information Co., Ltd. (万得信息, Shanghai)
profile: Lu Feng (陆风) founded Wind Information in Shanghai in the 1990s (sources give 1994 or 1998) and built it into mainland China's dominant financial-data terminal, often described as China's answer to Bloomberg, used by brokers, fund houses, banks and QFIIs. He remains chairman and is a part-time vice chair of the Shanghai Federation of Industry and Commerce's 14th executive committee.
interesting_fact: Wind's terminal is the default data source cited across Chinese financial media, research reports and academic papers; investors in the company have included Hillhouse Capital (2015) and Xinhu Zhongbao (2018).
deep_cut_fact: In a rare 2021 keynote at Huatai Securities' fintech open day he recalled that in 2006 Wind adopted the slogan '金融就是数据' ('finance is data'), described a 'digital twin enterprise' goal, and promoted Wind's 'Shared by Wind' program to share its data and networks with startups.
notes: Very low-profile founder; rarely gives interviews. Name collides with a Peking University economist Lu Feng (born 1951) - different person. Wealth is financial data, not energy, despite the 'energy' focus tag. Route via Wind corporate office in Shanghai.

name: Zhu Mengqian
current_role: Co-holder (with her father, chairman Zhu Shuangquan) of a family stake in Hubei Dinglong Holding (300054.SZ); no listed board or executive role found
profile: Hurun's 2026 China Rich List adds Zhu Mengqian (b. 1991, Wuhan; master's degree) jointly with her father Zhu Shuangquan, chairman of Wuhan-based Dinglong, a maker of semiconductor CMP polishing pads/slurries, display materials and printing consumables. The Zhu brothers (Shuangquan and Shunquan) control Dinglong with ~14.5% each; she is not among its directors, executives or top-10 holders.

name: Harvey Jones
current_role: Managing Partner, Square Wave Ventures; NVIDIA director since 1993 (Nvidia's board page lists him as Chair of the Board, plus audit and nominating/governance committees)
profile: EDA pioneer: co-founded Daisy Systems in 1981 (president/CEO to 1987), then led Synopsys 1987-1998 as CEO and executive chairman, and co-founded processor-IP firm Tensilica in 1997 (chairman until Cadence bought it in 2013). An Nvidia director since its 1993 founding, he became a billionaire from his Nvidia stake and invests via Square Wave Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Nvidia's board since the company was founded in 1993, and is a billionaire almost entirely from director compensation and stock, owning about 0.03% of Nvidia.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he discovered a teletype link to a timesharing system, taught himself BASIC, and 'sold my chemistry homework to my classmates' - his first entrepreneurial exercise. He then nearly took an IBM job on Allegheny Airlines' reservations system before joining CAD firm Calma.
notes: Georgetown math/CS and MIT Sloan MS. Gave a 2009 Computer History Museum oral history (good prep material). No personal social accounts or published Square Wave contact found; Nvidia corporate PR is the formal route. Chair title taken from nvidia.com board page (not independently re-verified).

name: Femi Otedola
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder (~27.7% as of Aug 2026), First HoldCo Plc (parent of First Bank of Nigeria)
profile: Lagos businessman who built Zenon Petroleum into a dominant diesel supplier, later controlled Forte Oil and then Geregu Power, whose majority stake he sold in 2025 for about $750M. He has since redeployed capital into First HoldCo, steadily raising his stake toward a stated goal of over 51%, and published the memoir 'Making It Big' in 2025.
interesting_fact: At one point he was Nigeria's largest private ship owner; one of his vessels, a flat-bottomed 16,000-tonne bunker ship, was reported as the first of its kind in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: In his memoir he recalls that while he was in A-levels his father set up Impact Press, a printing company in Surulere, Lagos; he became fascinated with the machines, skipped Upper Sixth to join the business, and became its MD at about 25 before founding Centre Force in 1994.
notes: Best route: the official memoir site's contact form, which has 'Media Inquiry' and 'Speaking Engagement' options. Active on social media; news reports cite X @realFemiOtedola, but I did not verify it from an official page, and reports give conflicting Instagram handles. First HoldCo site was unreachable from here. His memoir 'Making It Big' (Aug 2025) is a natural outreach hook.

name: Filippo Ghirelli
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Infracorp (infrastructure, energy, AI and space investment group); founder of family office Sophrance Global
profile: Monaco-based Italian engineer-entrepreneur (mid-40s). Built real estate businesses in Italy/North Africa, founded energy-efficiency firm Genera Group in 2009 (sold to SUSI Partners in 2024), and in 2023 bought a 25% stake in India's Nayara Energy refinery from Trafigura for $169M - the deal behind most of his ~$1.5B fortune. Infracorp (2024) targets airports, energy, data centres, AI and orbital modules.
interesting_fact: He bought Trafigura's 25% stake in Nayara Energy (India's second-largest refinery) for $169M, a 42% discount to Trafigura's 2017 price; Forbes estimates it is now worth at least $1.1B. Infracorp's plans include data centres in outer space.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating from college in Rome he left for Africa, starting his career as an engineer on infrastructure projects in Guinea and Mali.
notes: Strong fit for energy + data-center podcast (Infracorp plans ~600M in airports, data centres and space; AI lab 'Manthica'). Speaks publicly (Forbes interviews, SuperReturn Private Wealth speaker, appears on a Buzzsprout podcast). Nayara is EU-sanctioned due to Rosneft co-ownership - sensitive. Confirm sophrance.com is his Sophrance Global before using.

name: Wang Kunxiao
current_role: Director (formerly vice chairman and chairman), Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group (002353.SZ)
profile: Wang Kunxiao (王坤晓, b. 1969) is a co-founder of Jereh Group, founded in Yantai in 1999 with Sun Weijie and others; Jereh grew from oilfield equipment trading into fracturing fleets, gas compression, oil and gas engineering, new energy and power. He was vice chairman then chairman of the listed Jereh Oilfield Services and remains a board director.
interesting_fact: Jereh now runs a dedicated 'Data Center & Power' segment and markets PowerVEGA, a power-generation product built for AI data centers ('No waiting, power for AI now'), launched at RE+ 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a teacher at the Yantai Gold Technical School - the same school where co-founder Sun Weijie worked - before becoming deputy GM of Yantai Gold Economic Development Co.; he later earned an EMBA from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
notes: No longer chairman (current chairman Li Zhiyong; president Sun Weijie), so he is a lower-profile founder-director. Jereh's gas-turbine/data-center power push is a strong podcast hook; route via Jereh securities office (board secretary Qu Ning).

name: Somphote Ahunai
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Energy Absolute PCL (Thailand); resigned as director/executive effective July 2024
profile: Thai entrepreneur and former stockbroker/financier who founded Energy Absolute in 2006, turning a biodiesel plant into a SET-listed renewable group spanning solar and wind farms, a battery gigafactory (Amita) and electric buses/boats (Mine Mobility), earning it the nickname 'Tesla of Thailand'. He held roughly 30-40% of EA; he stepped down in 2024 and dropped off Forbes' list after 2024.
interesting_fact: Energy Absolute was dubbed the 'Tesla of Southeast Asia' as it expanded from renewables into EVs and a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to retire at 36 as a millionaire stockbroker, but was drawn into an unprofitable biodiesel factory his family had invested in; with an electrical-engineering background, he taught himself mechanical and chemical engineering from books and rebuilt the plant from scratch - the seed of EA. In 2020 he still wore a Uniqlo suit and rode the MRT.
notes: Sensitive: he and a deputy resigned from EA in July 2024 after Thailand's SEC filed a criminal complaint alleging fraud (see https://www.caproasia.com/?p=44424); approach with care and do not route via EA. MBA from Univ. of Pittsburgh (Katz), undergrad Chulalongkorn. No personal published contact found.

name: Neha Narkhede
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Oscilar (AI risk decisioning / fraud prevention); co-founder and former CTO of Confluent
profile: Pune-born engineer who, at LinkedIn, co-created Apache Kafka, the open-source streaming system now underpinning real-time data pipelines worldwide. In 2014 she co-founded Confluent to commercialize Kafka; it IPO'd in 2021 at ~$9.1B. Since 2021 she has run Oscilar, an AI-native risk and fraud-decisioning platform for fintechs and banks, and angel-invests in startups.
interesting_fact: She co-wrote the O'Reilly book 'Kafka: The Definitive Guide' (2017) with Gwen Shapira and Todd Palino, and Oscilar won a 2025 Banking Tech Award while she made Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders 500.
deep_cut_fact: Her fascination with computing began when her parents bought her a computer at age eight; after a BE from the University of Pune and an MS at Georgia Tech, her first job was at Oracle before she joined LinkedIn's Kafka team.
notes: Active public speaker (Money20/20, Fintech Meetup, Slush) and on X/LinkedIn - good podcast prospect for a data-infrastructure angle. Another Oscilar release routed media to an outside rep (Tim Granholm, Shallot). Input net worth is from 2022 Hurun; she dropped off Forbes' real-time list.

name: Sait-Salam Gutseriev
current_role: Russian businessman; co-owner of Gutseriev-family oil assets (took control of Neftisa and his brother Mikhail's RussNeft stake after 2021 EU sanctions on Mikhail); long-time head of PFC BIN
profile: Younger brother of Safmar founder Mikhail Gutseriev, born 1959 in Akmolinsk (now Astana). An oil engineer from Grozny, he ran the BIN industrial-financial company from 1993, sat on BIN bank and RussNeft boards, and served two terms in the State Duma (1999-2007). He became a key holder of the family's oil assets after Mikhail was sanctioned.
interesting_fact: He was a two-term State Duma deputy (1999-2007) and holds both a doctorate in economics (2003) and a candidate degree in law (2000).
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom of the oil-products business: in 1978 he was an operator at the Grozny oil distribution depot, becoming its workshop chief in 1983, after graduating from the Grozny Oil Institute in chemical-production machinery.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK in June 2022 - check sanctions rules before any outreach. Only on Forbes lists 2016-2017; no English Wikipedia page, very low public profile, no published personal or office contacts found. Web search budget ran out during this profile, so current holdings were not re-verified beyond Wikipedia.

name: Pantas Sutardja
current_role: Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO); founder & CEO of LatticeWork.
profile: Indonesian-born engineer (UC Berkeley EE/CS PhD, ex-IBM Almaden) who cofounded Marvell in 1995 with his late brother Sehat and Weili Dai, serving as VP engineering and CTO until 2014. He backed Credo's 2015 Series A and sits on its board (~3% stake); Credo's high-speed connectivity chips/AECs are now a key AI data-center supplier. He also runs consumer-storage firm LatticeWork.

Designed for 180 Mb/s, it was already running near 240 Mb/s when Seagate asked for 240 - Seagate became Marvell's first customer. As boys in Singapore he and Sehat built a Van de Graaff generator from surplus copper wire.
notes: Strong data-center angle via Credo (AI interconnect). Credo contacts are company IR/media (published in FY2026 earnings release), not personal. Avoid Marvell 2016 accounting-probe ouster topic (concerned his brother/sister-in-law).

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Applied Intuition (Sunnyvale, CA)

name: Azalia Mirheseini
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Ricursive Intelligence; Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Stanford University
profile: Azalia Mirhoseini (Forbes spells it Mirheseini) is an AI researcher who co-created AlphaChip, Google's deep-RL chip floorplanning system used on TPUs, and worked at Google Brain, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. notes: Correct spelling is Mirhoseini. Strong fit for an AI/data-center podcast (chips + energy efficiency of AI). Accessible academic; press via JConnelly. Forbes lists her as a 'former' billionaire in real-time data; her equity stake is undisclosed.

current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Ricursive Intelligence; Assistant Professor of Computer Science, Stanford (directs the Scaling Intelligence lab)

name: Jayashree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET)

notes: Highly relevant to data-center theme (AI networking). Media contact per Arista releases is Corporate Communications (Amanda Jaramillo); ir@arista.com seen in 2026 Business Wire release (could not load page directly, verify). Also active on LinkedIn/X as public CEO.

name: Michael P Scarpelli
current_role: Independent Director and Audit Committee Chair, ClickHouse (since Sept 2026); former CFO of Snowflake (2019-2025)
profile: Mike Scarpelli is one of tech's best-known CFOs. He was CFO of Data Domain, ServiceNow (2011-2019) and Snowflake (2019-2025), taking each through its IPO, including Snowflake's record 2020 software IPO; his Snowflake equity made him a billionaire. name: Chen Youxing
current_role: Listed as Vice Chairman / director, StarPower Semiconductor Ltd (SSE: 603290), Jiaxing (per third-party profiles)

name: Hock E. Tan
current_role: President and CEO, Broadcom Inc.; Director, Meta Platforms (since 2024)
profile: Penang-born Hock Tan (Tan Hock Eng) came to MIT on a scholarship, then held finance roles at GM and PepsiCo, co-founded a Singapore VC firm and ran Integrated Circuit Systems before becoming CEO of Avago in 2006. He built Avago into today's Broadcom through serial M&A (Broadcom, CA, Symantec enterprise, VMware) and now leads one of the key suppliers of custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and data-center networking chips.

deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he pledged $4M to MIT to endow the Nam P. Suh Professorship in mechanical engineering, honoring his former MIT professor (first holder: quantum-computing pioneer Seth Lloyd). He earned both his MIT BS and MS in mechanical engineering in 1975.

current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hunan Goke Microelectronics (国科微, SZSE: 300672), Changsha
profile: Xiang Ping (b. 1971) has led Goke Microelectronics, a Changsha-based fabless chip designer founded in 2008, serving as chairman and general manager since 2015 (earlier a supervisor). Goke listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017 and makes direct-broadcast-satellite HD chips, 4K/8K ultra-HD decoder and display chips, AI vision SoCs and automotive AI chips, including its own in-house NPU.

deep_cut_fact: He started out as a journalist, not an engineer: chief editor of the South China edition of 'Network News' (1995-97), then head of the Shenzhen bureau of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' newspaper Science Times (1997-2000) and deputy GM of its business centre (2000-04).

name: Huang Zezhong

profile: Huang Zezhong and his cousin Huang Yanhuang each own about 47.9% of Quanzhou Jiadeli, a Fujian maker of BOPP electrical film. That film is the core dielectric in the film capacitors used in EVs, solar and wind inverters and HVDC grid equipment. The pair took control in 2010, and Jiadeli listed on the Shanghai main board on 22 May 2026, putting him on the 2026 Hurun list.
interesting_fact: Jiadeli's niche is an energy-transition chokepoint. BOPP film for capacitors depends on electrical-grade polypropylene resin that is still mostly imported (about 80% of Jiadeli's comes from Borouge). The film goes into the capacitors used in EV drivetrains, renewable inverters and flexible HVDC transmission.
notes: The 'Jiadeli' in the dataset is Quanzhou Jiadeli Electronics Material (嘉德利). He is general manager, not chairman; the chairman is Huang Huanming. Board secretary is Huang Shengquan, reachable via ir@jdlxcl.com. He keeps a very low profile and I found no English-language coverage.

name: Zhang Xingang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Shaanxi Yuanjie Semiconductor Technology (STAR Market: 688498)
profile: Born in 1970, Tsinghua materials graduate with a USC materials-science PhD and a US citizen. He worked on optical chips at Luminent from 2001, then returned to China in 2013 to found Yuanjie in Xianyang, Shaanxi, an IDM making laser (DFB/EML) chips for optical transceivers. Demand for AI data-center optics sent the stock up ~780% in a year, making him a billionaire in 2026.

deep_cut_fact: Yuanjie's first product, launched after about a year of lab work, was a 2.5G 1310nm DFB laser chip. By 2018 it had shipped 10 million DFB chips, becoming China's first IDM to mass-produce optical chips at scale. He chose Xianyang because the city had just launched tech-startup support policies.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics theme. Forbes said the company did not respond to its request for comment. The board secretary (Cheng Shuo) is the published IR contact.

name: Vadim Vikulov

notes: Russia-based; Aston website (aston.ru) not reachable from here and no published press contact found. Consider sanctions/compliance context before any outreach to Russian agribusiness owners.

Sensitive context: Passes faces a lawsuit, and in 2026 there was press about her exit as CEO and a personal dispute. Avoid these in outreach. She also started a DJ/music side career in 2026.

current_role: President & sole shareholder, Headington Resources / Headington Companies (Dallas); co-founder, Ley Line Entertainment
profile: Dallas-born, Oklahoma City-raised oilman who founded Headington Oil in 1978 (moved to Dallas in 1984) and in 2008 sold North Dakota Bakken acreage to XTO Energy for $1.85B. His Headington Resources spans oil & gas, Dallas real estate and hotels (The Joule), private equity and entertainment; he's also a prolific film and theatre producer.

He co-founded the Headington Institute, which provides psychological care for humanitarian aid workers.

current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President and CEO, Super Micro Computer Inc. (Supermicro), San Jose

Co-founded Supermicro in 1993 with his wife Sara Liu as a five-person motherboard shop; it is now a leading builder of Nvidia-based AI server and liquid-cooled rack systems for data centres. notes: Low public profile compared with brother Ryan Smith (Utah Jazz owner, Qualtrics chairman). No published personal contact or verified social accounts found; Qualtrics press office or Ryan Smith's network are indirect routes.

SICC listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022 and added a Hong Kong listing in 2025.

deep_cut_fact: A silicate-engineering graduate of Shandong Institute of Light Industry, he spent 15 years as a process engineer at the Jinan Bulb Factory; when it closed he started over at 38 (2002) with Jinan Tianye, a Volvo excavator dealership that grew into Shandong's leading construction-machinery seller.
notes: No personal channels found. Company website www.sicc.cc (as listed in HKEX filings, e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0327/2026032704444.pdf); approach via SICC's board office/IR. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

profile: Tang Zhuang (b. 1973) is a co-founder and CTO of Maxscend (卓胜微), a Wuxi-based maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, filters) for smartphones that listed in Shenzhen in 2019. name: Wu Daohong

profile: Combustion engineer who did postdoctoral research at China University of Petroleum (1995) and founded Shenwu in 1996 to commercialise energy-saving industrial furnace and burner technology. name: David Yakobashvili
current_role: President, Orion Heritage Co. (private Museum 'Collection', Moscow); founder of InOil (GreenBooster fuel additive)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1957) entrepreneur who cofounded Russian dairy-and-juice giant Wimm-Bill-Dann and chaired it 2001-2010; it sold to PepsiCo for ~$5.7B in 2010-11, netting him ~$600M for his ~10% stake. current_role: President, Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM); owner of Kencana Capital Sdn Bhd
profile: Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir (b. 1961), son of ex-PM Mahathir, is a petroleum engineer who founded Kencana Petroleum. It merged with SapuraCrest in 2012 to form SapuraKencana (now Sapura Energy). He now invests via Kencana Capital and leads Malaysian motorsport as MAM president.

Shunfeng (01165.HK) is in liquidation (shares suspended 19 Nov 2025) and its only contacts are the liquidators. He is a creditor (via APRDIL). No published personal or office contact found. name: Zhang Tianren

profile: Zhang Tianren built Tianneng from a debt-laden battery workshop in Changxing, Zhejiang (1986) into China's largest lead-acid battery maker, powering the country's e-bike boom; it listed in Hong Kong in 2007 and its Tianneng Battery arm trades on Shanghai's STAR Market. He is now pushing Tianneng into lithium, sodium-ion and energy-storage batteries.

profile: Long Daqiang (龙大强, b. 1973) and his wife Meng Liye, both from Pei County, Jiangsu, moved from steel trading into solar in 2010, founding cell maker Zhongyu PV and then SolarSpace (中润光能). profile: Founded Hong Kong-listed Sinolink Worldwide (chairman 1997-2013), which built city-gas distributor Panva Gas and power business Enerchina. current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shijiazhuang Shangtai Technology (SZ:001301)
profile: Born 1966, Ouyang is a carbon-materials engineer who built Shangtai Technology in Hebei into a major maker of graphite anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. He owns about 36.5% of the company, which listed in Shenzhen in 2022. H1 2026 revenue rose 33% to RMB 4.5bn.
interesting_fact: Shangtai runs an integrated anode model that does the power-hungry graphitization step in-house. In H1 2026 demand outran this integrated capacity, so it had to outsource some graphitization to keep up with orders.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Hunan University in 1988, Ouyang spent 12 years (1988-2000) as an engineer at the Shanghai Carbon Factory, then ran Shanghai Shangtai Carbon before building the anode business in Hebei.

name: Shi Mingda
current_role: Honorary chairman (and vice chairman) of Tongfu Microelectronics (002156.SZ); son Shi Lei is chairman & president
profile: Nanjing University physics graduate and engineer (b. 1945) who in 1990 took over the debt-ridden Nantong Transistor Factory and turned it into Tongfu Microelectronics, now the world's No.4 chip packaging & test group. name: Gai Lujiang

profile: A finance professional and investor representative appointed chairman and CEO of Iluvatar CoreX (founded 2015) after its 2022-23 management changes. name: Dai Weimin
current_role: Founder, Chairman, President and CEO, VeriSilicon Microelectronics (688521.SH), Shanghai
profile: Dai Weimin (Wayne Dai) earned his BS and PhD in EECS at UC Berkeley, taught computer engineering at UC Santa Cruz and founded chip-design-software firms Ultima and Celestry (bought by Cadence in 2002). He founded VeriSilicon in Shanghai in 2001, building it into a major custom-silicon and semiconductor-IP supplier listed on Shanghai's STAR Market.

deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a chip entrepreneur he spent 17 years in academia at UC Santa Cruz (1988-2005), rising from tutor to full professor of computer engineering, and overlapped his professorship with founding Ultima (1995) and VeriSilicon (2001).
notes: Known in English as Wayne Dai (Wei-Ming Dai). Speaks frequently at industry events (e.g. on chiplets and AI chips), English-fluent - a plausible podcast guest; route via IR or company news enquiry.

current_role: Private investor; owner of the Uvalnaya coal-mining project (Kuzbass), per Forbes
profile: Russian mining engineer (b. 1952, Tula Oblast) who designed Soviet coal-mining machinery, then in 1995 co-founded coal producer Sibuglemet, which he ran until 2003. He made his fortune selling his Sibuglemet and Uralkali (potash) stakes in 2013; since 2017 he has developed the Uvalnaya coal project, producing 6M+ tonnes a year.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a coal baron he was an engineer-designer of Soviet machine-building plants and worked at state coal monopoly Rosugol, taking part in the reform of the Russian coal industry.
deep_cut_fact: As chief technical designer at the Kopeisk Engineering Plant he helped design the GPKS, one of the most widely used continuous heading (tunnelling) machines in Soviet/Russian mines; he holds 41 patents and inventor's certificates and a 1991 PhD on mining machinery.
notes: Very private; no published personal, office or press contact found. Russia-based coal investor - check sanctions/reputational issues before any outreach. Web-search quota ran out, so current Uvalnaya ownership is per Forbes only.

name: Sung Kyu-dong
current_role: Founder and CEO (co-CEO with Park Jong-goo), EO Technics (KOSDAQ: 039030), Anyang, South Korea
profile: Sung Kyu-dong (성규동) founded EO Technics in 1989 and listed it on KOSDAQ in 2000. The company makes laser equipment for memory-chip production: laser markers that etch traceability codes onto chips and laser annealing (LA) tools, plus dicing/grooving systems; it is reported to supply laser annealing tools to Samsung. Ranked #49 on Forbes' 2026 Korea's 50 Richest.
interesting_fact: EO Technics' flagship laser markers etch an ID code onto each chip so manufacturers can trace the source of any defect; its LA tools use targeted laser heat to activate the electrical pathways inside chips.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding EO Technics he worked at the Goldstar (now LG) Central Research Center, Daewoo Heavy Industries and Korea Laser, the company that pioneered industrial laser technology in South Korea.
notes: Low-profile engineer-founder. Company site publishes only a sales address (sales@eotechnics.com) and a Q&A form; no press/IR email found. Good fit for AI-memory/HBM supply-chain angle. Korean-language outreach likely needed.

name: Huang Shanbing
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu JieJie Microelectronics Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen: 300623)
profile: Huang Shanbing (黄善兵) founded the predecessor of JieJie Microelectronics in Qidong, Jiangsu in 1995 and chairs the company, which makes power semiconductor discrete devices such as thyristors (triacs/SCRs) and protection devices; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2017.

current_role: Venture Partner, New Enterprise Associates (NEA); director and audit committee chair of Nvidia, Tenable and GoodLeap

profile: Li Zhen (李缜, b. 1964, Tongcheng, Anhui) left a Hefei government research post for business, moving from property into batteries with Hefei Guoxuan High-Tech in 2006. Gotion makes LFP/NMC cells and cathode/anode materials, listed in Shenzhen in 2015, raised $685M on SIX Swiss in 2022, and counts Volkswagen as a ~24% shareholder.

name: Igor Yusufov
current_role: Former Russian Minister of Energy (2001-04) and founder of Fund Energy; per Forbes Russia, no longer manages projects (since 2020) and divested declared assets by March 2022
profile: Dagestan-born (1956) power engineer turned official: ran the state reserves agency, served as Russia's energy minister 2001-04, then presidential envoy for international energy cooperation and a Gazprom board member (2003-13). After 2011 he invested via Fund Energy in oil and gas, mining and renewables, but Forbes Russia reports he exited those holdings by 2022.

deep_cut_fact: Before government he was a working power engineer: after Novocherkassk Polytechnic he worked at Mosenergo, then spent four years in Cuba as a technology expert on the construction site of a Havana thermal power plant.
notes: Dropped off Forbes lists (listed as 'former'); says he has exited his assets. No published contact found; former company site corporationenergy.ru may be stale. Outreach to a former Russian minister may raise sanctions/compliance questions; check before contacting. Low fit unless covering Russian energy history.

name: Sanjay Mehrotra
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Micron Technology (MU); director, CDW
profile: Kanpur-born (1958) electrical engineer (UC Berkeley BS/MS) who co-founded SanDisk in 1988 with Eli Harari and Jack Yuan and was its CEO 2011-2016 until the Western Digital sale. CEO of Micron since 2017, he has steered it into the AI boom via high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for data-center GPUs, which drove Micron's surge and his billionaire status.
interesting_fact: He holds dozens of flash-memory patents and was elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in 2022 for contributions to multilevel-cell (MLC) NAND flash design that made dense flash storage practical.

Later, in 1984, he was slated to be one of four Atmel co-founders with mentor George Perlegos, but stayed at Seeq out of loyalty.
notes: Public-company CEO; requests go via Micron corporate communications. Very strong data-center/AI memory angle (HBM). Gave a 2019 Computer History Museum oral history, useful for prep.

name: Zhang Jianhui
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, HyperStrong (Beijing HyperStrong Technology / 海博思创, Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Dr. Zhang Jianhui (张剑辉) founded HyperStrong in Beijing in 2011 after studying at Tsinghua and Berkeley and working as a chip R&D/design engineer in Silicon Valley. HyperStrong became one of China's top battery energy-storage system integrators (400+ projects, 70+ GWh in 30+ countries) and listed on the STAR Market in 2025. He now pushes a 'storage + X' strategy, including storage-plus-compute.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 HyperStrong broke ground in Baotou on an integrated storage-and-compute project with a 'token factory' (词元工厂): grid-side batteries co-sited with a distributed AI computing center selling metered AI compute, using its own solid-state transformer (HyperSST).
deep_cut_fact: Before energy storage he was a Silicon Valley chip R&D/design engineer ('from Tsinghua to Berkeley'); in Sept 2026 he was named one of the '2026 Beijing Role Models' (北京榜样) for August.
notes: Excellent fit for the energy x data-center theme (storage-compute 'token factory' in Baotou). HyperStrong has US offices (Chicago, Houston, San Francisco) and is shortlisted at the Energy Storage Awards in London on 19 Nov 2026, possible in-person angle. Contact is company-level only.

He then invested in Hawaii (owning ~80% of macadamia producer Royal Hawaiian Orchards by 2018) and in solar-panel maker First Solar.

name: Chi Fung Cheng
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Technology Officer and Director, Credo Technology Group (Nasdaq: CRDO)
profile: Chi Fung 'Lawrence' Cheng, 57, co-founded high-speed connectivity chipmaker Credo in 2008 after 11 years as an engineering director of analog design at Marvell, and has been CTO since. Credo's SerDes/DSP chips, retimers and 'ZeroFlap' active electrical cables connect servers and switches in AI data centers at up to 1.6T; it listed on Nasdaq in 2022. name: Andrew Feldman
