Cerebras IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2026 at $185/share, raising $5.55B and jumping ~68% on day one; he owns roughly 5% between stock and options.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' Wafer-Scale Engine uses an entire silicon wafer as one processor (WSE-3: 4 trillion transistors, 900,000 cores); in 2022 the Computer History Museum installed a permanent display of it as the first wafer-scale integration achieved in computing history.
deep_cut_fact: Data-center energy was his theme long before AI: his prior startup SeaMicro was 'founded to dramatically reduce the power consumed by servers' - its microservers used about a quarter of the power and a sixth of the space of conventional servers - and AMD bought it in 2012 for ~$334M.

public_contacts.value: pr@zmcommunications.com (ZM Communications, media contact on Cerebras press releases)

notes: Highly media-accessible and a frequent podcast guest; excellent fit for AI chips/inference and data-center power. PR agency contact dates from 2024 releases - check a recent Cerebras release for the current media contact. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified in this pass.

name: Jay Hyung Son
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, Innoscience (Suzhou) Technology (HKEX: 2577) - responsible for business development (per Dec 2024 prospectus)

name: Rodney Lewis

deep_cut_fact: He holds a BA in criminal justice from what is now Texas A&M International University in Laredo, paid $13,000 for his first well, and in 2014 received Webb County's 'Angel of Hope' award for providing Christmas gifts to needy children.

He was re-elected chairman and named general manager in February 2026.

Leyard screens lit the 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony and it supplied most of the giant LED floor for the 2022 Winter Olympics opening.

name: Chen Gang
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy Co. (AIKO, SSE: 600732)
profile: Chen Gang founded Aiko Solar in 2009 (Guangdong Aiko Technology), a solar cell maker with plants in Foshan, Yiwu and Tianjin that sells globally. Aiko rose from a mid-sized player to the world's No.1 PERC cell shipper in 2018, listed via a backdoor deal with ST Xinmei in 2019, and now champions n-type back-contact (ABC) cells and modules. He continues to lead it through the industry's consolidation.
interesting_fact: Aiko went from outside China's top 10 cell makers to No.1 globally in PERC cell shipments in 2018; Chen chose a backdoor listing because 'in an industry reshuffle, time matters more than money.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2017, while ordinary mono cells were very profitable, he halted his own mono lines to bet on unproven tubular PERC tech, pre-agreeing with suppliers to convert the equipment back if it failed. His rule: 'If even the worst outcome isn't bad, you dare to do it' (最坏的结果都不坏，你就敢做了).
notes: Common name - matched via Aiko Solar. Gives interviews to Chinese press (People's Daily Energy, The Paper at SNEC 2025); likely needs Mandarin outreach. Co-owner listed: Ou Chunlian. No dedicated English IR email found; Chinese annual report may list a securities-affairs email.

profile: Hurun lists Ou Chunlian (欧春连) jointly with Chen Gang, founder, chairman and controller of Aiko Solar (爱旭股份), a leading Chinese maker of high-efficiency PV cells and modules. current_role: Chairman of the board, Meijin Energy Group (controlling shareholder of Shanxi Meijin Energy, SZSE: 000723)

current_role: President Commissioner, PT Prima Andalan Mandiri Tbk (IDX: MCOL, 'Mandiri Coal'); controlling shareholder of Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa (Mandiri Services)
profile: Indonesian coal magnate behind the Mandiri group, whose PT Mandiri Intiperkasa mine in North Kalimantan sells coal under the 'Mandiri Coal' brand, with in-house mining contracting and barging units. He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021 and the coal-services arm in 2023; his family controls ~70% of MCOL. Brother Handy Glivirgo is president director.
interesting_fact: Detik dubbed him one of Indonesia's 'OKB' (new rich) when he debuted on Forbes' billionaire list with US$1.2B; Mandiri Coal hit record output of 9.02 million tonnes in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: The group's mine traces back to a 1994 Coal Contract of Work (No. 08/PK/PTBA-MI/1994) for a 50,000-ha area in North Kalimantan; after revisions cut it to 9,240 ha, production only began in 2004, a decade later. He has been president commissioner of PAM since 2005.
notes: Very low media profile; no personal accounts found. Best route is MCOL's corporate secretary. Commissioner-since-2005 detail from Detik.

name: Xu Yingtong
profile: Chinese energy-storage entrepreneur who briefly appeared on Forbes' real-time billionaires list (est. ~US$1.03B, now 'former') and on the Hurun China 2026 list. The Forbes profile page no longer renders details, and the company could not be confirmed from accessible sources.
notes: UNVERIFIED lead: may be the founder/chairman of Shenzhen SOFAR New Energy (首航新能源, SOFARSOLAR; Shenzhen IPO 2025, inverters/storage) — check its prospectus before use. Web search budget ran out mid-lane; Baidu Baike blocked, so identity left uncertain.

name: Lee Chae-yoon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Leeno Industrial (KOSDAQ: 058470), Busan
profile: Lee Chae-yoon (b. 1950, Namhae County) founded Leeno Industrial in 1978, nine years after finishing technical high school in Busan. Leeno makes IC test sockets and 'Leeno Pin' probes that check chips for defects, for more than 1,000 customers including Nvidia, Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC. AI-driven demand made him a billionaire in 2024; he owns about 35% of the company.
interesting_fact: The company name combines his surname with his wife's. Leeno was the first Korean maker of semiconductor test sockets and probes, which were entirely imported until the 1980s. 'Leeno Pin' is now the industry's generic word for test probes, with about 70% global share.
deep_cut_fact: A self-made engineer who kept studying: he finished Kwangsung (Kyeongsung) Engineering High School in 1969, founded Leeno in 1978, and earned his Dong-Eui University degree only in 1991, 13 years after starting the company. He later completed a KAIST executive programme.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. Route via Leeno's general company email or contact page in Busan. Korean-language outreach is advisable. Forbes source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnkang/2024/03/14/founder-of-chip-testing-firm-rides-ai-boom-to-become-south-koreas-newest-billionaire/

name: Toby Neugebauer
current_role: Co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (FRMI); former CEO (left April 2026); co-owner of MLS club Austin FC
profile: West Texas-born energy investor (NYU BBA '93) who worked at Kidder Peabody, co-founded Windrock Energy (sold to Macquarie) and in 1998 co-founded Quantum Energy Partners, running five funds. In 2025 he co-founded Fermi America to build 'Project Matador', a multi-gigawatt private power grid and AI data-center campus near Amarillo, and took it public in Oct 2025.
interesting_fact: Fermi's Project Matador in the Texas Panhandle was pitched as one of the world's largest energy-and-data campuses, combining gas, nuclear, solar and grid power to serve hyperscale AI tenants.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, his philanthropy has focused on family formation in US inner cities, and abroad he has worked with orphanages in China and helped build and maintain schools in Rwanda and Zambia.
notes: Sensitive timing: he left Fermi as CEO in April 2026, was removed from the board, and has been in a public proxy fight with the company (calling for a sale/special meeting). Avoid the dispute in outreach; his PR firm Collected Strategies issues his statements. Fermi IR is not a good route for him now.

name: Fang Xiaoling
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Maxio Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (STAR Market: 688449).
profile: Fang Xiaoling (b. 1963, US citizen) holds Zhejiang University BS/MS degrees and a University of Utah EE PhD. After co-founding Taiwanese fabless firm JMicron, she founded Maxio in Hangzhou in 2014; it designs SSD/data-storage controller chips and AIoT signal-processing chips, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in late 2024. She controls ~45% of Maxio.
interesting_fact: Surveillance giant Hikvision invested in Maxio in its third year and became its 2nd-largest shareholder (37% with a subsidiary pre-IPO); Maxio's controllers are mass-deployed at YMTC and Longsys.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips for storage, she was a principal engineer at Sonic Innovations, a Salt Lake City hearing-aid maker (then ranked world No. 7), from 1995-2001 right after her Utah PhD; she then cofounded JMicron and ran JMicron USA for 15 years.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Maxio IR (board secretary/CFO Qian Xiaofei). Data-center angle: enterprise SSD controllers.

name: Luo Yungang
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List in 2017-2018 with wealth attributed to Bao Ta (Baota) Petrochemical and education. Searches found no public source tying a Luo Yungang (罗运刚) to Baota Petrochemical Group (Ningxia), whose publicly known head was Sun Hengchao, so his role could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity unconfirmed; no web footprint found in Chinese or English. Only appears on Hurun 2017-18. Baota Petrochemical Group ran into a bond default and its founder was detained in 2018, so the listing may be stale. Recommend dropping or verifying via Hurun directly.

name: Wang Jingliang
profile: Listed once on the Hurun China Rich List (2021) with wealth from 'Energy New Material' in the packaging production industry. Chinese-language searches for 王敬良 did not reliably link him to a specific company, so the company and his role could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not identify him. The 'Energy New Material' + packaging description resembles Yunnan Energy New Material (SEMCORP, 恩捷股份, which started in packaging), but no source ties 王敬良 to it. Do not use without manual verification, e.g. Hurun 2021 list entry or company filings.

name: Ye Liaoning
current_role: Co-founder and consultant, Sunny Optical Technology; chairman until 1 Nov 2025 (retired from the board citing retirement age)
profile: Ye Liaoning (叶辽宁, b. ~1965) joined the Yuyao Chengbei optical-instrument factory that became Sunny Optical in 1984 and is counted among the group's founders. He rose to deputy GM (1995), executive director (2007) and chairman, leading Sunny's growth into a global phone/auto camera-optics leader, then stepped down in Nov 2025 and stays on as a consultant.
interesting_fact: He stepped down as chairman effective 1 Nov 2025 ahead of reaching retirement age in early 2026, handing over to founder Wang Wenjian's son Wang Tan Jiong, and remains a consultant to the group.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the factory in 1984 as a teenager and earned his diploma part-time from Zhejiang Radio & TV University only in 1999; he received China's National May-First Labor Medal (2019) and the title National Model Worker (2020).
notes: Low international profile; now retired from the board. Only published route is Sunny's IR office. Fortune shared with Sunny co-founders (see Wang Wenjian, P05955).

name: Ivan Müller Botelho
current_role: Patriarch of the controlling Botelho family of Energisa S.A. and its long-time former chairman; he is not listed on the board elected in April 2026
profile: An electrical engineer (University of Miami) from Leopoldina, Minas Gerais, Ivan Botelho is the third generation of the family that has controlled Brazilian utility Energisa since 1905. He built it from a regional Cataguases utility into a group with nine state distribution companies, transmission and gas, serving more than 20 million customers. His sons Ricardo (CEO) and Maurício (CFO) now run it.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Energisa, the underdog bidder, won the 2013 creditors' vote for the bankrupt Grupo Rede over CPFL, a deal that changed the group's scale. In 2026, at 92, he published a memoir, 'A jornada da Energia para o futuro', based on his testimony to journalist Plínio Fraga.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the front line, in the lines and power plants. His memoir recalls installing Brazil's first photoelectric cell to switch street lighting on automatically, and a safety-glove demonstration that ended up shutting down power to the whole town. He was also an early backer of the Instituto Liberal think tank.
notes: He is about 92 (per JB, March 2026), so the realistic route is via Energisa IR or his sons; CEO Ricardo Botelho is the active public face. The new memoir (2026) is a natural hook for outreach. Confirm his current board status in Energisa's Formulário de Referência.

name: Muhammed Aziz Khan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Summit Group (Bangladesh); based in Singapore
profile: Bangladesh-born, Singapore-based Muhammed Aziz Khan (b. 1955, Dhaka IBA MBA) started out as a trader and founded Summit in 1985; it built Bangladesh's first independent power plant (Khulna, 1998) and its first private off-dock port, and now spans power, LNG, ports, fibre optics and real estate. Japan's JERA owns 22% of Summit Power International, run by his daughter Ayesha.
interesting_fact: He told Nikkei Asia Summit plans Bangladesh's first data centre using Summit Power's gas-fired capacity: 'Summit Group's next phase focuses on integrating energy and data, leveraging our LNG and fibre-optic expertise.'
deep_cut_fact: Singapore's Prime Minister's Office awarded him the Public Service Medal (COVID-19) for financially helping Bangladeshi workers in Singapore during the pandemic; he and his wife were also the first Bangladeshis named UNICEF International Council members.

public_contacts.value: enquiry@summitpowerinternational.com (Summit Power International, One Raffles Place, Singapore)

notes: Very good fit: energy + data-centre angle (gas-to-data-centre plan, fibre/LNG). Gives interviews to Bangladeshi press and Nikkei. Best route: Summit Power International Singapore enquiry form (press category).

name: Gennady Kozovoy
current_role: Shareholder (~5.7%) of Evraz plc; former CEO and board member of Raspadskaya coal company (Mezhdurechensk, Kuzbass)
profile: Siberian coal executive who rose through Russia's Raspadskaya mine. In 1993 he was elected general director and, with partner Alexander Vagin, gained control of the company as workers' shares were bought up. Raspadskaya listed in 2006. In 2012 they sold control to Evraz for cash plus Evraz shares, his main asset today. He stepped down as CEO in July 2014.
interesting_fact: Kozovoy and Vagin turned Raspadskaya, once a 'people's enterprise' owned by its miners, into one of Russia's biggest coking-coal producers. They sold their stake to Evraz for about $202M plus roughly 11% of Evraz.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 36 years at Raspadskaya, starting as an electrician-fitter (elektroslesar) at the mine and rising to general director, as the company noted when he handed over the CEO role in 2014.
notes: Very private and gives virtually no press. Russia-based. Evraz was sanctioned by the UK in 2022 (Abramovich link) and is no longer LSE-traded, so outreach may be impractical. Patronymic Ivanovich. No published contact found.

name: Mikhail Abyzov
current_role: None; former Russian Minister for Open Government Affairs (2012-2018), now serving a prison sentence in Russia
profile: Minsk-born Russian energy and engineering businessman (b. 1972) who built his fortune via fuel supply and power assets such as Novosibirskenergo, and chaired engineering group E4. He was Russia's Minister for Open Government Affairs 2012-2018. Arrested in 2019, he was sentenced in Dec 2023 to 12 years; a later RVC-related conviction raised the total to 14 years.
interesting_fact: He set up his first company, Intershops, in 1990 at about 18, selling Turkish consumer goods and later office equipment, before moving into fuel supply and Siberian power utilities.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: imprisoned in Russia (12-year sentence Dec 2023 per Moscow Times https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/12/22/former-russian-minister-sentenced-to-12-years-for-embezzlement-a83522; further cases since, incl. 14-year combined sentence reported by Current Time). He denies the charges. No public contacts; deep-cut fact left empty deliberately.

name: Kirill Shamalov
current_role: Shareholder of PAO SIBUR Holding (about 4% per Forbes); listed by the UK sanctions register as Deputy Chairman of SIBUR's Management Board (current status unverified)
profile: Russian petrochemicals investor and son of Rossiya Bank co-owner Nikolai Shamalov. He joined Sibur as a vice president in 2008, became deputy CEO in 2012 and built up a stake that made him briefly Russia's youngest billionaire. He later sold most of it and is believed to keep about 4% of Sibur. He is under US (2018), UK and EU sanctions.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes he became a vice president of Sibur, Russia's largest petrochemicals company, at age 26, after studying law at Saint Petersburg State University.
deep_cut_fact: According to a Sibur biography cited by Bloomberg, in 2002, at about 20 and still a law student, he was named Gazprom's chief legal counsel for foreign economic activity. He later became chief legal counsel at Gazprombank before joining Sibur in 2008.
notes: High risk: he is sanctioned by the US, UK and EU, and most coverage concerns his former marriage to Putin's daughter and how he got his Sibur shares. He is very private and gives no interviews. The only route is Sibur's corporate press office, and it is unclear whether he still holds a Sibur post. Probably not a suitable podcast guest.

name: Cesar Maklary
current_role: Co-founder and President, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, HQ New York)
profile: French co-founder (with Gary Wu and Jamie Cox) of Fluidstack, which grew from an Oxford-born GPU marketplace into a builder/operator of large AI data centers for customers including Anthropic, Google and Meta. A ~$1.5B round led by Jane Street in 2026 valued Fluidstack at over $18B, making the three co-founders billionaires at around 30; he joined in 2020.
interesting_fact: Maklary was the face of Fluidstack's Feb 2025 deal, announced by Emmanuel Macron at the Paris AI Action Summit, to help build an $11.5B AI data center in France ('Nvidia has told me that they will send those chips when we need them'); later that year Jensen Huang signed a Lego model of an Nvidia chip for him and Wu at GTC.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he worked on aerodynamics for a Formula One team. He has explained Fluidstack's origin as matching PhD friends starved for compute with 'hardcore cloud gaming friends' whose rigs sat idle most of the week.
notes: Great fit for data-center podcast. Speaks at conferences (e.g. RAISE Summit Paris). France data-center project was reportedly scrapped in 2026 in favour of US sites (avoid framing as failure). Fluidstack declines to comment on valuation/net worth.

name: Gary Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, New York)
profile: Most likely the Gary Wu who co-founded Fluidstack in 2017 while studying economics at Oxford. It began renting idle gamers' GPUs to AI researchers and now builds gigawatt-scale AI data centers, incl. Anthropic's planned $50B build-out on Google TPUs. A Sept 2026 round valued it above $18B, making Wu (31) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Fluidstack's backers project it managing up to 1.3 GW across 10+ sites in 2026 and aspire to 17+ GW by 2030; it appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google.
deep_cut_fact: Fluidstack started in 2017 helping gamers make 'beer money' by renting out their idle GPUs to AI researchers; the company never disclosed raising any outside funding until July 2026.
notes: Identity uncertain only because the input lists country 'China' while Fluidstack is UK-founded and now New York-HQ; source of wealth ('AI datacenter builder') and new-billionaire status match strongly. Founders give few interviews; Fluidstack declines press comment. Note Anthropic is a major customer (research compiled by Claude, an Anthropic model).

name: James Dacombe
current_role: Founder & CEO, Olix (OLIX Computing, London AI-inference chip startup); founder & CEO, CoMind (brain monitoring)
profile: British serial founder (b. ~2001) who dropped out of school at 17 to build CoMind, a non-invasive brain-monitoring company, then in 2024 founded Olix (formerly Flux Computing), which designs chips and systems for AI inference. Olix raised $312m in August 2026 at ~$3.3bn, making him Europe's youngest self-made billionaire per Forbes (~30% of Olix, ~12% of CoMind).
interesting_fact: Forbes counts him as one of only 11 self-made billionaires worldwide under 30 - and one of four based outside the US; Olix tripled in value between February and August 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started programming apps and websites at 13 while at Ashville College in Harrogate, North Yorkshire, then became a Thiel Fellow. He told the Sunday Times in 2024: 'An advantage of starting my business so young was naivety... you just try a lot of things.'
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI-infrastructure angle (Olix pitches a 'token factory' rebuild of the datacentre). Olix and CoMind did not respond to Forbes/Fortune comment requests in Aug 2026, so expect a press-office gate; press@olix.com is the best route.

name: Jamie Cox
current_role: Cofounder, Fluidstack (AI cloud / data-center builder, now HQ'd in New York)
profile: British cofounder (with Gary Wu, later Cesar Maklary) of Fluidstack, started in 2017 as a marketplace renting idle gamer GPUs to AI researchers and now a builder/operator of large AI data centers, including custom sites for Anthropic in New York and Texas and a planned 1GW campus in France. A 2026 Jane Street-led $1.5B round valued it at $18B+, making Cox (29) a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes reported Fluidstack appears to be the first publicly known operator of Google TPU data centers outside Google; Macron announced its ~EUR10B, 1-gigawatt French AI data center project in Feb 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He was reading classics at Oxford when he met economics student Gary Wu; he dropped out in 2018 to become a Thiel Fellow, and in 2020 he and Wu started Treecard, a cashback card that funded tree planting, alongside Fluidstack.
notes: Prime fit for the data-center podcast. Specific exec title not published (Wu is CEO, Maklary President). Company declined comment to Forbes on funding; route via press@fluidstack.io.

name: Baoshen Zhong
current_role: Chairman and President (General Manager), LONGi Green Energy Technology Co. (SSE: 601012)
profile: Zhong Baoshen chairs LONGi Green Energy, a global leader in monocrystalline solar wafers, cells and modules. He first built Fushun Magnetic Equipment, then joined Lanzhou University classmate Li Zhenguo at LONGi in 2006 as chairman, adding the CEO role in 2025. He is now steering LONGi through a PV downturn and into energy storage and hydrogen.
interesting_fact: LONGi bet early on monocrystalline silicon when multicrystalline was the industry mainstream, and that bet made mono the dominant solar technology. In 2026 Zhong set a goal of growing LONGi's energy-storage business to a scale close to its PV business within five years.
deep_cut_fact: LONGi's origin story starts with a phone call. In September 2005 Zhong was sightseeing at the Petronas Twin Towers after a business trip to Malaysia when Li Zhenguo, his 1986-entry Lanzhou University physics classmate and fellow Henan native, called about buying used US mono-crystal pullers. Zhong replied: 'Wait for me to come back' (等我回来).
notes: Very visible: NPC deputy, Boao and UN energy forum speaker, regular earnings-call commentator. Best route is LONGi PR (PR@longi.com). Topical hooks: solar-plus-storage ('光储融合') and the anti-'involution' push in Chinese PV. Sources differ on his major (Forbes says metallurgy, Chinese media say physics).

name: Zhang Xuezheng
current_role: Founder and actual controller (via Wentianxia Technology Group) of Wingtech Technology (600745.SH); former chairman of Wingtech (to 2025) and CEO of Nexperia (suspended by Dutch order, Sept 2025)
profile: Born 1975, studied at Guangdong University of Technology, then worked at STMicroelectronics and ZTE before founding Wingtech in 2006. Wingtech became China's top phone ODM (it made Xiaomi's Redmi line), then bought Dutch chipmaker Nexperia in 2019. In 2025 the Dutch government took control of Nexperia, suspending him as CEO; he remains Wingtech's controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Wingtech designed and built Xiaomi's Redmi 1, the first smartphone to retail for under 1,000 yuan (799 yuan), which sold more than 30 million units.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he reportedly started Wingtech in Jiaxing with about 30 staff and 100,000 yuan, then went door-to-door in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei with three salespeople to sell its first phone mainboard, the W100. It went on to ship 18 million units.
notes: Highly sensitive: Nexperia/Dutch government dispute (2025-26), a 2024 CSRC fine, and 2026 share freezes tied to an arbitration. Wingtech denied 'fled' rumours in Sept 2026. Rarely gives interviews. No published press/IR email found on the Wingtech English site. Career timeline (ST 1997-98, ZTE 1998-2002) per https://www.maigoo.com/mingren/24826.html.

name: William Moncrief-jr
current_role: Deceased (died 29 December 2021, Fort Worth, aged 101); formerly head of Moncrief Oil
profile: William Alvin 'Tex' Moncrief Jr., Fort Worth wildcatter who with his father 'Monty' built the Moncrief oil and gas business over 70+ years, died on 29 December 2021 aged 101.
notes: Deceased - death reported by NBC DFW and Hart Energy (Dec 2021). Source for death: https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/texas-oil-billionaire-william-tex-moncrief-jr-dead-at-101/2848207/ ; also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Moncrief

name: Randal Nardone
current_role: Director and major shareholder, New Fortress Energy (Nasdaq: NFE); co-founder of Fortress Investment Group
profile: Lawyer-turned-investor Randal Nardone co-founded Fortress Investment Group in 1998 with Wes Edens and Rob Kauffman, served as its CEO 2013-2017, and became a billionaire on Fortress's 2007 IPO; SoftBank bought Fortress in 2017. He sits on the board of Edens' LNG-to-power company New Fortress Energy (about 9.6% holder per its 2025 proxy), which recently agreed to lease 300MW of mobile turbines to a US investment-grade customer.
interesting_fact: Fortress was the first major US private-equity/hedge-fund manager to go public (Feb 2007), which put Nardone on the Forbes billionaires list that year.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, Nardone was a partner and member of the executive committee at New York law firm Thacher Proffitt & Wood, then a principal at BlackRock Financial Management; he holds a BA from UConn and a JD from Boston University School of Law.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Wes Edens (NFE CEO) is the public face. NFE has been through financial stress/refinancing in 2025-26, so avoid wealth/stock topics. Power-for-data-centers angle: NFE's Oct 2026 300MW turbine lease.

name: Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Chairman and CEO, King Power International (Thailand); Chairman, Leicester City FC
profile: 'Top' (b. 1985) took over Thailand's dominant airport duty-free operator King Power, founded by his late father Vichai in 1989, after Vichai's death in an October 2018 helicopter crash; the family fortune is shared with his mother and siblings. He chairs Leicester City (family-owned; reported in Aug 2026 to be up for sale) and the family also owns OH Leuven and a stake in Bangkok's MahaNakhon tower.
interesting_fact: The family name was a gift: Thailand's late King Bhumibol Adulyadej gave Vichai the surname Srivaddhanaprabha; Aiyawatt was born Aiyawatt Raksriaksorn.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious polo player who represents Thailand: he won gold in mixed 2-4 goals polo at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand, and team silver at the 2017 SEA Games in Kuala Lumpur.

public_contacts.value: https://www.lcfc.com (Leicester City FC; chairman statements published here)

notes: Sensitive moment: Leicester relegated to League One (Apr 2026) and reportedly put up for sale (Aug 2026) — avoid in outreach. Only customer-service emails are published by King Power/LCFC; no press contact for him found. Energy-focus tag in input looks weak (duty-free retail).

name: Xu Shijun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Haili Wind Power Equipment Technology Co., Ltd. (海力风电, SZ:301155)
profile: Xu Shijun (b. 1963) controls Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, a Nantong-based maker of wind-turbine towers, monopiles and other offshore foundation structures, which listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2021. A trained mechanical engineer and senior economist, he joined Haili in 2009 and has chaired it since. He shares the Hurun listing with Xu Chengchen, a fellow director.
interesting_fact: Haili builds the giant steel towers and pile foundations that hold up China's offshore wind turbines. That made Xu one of the few billionaires whose fortune comes directly from the build-out of offshore wind in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
deep_cut_fact: Before wind power he worked his way up at the Rudong County Cotton Machinery Factory (如东县棉机厂) in Jiangsu, first as head of supply and sales and then as factory director. He also still chairs Longteng Machinery (龙腾机械).
notes: 'Haili' here is Jiangsu Haili Wind Power, not the unrelated NEEQ-listed Zhejiang Haili (835787). Xu is low-profile and the IR inbox is the only published route. The listed sector 'Energy' fits: offshore wind supply chain.

name: Mehmet Rustu Basaran
current_role: Chairman, HABAŞ Group (Habaş Sınai ve Tıbbi Gazlar İstihsal Endüstrisi); chairman and part-owner of Anadolubank
profile: Turkish industrialist (b. ~1946/47) who heads Habaş, founded by his father Hamdi Başaran in 1956 in Istanbul as the Topkapı oxygen plant. Habaş grew from industrial/medical gases into one of Turkey's largest steel producers, with LPG/LNG/CNG distribution, storage, shipping and port operations; he also controls Anadolubank.
interesting_fact: Per Forbes, he is a serious car collector whose collection has included a Ferrari 288 GTO, Ferrari F40, McLaren F1, Porsche Carrera GT and Hennessey Venom GT.
notes: HIGHLY SENSITIVE / timing: on 10 Nov 2026 he was reported detained in Istanbul in the probe into a deadly explosion at Habaş's Aliağa (İzmir) steel plant (reported 18 dead). Source: https://www.timeturk.com/habas-patronu-mehmet-rustu-basaran-kartalda-gozaltina-alindi. Forbes says he seldom appears in public and doesn't talk to press. Outreach not advisable now.

name: Yao Lisheng
current_role: Non-independent director and major shareholder, Maxscend Microelectronics (卓胜微, SZSE: 300782), Wuxi
profile: Yao Lisheng (姚立生) is a co-founding shareholder and long-time board member (since 2017) of Maxscend Microelectronics, a Wuxi-based fabless maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, modules) for smartphones that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in June 2019. His fortune tracks his Maxscend stake; he dropped off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2022 as the shares fell.
interesting_fact: Maxscend's predecessor was set up in August 2012 with RMB10m registered capital by just three backers: CEO Xu Zhihan, Yao Lisheng and Tianjin Xundu.
deep_cut_fact: He studied as an undergraduate at Tsinghua University and did graduate work at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
notes: Very low public profile; not an executive (chairman/CEO is Xu Zhihan). Education detail comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify against Maxscend's annual report director bios. Route via company general/IR inbox.

name: Ghan Djoe Hiang
current_role: Family shareholder, Baramulti Group (Indonesian coal; listed arm PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk, IDX: BSSR)
profile: Jakarta-based widow, about 86, of Athanasius Tossin Suharya (d. 2020), who started the Baramulti group in 1971 as general contractor PT Ensicon Indonesia and moved into coal trading in 1988. Her wealth comes from the family's coal holdings; the group owns 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra. Forbes listed her as a billionaire only in 2023.
interesting_fact: Baramulti grew from a 1971 construction contractor into the owner of 11 coal concessions in Kalimantan and Sumatra; its listed unit BSSR mines near Samarinda, East Kalimantan.
notes: Extremely private: no interviews or public role found. The group's site lists only phone numbers, no email. She dropped off Forbes' list after 2023, and no recent news was found to confirm she is alive (Forbes gave her age as 83 in 2023). Family members such as Daniel Suharya appear on the BSSR board; the company is a better route than her personally.

name: Dai Wenyuan
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, 4Paradigm (Beijing Fourth Paradigm Technology, HKEX-listed)
profile: AI researcher-turned-founder who started 4Paradigm in 2014 after serving as chief architect of Baidu's Phoenix Nest ad system and principal scientist at Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab. 4Paradigm sells enterprise machine-learning/AI platforms and is HK-listed; he holds degrees from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and HKUST.
interesting_fact: He is a former ACM-ICPC (international collegiate programming contest) world champion, per 4Paradigm's leadership page, and was named to MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 (China) and Fortune's 40 Under 40.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of 'Boosting for Transfer Learning' (ICML 2007, with Qiang Yang, Gui-Rong Xue, Yong Yu), which introduced TrAdaBoost, the first boosting-based transfer-learning algorithm and a widely cited classic in the field.
notes: Data-center/AI angle: 4Paradigm builds enterprise AI platforms and compute solutions. Best route is 4Paradigm PR (pr_co@4paradigm.com).

name: Bryan Sheffield
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Formentera Partners (Austin, TX)
profile: Son of Pioneer Natural Resources CEO Scott Sheffield. current_role: Private investor; early backer and former director of Veeva Systems (2007-2015); co-founder/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020) per aggregator listings
profile: A veteran of enterprise sales in pharma software, Armenante worked at Information Resources Inc. and Oracle, ran PharmaSystems, and spent over ten years as a Siebel Systems group VP. In 2007 he became one of Veeva's first outside backers and directors. He held about 13% of Veeva before its 2013 IPO, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Veeva's 2013 S-1 shows he owned 14.8 million shares (13.2%) before the IPO, nearly as many as CEO Peter Gassner's 15.2 million. That made him one of the company's largest individual holders.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Veeva, he was President of PharmaSystems, Inc., a pharmaceutical sales-force management company, from 1991 to 1994. That is essentially the market Veeva later dominated. He also holds a biology degree from Case Western Reserve University.
notes: He was about 74 in 2026 (61 at the S-1 in 2013), and I found no recent public activity or confirmation that he is alive. He has no public social or website presence, and some aggregator claims (e.g., 'founder' of Veeva) are imprecise. He was a Series A investor and director rather than an operating co-founder.

name: Ray Irani
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Occidental Petroleum (1990-2011); reported as chairman/CEO of private investment firm Ray Investment, LLC
profile: Lebanese-born chemist (b. 1935) who worked at Monsanto and was president/COO of Olin before Armand Hammer brought him to Occidental in 1983; Hammer named him heir in 1990 and he led Oxy for two decades, growing it into a major US oil producer. He stepped down as CEO in 2011 and as chairman in 2013 and has since kept a low profile.
interesting_fact: Armand Hammer, then 91, picked Irani as his successor at Occidental in February 1990; by 1988 Irani's team was already running day-to-day operations for the nonagenarian founder.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry BS from the American University of Beirut in 1953, moved to Los Angeles at 18 and had a USC physical-chemistry PhD by 1957; USC named its life sciences building Ray R. Irani Hall in 2007, and he was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2012 for work on particulate systems.
notes: Aged ~91; no death reported in searches as of Nov 2026 (Wikipedia lists him as living) - verify before outreach. No published personal or office contact found. Possible routes: AUB trustees emeriti page (https://www.aub.edu.lb/AboutUs/bot/emeriti/Pages/irani.aspx) or USC. Avoid executive-pay and tax-shelter controversies.

name: Cao Jianwei
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical (SZSE: 300316); co-actual controller with founder Qiu Minxiu
profile: Cao Jianwei (曹建伟, b. 1978), an engineering PhD, has run Jingsheng since its early years (GM from 2010, chairman since 2016). Founded in 2006 by Zhejiang University professor Qiu Minxiu, it makes crystal-growth furnaces for solar and semiconductor silicon plus sapphire and SiC substrates; listed in Shenzhen in 2012.

deep_cut_fact: A researcher in hydraulic transmission and electromechanical control, he has won two first-class Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology awards, and was named one of Shaoxing's Top Ten Outstanding Young People and a recipient of the Chinese Red Cross Humanitarian Service Medal.
notes: Engineer-chairman; few English-language interviews. Data-center/AI angle via semiconductor equipment and SiC substrates (power electronics). Route via company securities office.

name: Kiki Barki
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, PT Harum Energy Tbk (IDX: HRUM); owner of private coal miner Tanito Harum
profile: Indonesian coal pioneer Kiki Barki (Ji Qihui) founded Tanito Harum in 1988 and Harum Energy in 1995, listing Harum in 2010. His sons now run Harum, which has diversified from Kalimantan thermal coal into nickel, including a stake in ASX-listed Nickel Industries with nickel pig-iron plants in Indonesia.
interesting_fact: Then-mining minister Ginandjar Kartasasmita recalled that Barki spoke Mandarin better than Indonesian, having lived and studied in China for more than 10 years before returning to set up Tanito Harum, one of the few Indonesian-owned coal miners of the late 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Bandung in 1939 to a Hokchia (Fujian) family, he finished secondary school in Beijing and trained at a mining academy there; before coal he helped run his father's textile, hotel and banking businesses, and in 1993 his interests backed PT Vietmindo Energitama, a coal mine in northern Vietnam.
notes: Aged ~87; alive status based on Forbes' 2026 profile wording, not independently confirmed (web-search budget ran out). Very private; day-to-day leadership is with his sons at Harum. harumenergy.com is behind bot protection, so its IR/corporate secretary contact could not be extracted - check its Investor Relations page manually.

name: Sean Lie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: MIT-trained chip architect and one of Cerebras' five co-founders, who all came from SeaMicro (sold to AMD in 2012). As CTO since 2022 he leads the technology behind the Wafer-Scale Engine, a dinner-plate-sized AI chip, and Cerebras' inference cloud and data centers. Cerebras listed on Nasdaq in May 2026; his roughly 5.3M pre-IPO shares are the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' May 2026 IPO raised $5.55B at $185 a share, the largest U.S. tech IPO since 2019. The stock opened at $350, valuing the wafer-scale chipmaker at about $95B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cerebras, Lie was a microprocessor architect on AMD's advanced architecture team (2004-08). At SeaMicro he was lead hardware architect of the IO-virtualization fabric ASIC that linked hundreds of tiny CPUs in its dense servers, and after AMD bought SeaMicro he was Chief Architect for Data Center Server Solutions.
notes: Core AI/data-center guest. He often gives technical talks (e.g. at Hot Chips) on the WSE architecture. The X and LinkedIn listed are Cerebras corporate accounts, not his. Media route is pr@cerebras.ai; the general inbox is info@cerebras.ai.

name: Lee Man Chun
current_role: Chairman and founder, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd. (HKEX: 2314)
profile: Raymond Lee Man Chun founded and chairs Lee & Man Paper, a Hong Kong-listed maker of containerboard, tissue and pulp with ~10,000 staff and mills in mainland China and Vietnam. A UBC engineering graduate, he is a CPPCC National Committee member, holds the Silver Bauhinia Star and is an INED of Beijing Enterprises Water.
interesting_fact: He was named a Hong Kong Young Industrialist (2002) and one of Hong Kong's Ten Outstanding Young Persons (2003), and is an honorary citizen of both Dongguan and Changshu, where Lee & Man runs major mills.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: he holds a B.A.Sc. (applied science) from the University of British Columbia, which also awarded him an honorary Doctor of Laws in 2014. He chairs the Bai Ren (百仁) Foundation and joined City University of Hong Kong's Council in 2015.

Web search budget ran out while researching this person; bio from 10jqka HK executive profiles.

name: Liu Minghui
current_role: Founder, chairman and president (总裁), China Gas Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0384)
profile: Liu Minghui (Liu Ming Hui, b. June 1963) is the founder and president of China Gas Holdings, one of China's largest cross-regional city-gas distributors, piping natural gas to households and industry in hundreds of Chinese cities and expanding into LPG, integrated energy and renewables. name: Zhang Qin
current_role: Executive Director, Vice Chairman, Deputy General Manager and Board Secretary, SG Micro Corp (300661.SZ / 03661.HK)
profile: Zhang Qin co-founded SG Micro (圣邦微电子), a Beijing analog-chip designer started in January 2007 with chairman Zhang Shilong. It is China's No. 1 domestic analog IC company by revenue and No. 8 globally. Listed in Shenzhen (2017) and Hong Kong (2026), it is part-owned by her: she holds about 8% and belongs to the controlling group.

She has been on SG Micro's board since its first month in January 2007 and has also been board secretary since 2012.

name: Lu Xinchun
current_role: Chief Scientist, Hwatsing Technology (华海清科, SSE STAR: 688120); Chief Researcher, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, Tsinghua University
profile: Tsinghua tribologist (b. 1966, Yantai) whose team began chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) research in 2000 and spun it out in 2013 as Hwatsing, now China's No.1 domestic CMP and wafer-thinning equipment maker, listed on the STAR Market in 2022. He was chairman until 2025 and remains chief scientist guiding R&D.
interesting_fact: His team launched China's first 12-inch CMP tool with domestic IP and an integrated grinding-polishing thinning tool, key equipment for chipmaking and advanced packaging; he won a 2025 Ho Leung Ho Lee Science and Technology Innovation Prize.
deep_cut_fact: An academic first: he earned his bachelor's and master's at Jilin University of Technology (1988, 1991), a PhD at the CAS Institute of Metal Research (1994), and did his postdoc at Tsinghua's State Key Laboratory of Tribology, the field of nano-scale friction behind CMP.
notes: Academic-founder; stepped down as Hwatsing chairman in 2025 (Wang Tongqing is now chairman & GM) but remains chief scientist (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2273649). Routes: Hwatsing board office (secretary Chen Zhenyin) or Tsinghua Mechanical Engineering dept. Likely Chinese-language outreach needed.

name: Le Weiping
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Technology (Hengyunchang, STAR Market: 688785).
profile: Le Weiping (b. 1973) spent ~11 years at US plasma-power maker Advanced Energy in Shenzhen and Shanghai before founding CSL Vacuum (Hengyunchang) to localise plasma RF power systems for chip equipment. Its main customer is Piotech; the company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026. He controls ~73% of voting rights (wealth shared with Cao Li per Hurun).
interesting_fact: He quit a well-paid multinational job in 2013, when China's chip-equipment sector was nascent, and started CSL with five employees in an office under 100 square metres in Shenzhen's Bao'an district.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a technician/engineer at the telecom-equipment factory of the Taoyuan County Post & Telecom Bureau in Hunan; he joined Advanced Energy Shenzhen in 2003 as a test technician and rose to product-applications engineer and senior sales manager in Shanghai.
notes: Recent IPO (Jan 2026); low personal media profile. Board secretary Zhuang Lihua handles IR. Relationship to co-listed Cao Li not confirmed.

name: Cao Li
current_role: Major shareholder (back-office management), Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology (恒运昌, STAR 688785)
profile: Co-owner, with chairman Le Weiping, of Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology, which makes plasma RF power supplies and related core components for semiconductor process equipment. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026, which put the couple on the 2026 Hurun China list. Per IPO disclosures she handles back-office management rather than operations.

name: Green Chang-Lin
current_role: Chairman, MPI Corporation (旺矽科技, TWSE: 6223), Hsinchu, Taiwan
profile: Ko Chang-lin (葛長林; listed by Hurun as 'Green Chang-Lin') started out in semiconductor equipment distribution and built MPI Corporation, now described as the world's fourth-largest probe-card maker. He won the brewpub franchise after a meeting in the US was postponed and he spent the evening tasting 10+ experimental beers with the brewer until midnight; the first Taipei outlet opened in 2008. He says it made him no money but 10+ years of happiness.
notes: Listed with country China (Hurun) but he is Taiwan-based. Strong AI/data-center supply chain angle (probe cards for AI ASIC/GPU testing). Mandarin-language media interviews are common; route via MPI IR.

name: Jones Chen
current_role: Chairman, Genius Electronic Optical Co. (GSEO, TWSE: 3406), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Chen Tien-ching (陳天慶, 'Jones Chen') leads Genius Electronic Optical, a Taiwanese maker of precision plastic lenses for smartphone cameras (a major Apple supplier), founded 1990 and listed 2005. Under him GSEO is expanding into smart-glasses optics, humanoid-robot lenses and data-center optical interconnects / co-packaged optics.

IR contact is a named IR officer published on the company IR page. Deep-cut source (Global Views 2006) could not be fetched directly; verify before use.

name: Wu Zuyu
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology (海辰储能)
profile: Wu Zuyu (吴祖钰), born in the mid-1980s, holds an applied-chemistry BSc from Shandong Normal University and a chemical-engineering MSc from Fuzhou University. He was an engineer at CATL before founding Hithium in Xiamen on 27 Dec 2019. Within about six years Hithium became one of the world's top three makers of stationary storage batteries, passing 100 GWh of shipments, and it is pursuing a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: Hithium went from founding to roughly third in global energy-storage cell shipments in about five years. Hurun valued it at RMB 25bn in 2024, and it now sells 5 MWh containers and 8-hour long-duration storage systems in the US, Australia and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: As a CATL engineer he was first-named inventor on a run of energy-storage patents covering current collectors, electrode sheets and cells. One count puts it at 67 such patents between 2012 and 2018.
notes: Very low public profile; Hithium's prospectus is the main source on him. The press email comes from an older Hithium newsroom release and may be outdated. Avoid the topic of CATL in outreach: there are ongoing non-compete and unfair-competition disputes, which also delayed the HK IPO. The 67-patent count is from 36kr (https://www.36kr.com/p/2541517764011779).

name: Wei Jisheng
current_role: Chairman, Longkou Shengtong Group; major shareholder (27.7%) and long-time director of Senton Energy / Shengtong Energy (SZSE: 001331)
profile: Wei Jisheng (b. 1963) built a trucking business in Longkou, Shandong into Senton (Shengtong) Energy, an LNG trading and tank-truck logistics firm ranked 5th in China for both LNG trading and LNG transport in 2025, listed in Shenzhen. In 2026 his family sold control (~45% incl. tender offer) to Qiteng Robotics; he still held 27.73% at mid-2026.

name: Jacob DeWitte
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO)
profile: Nuclear engineer (Univ. of Florida BS 2008; MIT SM/PhD) who worked at Sandia, Urenco USA, the Naval Nuclear Laboratory and GE (core design lead on the PRISM sodium fast reactor) before co-founding Oklo in 2013 with Caroline Cochran (COO). Oklo, developing small advanced fission 'powerhouses' aimed partly at data centers, listed in 2024 via a Sam Altman-backed SPAC.
interesting_fact: Oklo is named after the uranium deposits at Oklo, Gabon, where natural self-sustaining fission reactions occurred about two billion years ago; DeWitte also raised the first modern institutional VC-led financing of a fission company.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Albuquerque, he spent weekends with his dad getting donuts and visiting the National Nuclear Science Museum; his favourite exhibit was a simulated fuel pellet the size of a pencil eraser holding the energy of a ton of coal. He later talked his family into detouring to Arizona's nuclear plant on a Grand Canyon trip.
notes: Highly relevant (nuclear for data centers). Frequent conference speaker (CERAWeek etc.) and congressional witness; 2014 Forbes 30 Under 30 (Energy). Oklo's site lists investors@oklo.com as its single media/investor contact; company X is @oklo. UF 2021 Distinguished Early Career Alumni Award: https://mse.ufl.edu/jacob-dewitte-2021-distinguished-early-career-alumni-award/

name: Caroline Cochran
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Operating Officer and Director, Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO)
profile: Co-founded advanced-fission company Oklo in 2013 with her husband, CEO Jacob DeWitte; she now also goes by Caroline DeWitte. Oklo went public in 2024 through a SPAC backed by Sam Altman. It is building 75 MW 'Aurora' fast-reactor powerhouses, the first in Idaho, aimed at AI data centers, including a 1.2 GW agreement with Meta in Ohio.
interesting_fact: Oklo is named after the Oklo uranium deposits in Gabon, where natural nuclear fission reactions ran on their own about two billion years ago.
deep_cut_fact: She started out as a climate-concerned nuclear skeptic. She holds a BA in economics and a BS in mechanical engineering from the University of Oklahoma, where she later helped set up a technology-commercialization program, and she is one of the youngest recipients of OU's Regents' Alumni Award.
notes: A strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast, and she does podcasts (Business for Good, 2026). She is a former member of DOE's Nuclear Energy Advisory Committee. Use the Cochran/DeWitte name variants. Oklo's head of communications is listed as the media@oklo.com contact.

name: Steve Ells
current_role: Founder and COO, Counter Service (NYC fast-casual sandwich chain, formerly Kernel); founder of Chipotle
profile: Founded Chipotle in Denver in 1993 at age 26 and ran it as CEO/co-CEO until 2017-18, building the 'food with integrity' fast-casual model; left Chipotle's board in 2020. His next venture, Kernel, began as a robot-assisted vegan concept and has been reworked into Counter Service, a five-unit NYC sandwich brand (2026) run with Peloton co-founder Tom Cortese as CEO and preparing to expand beyond New York.
interesting_fact: He describes Kernel's pivot with self-deprecation: of the original vegan, robotics-heavy menu, 'I thought the food was delicious... And so did a few of my customers.' Cortese admits he first thought Ells was 'absolutely bonkers'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Chipotle he earned an art history degree at CU Boulder, graduated from the Culinary Institute of America (1990) and spent two years as a sous chef under Jeremiah Tower at Stars in San Francisco; the first Chipotle opened near the University of Denver campus.
notes: Listed as former Forbes billionaire (~$0.97B). Energy/data-center angle is weak; best angle is automation/robotics in restaurants and founder reinvention. Speaks at industry events (NRN CREATE 2026).

name: Gunkul Dhumrongpiyawut
current_role: Chairman of the Board (non-executive), Gunkul Engineering PCL (SET: GUNKUL), Bangkok
profile: Founded Gunkul Engineering in 1982 as a trader importing electrical equipment for Thai government agencies, opened its own factory in 1992 to replace imports, then pivoted to renewables in 2007. Gunkul now runs solar and wind projects in Thailand, Malaysia, Japan and Vietnam. His wife Sopacha leads management as executive committee chair; daughter Naruechon is COO.
interesting_fact: Gunkul transformed from an electrical-equipment importer (1982) to a domestic manufacturer (1992) to one of Thailand's renewable-energy producers (from 2007), with solar projects across four Asian countries.

name: Jeffrey Henley
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation; Chair, Institute for Energy Efficiency, UC Santa Barbara
profile: Finance executive who joined Oracle as CFO in 1991 to lead its turnaround, served as CFO until 2004, chairman 2004-2014, and has been vice chair since 2014 (Oracle's site now says executive vice chair). His wealth comes from decades of Oracle stock. Earlier he was CFO of Saga Corp. (food service) and Pacific Holding Co., after finance roles at Memorex and Fairchild.
interesting_fact: He and wife Judy pledged $50m to UC Santa Barbara in 2012 to support its Institute for Energy Efficiency and College of Engineering - and he chairs that institute today, a natural hook for an energy/data-center conversation.
deep_cut_fact: Oracle recruited him in 1991 for his reputation as a turnaround CFO; he calls Oracle 'the biggest turnaround, financially, of anything I'd done before.' At UCSB ('66) he cut his teeth as treasurer of the SigEp chapter, and he advises: 'If you think you want to be a CFO, you can't wait until you're 30.'
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. UCSB Institute for Energy Efficiency (iee.ucsb.edu) is an alternative, warmer route given his chair role there. Forbes lists him as 'former' billionaire (~$965m).

name: Gang Chen
current_role: Chairman and founder, Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy (SSE: 600732)
profile: Chen Gang (陈刚) founded Aiko Solar in 2009 after 20 years in aluminium manufacturing. Aiko became a top PERC cell maker after a 2017 breakthrough and an IDG-backed expansion, listed via a 2019 backdoor deal, and now pushes ABC back-contact cells and modules from plants in Foshan, Yiwu and Tianjin. He holds roughly 15% of the company.

deep_cut_fact: A Ganzhou, Jiangxi native, he graduated in 1991 from the Southern Institute of Metallurgy (now Jiangxi University of Science and Technology), moonlighted as a 'Sunday engineer' at a Foshan state firm, cofounded the Aoumei aluminium JV, then switched to solar at 40. His motto on risky R&D: 'If even the worst outcome isn't bad, you dare to do it.'
notes: marketing@aikosolar.com is the general marketing inbox (listed for Thailand/Germany offices), not a dedicated press desk. Chinese-language outreach advised. Has given interviews to People's Daily's China Energy News (2024).

name: Cai Hao
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Arctech Solar Holding Co. (中信博, SSE STAR: 688408), Kunshan
profile: Cai Hao founded Arctech Solar in Kunshan in 2009 and built it into one of the world's top suppliers of single-axis solar trackers, fixed racking and BIPV systems. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and has 110+ GW installed globally. In 2026 he broke ground on a RMB 2bn+ 'global zero-carbon HQ' in Kunshan and is expanding into tracker-plus-storage microgrids.

The profile describes his management style as blending Western business methods with traditional Chinese philosophy.

name: George Sakellaris
current_role: Founder, Chairman, President and CEO, Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC), Framingham, MA
profile: Greek-born engineer George Sakellaris started at utility New England Electric System, ran energy-services firm Noresco (1989-2000), then founded Ameresco in 2000 and took it public in 2010. Ameresco develops energy-efficiency retrofits, renewable-gas, solar and battery-storage projects for governments, utilities and corporates, and he still runs it as CEO.

name: Jeffrey W Clarke
current_role: Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer, Dell Technologies

name: Bahram Akradi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Life Time Group Holdings (NYSE: LTH); Director, Northern Oil and Gas (NOG)
profile: Tehran-born entrepreneur who came to Colorado at 17, began selling memberships at a Nautilus gym, co-led U.S. Swim & Fitness in Minneapolis (1984-89), then founded Life Time in 1992. Life Time runs 180+ 'athletic country club' destinations plus events like Leadville 100 and Unbound Gravel, and returned to the NYSE in 2021. He also sits on the board of oil producer Northern Oil and Gas.
interesting_fact: He has built Life Time into a 'healthy way of life' company spanning clubs, MIORA longevity clinics, LT Work coworking and endurance events, and writes personal essays for the company's Experience Life magazine.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he wanted to fly for the Iranian air force like his brother Davood, so he majored in electrical engineering at UC Colorado Springs as a route to aerospace. He cooked nights as 'Chef Akradi', outsold the local Nautilus gym's top salesman within 3 months, and drove a U-Haul to Minneapolis in March 1983.
notes: Strong podcast fit (founder story, immigrant entrepreneur), and the NOG directorship gives an energy angle. Writes first-person pieces in Experience Life magazine. Best route is Life Time public relations.

name: Yang Jianliang
current_role: Chairman, Hoyuan Green Energy Co. (formerly Wuxi Shangji Automation; SSE: 603185), Wuxi
profile: Yang Jianliang (b. 1969) co-founded Wuxi Shangji Grinding Machine Co. with his wife Hang Hong in 2002; from 2004 it made grinding and slicing machines for solar, listed in Shanghai in 2018, then expanded into wafers, polysilicon, cells and modules with big bases in Baotou. He was chairman and GM until 2022 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 Hoyuan (HY Solar) said it produced 40-micron 'engineering-ready' ultra-thin silicon wafers at its Baotou plant using slicing equipment it designed in-house - a nod to its machine-tool roots.
deep_cut_fact: His company began life as a grinding-machine maker and, by its own account, entered PV equipment in 2004 as one of China's earliest dedicated solar-equipment manufacturers. He is a senior economist, a Jiangsu CPPCC member and vice-chair of the Wuxi Energy Industry Association.
notes: IR email is the company securities department (board secretary Zhuang Kejie). Son Yang Hao (b. 1992) has been general manager since 2022 and is a more public, younger face of the company. Solar sector downturn hit results in 2024; keep outreach upbeat.

name: Xue Guanglin
current_role: Founder of Brightoil Petroleum (HKEX: 933); no longer chairman/CEO since 2019 (later named strategic adviser)
profile: Anhui-born Xue Guanglin (Cantonese: Sit Kwong Lam) founded Brightoil in the 1990s and built one of China's largest private oil groups, spanning oil trading and marine bunkering, an oil-tanker fleet, storage terminals in Shenzhen, Zhoushan and Dalian, Xinjiang gas fields and Bohai Bay offshore oil interests. He ranked in Forbes China's top 60 rich list in 2012-2015 and served on the national CPPCC from 2003.
interesting_fact: At its peak Brightoil had about 12 million cubic metres of oil storage capacity and a 3-million-DWT ocean tanker fleet, unusual scale for a private Chinese energy company.
deep_cut_fact: In his chairman's message on Brightoil's website he wrote: 'More than 20 years ago, I had a dream: to build a privately owned Chinese global energy company.' He served as a member of the 10th through 13th CPPCC National Committees.
notes: Not recommended as a guest: Hong Kong High Court declared him bankrupt in April 2019 over ~US$1.4B in personal guarantees for Brightoil debts; he lost his chairman/CEO roles. His listed fortune is out of date. Current status and activities unclear. No published contact found.

name: Wang Yihui
current_role: Chairwoman and General Manager, Zhuhai Jieli Technology (杰理科技, BSE: 920138)
profile: Wang Yihui (b. Oct 1970) founded Zhuhai Jieli Technology in 2010 after seven years as vice-president of Zhuhai chip firm Jianrong; Jieli designs low-cost Bluetooth audio, wearable and IoT SoCs used widely in earbuds and smart devices. She is one of four co-controllers (80%+ of votes); after several earlier attempts, Jieli listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange on 12 Aug 2026, opening up 191% at a RMB 23.8bn market cap.
interesting_fact: Jieli finally went public on its fourth IPO attempt: its Beijing Stock Exchange debut on 12 August 2026 opened 191% higher, valuing the company at about RMB 23.8 billion; Xiaomi is also a shareholder (~2.7%).
deep_cut_fact: She did not start in tech: her first job (1994-97) was as a staff member at Zhuhai Hengtong Shipping Group, followed by six years as head of administration at Zhuhai Xike Network Technology before she moved into chips in 2003.
notes: Wang Yihui is female (filings say 王艺辉女士). Very low media profile. Avoid the 2012-17 trade-secret litigation with former employer Jianrong (withdrawn). Board secretary Hu Xiangjun is the formal IR route; info@ is the company email listed in filings.

name: Yan Hongjia
current_role: Chairman/head of Mingguan New Material (明冠新材, SH:688560); co-founder and controlling figure of Yunnan Yuze New Energy (formerly Yuze Semiconductor), an N-type silicon wafer maker
profile: Yan Hongjia was born in 1980 in Xinzhou, Shanxi. With his brother Yan Yong he founded Mingguan New Material in 2007; it makes solar backsheets and lithium-battery aluminium-plastic film and listed on the STAR Market in 2020. In 2019 the brothers founded Yuze Semiconductor in Chuxiong, Yunnan. It makes N-type wafers for HJT, TOPCon and IBC cells, has raised more than RMB 2B and filed for IPO tutoring in 2024 as Yuze New Energy.
interesting_fact: Yuze kept a low profile until June 2022, when Tongwei disclosed polysilicon supply contracts with it worth about RMB 38.5B. Yuze is one of a cluster of solar plants that turned Chuxiong in Yunnan into an unlikely new-energy hub.
deep_cut_fact: After high school he skipped university to ease his family's finances and went south to work. In 2003 he and his brother set up Yuntian Electronics in Kunshan, Jiangsu, and made their first money selling computer consumables. In 2006 he moved into new energy in Jiangxi.

public_contacts.value: ir@mg-crown.com (Mingguan New Material board secretary's office)

notes: The 'Yuze' in the dataset is Yuze Semiconductor / Yunnan Yuze New Energy (Chuxiong). The more reliable route is via listed Mingguan (Yichun, Jiangxi), where he is the legal head. He co-controls both companies with his brother Yan Yong. Low profile.

name: Guo Chunxuan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Xinxiang Richful Lube Additive Co. (瑞丰新材, SZSE: 300910)
profile: Guo Chunxuan (郭春萱, b. 1964) built Richful in Xinxiang, Henan, into China's leading domestic maker of lubricant additives (plus carbonless-paper developer), exporting to North America, Europe and emerging markets. He has chaired the business since 1996 and listed it in Shenzhen in 2020; Richful competes with global additive majors (Lubrizol, Infineum, etc.).
interesting_fact: Richful is regarded as China's leading domestic lubricant-additive maker; in Sept 2026 it launched RF60300, an additive package to help oil blenders meet the new API CL-4/FB-4 performance categories.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a workshop director at Hubei's Echeng Iron & Steel Works (1985-87), then was a technician at the Xinxiang Chemical Research Institute, and is a named inventor on patents for zinc dialkyl dithiophosphate (ZDDP) and dithiocarbamate preparation methods. He also chairs the additives committee of the Shanghai lubricant industry association.
notes: Low profile, technical founder. Best route: securities affairs office (zqb@richful.com, published in a July 2024 board announcement).

name: Xu Ligang
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder, Director & General Manager, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext: 301707), Nanjing
profile: Xu Ligang (徐立刚, mid-40s) holds a PhD in power electronics from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and co-founded Nanjing-based X-chip in 2018 with fellow NUAA alumnus Wen Zhenlin. X-chip designs high-reliability analog power-management chips and DC/DC micro-modules; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026 and surged ~360% on debut.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO priced at 23.45 yuan and opened 360% higher on day one (peaking near 129.90 yuan), making Xu and co-founder Wen Zhenlin newly minted chip billionaires in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he worked as an engineer at Shenzhen Qingxuan Electronics and at Silergy's Hangzhou arm, then ran the Zhuzhou Zhanxin business unit; X-chip's leadership and independent directors are largely fellow NUAA power-electronics alumni.
notes: Hurun 'X-Chip' = 江苏展芯半导体 (Zhanxin). Chairman is co-founder Wen Zhenlin; Xu is GM. Company focuses on military/high-reliability power chips, so expect low media appetite. Route via IR email.

name: Ou Xinhua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Prisemi Electronics (芯导科技, STAR Market: 688230)
profile: Engineer-founder who set up Shanghai Prisemi in Nov 2009, a fabless designer of power semiconductors (TVS/ESD protection devices, MOSFETs, Schottky diodes, power-management ICs) for consumer electronics, with Xiaomi among its major customers. He controlled 100% of the company before its 2021 STAR Market listing and was re-elected chairman in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Prisemi was his first startup, and he kept 100% control of it right up to its STAR Market IPO filing, with no outside VC shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Prisemi he was an R&D engineer and project manager at Shanghai Guangyu Ruixin Microelectronics and then technical director at Suzhou Jingxun Technology.
notes: Low public profile with no interviews found. Prisemi does power and protection chips, mainly for phones and consumer devices, so the data-center link is indirect.

name: Li Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, 51WORLD (Beijing 51World Digital Twin Technology; HKEX-listed)
profile: Li Yi (Archer Li) founded 51WORLD in Beijing in 2015, evolving it from a VR startup into a digital-twin and simulation platform used for autonomous-driving testing, transport hubs, smart factories, water management and energy. Backed by Sky9 Capital from its Series A, 51WORLD listed on the HKEX main board; he now pitches it as a data engine for embodied AI and robotics.
interesting_fact: His stated goal is to build a 'Digital Twin Earth' - a complete virtual replica of the world - by 2030; 51WORLD's simulation platform serves nearly a hundred intelligent-driving customers.
deep_cut_fact: On investor Sky9 Capital's founder page he lists as his favorite quote: 'Pessimists are always right but optimists are more likely to succeed.'
notes: Goes by 'Archer Li' in English. aes@51aes.com is 51WORLD's published customer-service email (no dedicated press address found). Data-center/energy angle: digital twins for energy sites and factories; recent focus on robotics training data.

name: Ao Fengting
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inner Mongolia Mengtai Group (coal, power, aluminium; Ordos)
profile: Inner Mongolia energy entrepreneur who founded Mengtai Group (formerly Ordos Mengtai Coal & Power), an integrated coal-mining, power-generation and aluminium producer in Ordos. Hurun has listed him every year since 2010; in 2024 he ranked 9th in Inner Mongolia with RMB 5.3bn. He reportedly also serves as a vice-president of the China Ethnic Trade Promotion Association.
interesting_fact: Mengtai follows the classic Inner Mongolia 'coal-power-aluminium' integration model, using its own mine-mouth coal power to run energy-intensive aluminium smelting.
notes: Very low profile with minimal public information; the biography above comes from a Hurun-derived list (maigoo.com/news/725273.html). I could not reach a company website or published contact. Identity is matched by name and company only.

name: Liang Meizhen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (acting in concert with Yu Zhong and Zuo Guojun) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
profile: One of three actual controllers of S.C New Energy, a Shenzhen solar-equipment maker founded in 2003 that builds PECVD, diffusion, texturing/etching and automation tools for crystalline-silicon PV cell lines; it listed on ChiNext in 2018. She directly holds about 7% and controls about 11% of voting rights (incl. shares held by her son), per 2025 filings. No executive role found.
interesting_fact: 'SC' in the Hurun listing is S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创), one of China's main suppliers of solar-cell manufacturing equipment, whose PECVD tools deposit anti-reflective and passivation layers on PV cells.
notes: Identity inferred from Hurun 'SC' + green energy and confirmed by S.C New Energy filings naming 梁美珍 as co-actual controller. Appears to be a passive shareholder with no public profile; better interview targets are chairman Zuo Guojun or CEO Yu Zhong.

name: Hu Xinrong
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and core technical staff, Shenzhen Xinyichang Technology (Hoson, SSE STAR: 688383)
profile: Shenzhen engineer who co-founded Xinyichang with Song Changning in 2006; the two are its controlling shareholders. Starting with capacitor aging-test machines, the company became a leading Chinese maker of LED (incl. Mini LED) die bonders and expanded into semiconductor die-attach and lithium-battery equipment. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Xinyichang began in 2006 making aluminium electrolytic capacitor aging-test machines, then used that know-how to break into LED die bonders, and later developed six-head high-speed die bonders for Mini LED and chip-packaging die bonders for semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: He worked his way up from the shop floor: a technician at Shenzhen Huachang Electronics, then technician and equipment supervisor at Shenzhen Datong, before running two small Bao'an workshops (Hengchang machining plant and Yichang electronics factory) that preceded Xinyichang.
notes: Hurun's 'Xinyichang' = 新益昌 (Hoson). Low media profile; route via board secretary Liu Xiaohuan's office (hoson@szhech.com, listed in 2024 interim report). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Pua Khein Seng
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Phison Electronics Corp. (Hsinchu, Taiwan; NAND flash controllers/SSDs); founder of Malaysian IC-design arm MaiStorage
profile: Malaysian engineer (b. 1974, Sekinchan, Selangor) who studied electrical and control engineering at National Chiao Tung University and in 2000, aged 27, co-founded Phison with four schoolmates. Phison is credited with the first single-chip USB flash drive controller and now supplies NAND controllers and enterprise SSDs, including aiDAPTIV+, which uses flash to extend GPU memory for AI. He stepped back as chairman but remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He is widely known in Malaysia as the 'father of the pen drive' for Phison's single-chip USB flash drive, and was made a Dato' by Penang in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: A farming-town boy from Sekinchan, Selangor, he attended Pin Hwa High School in Klang before going to Taiwan for university. He founded Phison in 2000 at 27, and in 2024 the KL20 Summit celebrated his 'homecoming' as he set up MaiStorage to train Malaysian chip designers.
notes: Hurun lists him under China, but he is a Malaysian citizen based in Taiwan. Strong data-centre/AI-storage angle (NAND shortage, aiDAPTIV+). Phison sites block automated fetches; the press email comes from 2026 Business Wire releases as indexed by search. Some releases list spokesperson Antonio Yu instead.

name: Wong Howard
current_role: Executive Director, Chairman and CEO, Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction Ltd (9900.HK; formerly Gain Plus Holdings)
profile: Howard Wong (黄晞), about 70, is a Hong Kong businessman who took control of construction subcontractor Gain Plus Holdings via his wholly owned Asia General Industries (~32%) and became chairman and CEO in February 2025. He renamed it Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction in 2025 to reflect a 'technology construction' focus; the share rerating put him on the 2026 Hurun China list.
interesting_fact: After his takeover the company rebranded from Gain Plus Holdings to Hong Kong ZCloud Technology Construction (ticker 'ZCLOUD TECH CON' from 26 May 2025) and split each share into eight in August 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier career was in retail and trading: from 2000 to 2015 he was an executive director of Chaifa Holdings (stock code 139), whose businesses at times spanned garments, shoes, car audio equipment and early internet ventures.
notes: Very little public profile; no interviews, website contacts or social accounts found. Listed-company announcements on HKEXnews (stock 9900) are the main public record. Company's core business is still HK building subcontracting/RMAA; data-center link is not documented in sources found.

name: Wang Xingchun
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Winsway Coking Coal (now E-Commodities Holdings, HKEX 1733); no current board seat found
profile: Wang Xingchun (王兴春) built Winsway into the largest importer of Mongolian coking coal into China, with its own cross-border logistics, and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010 as chairman and CEO (it also had a Mongolian JV with Peabody). The company was renamed E-Commodities Holdings; filings since 2023 show others chairing the board.
interesting_fact: Before coal, he spent 15+ years building cross-border logistics: in 1995 he invested in and became vice chairman of Manzhouli Haitie Yonghui, which runs oil and petrochemical transshipment facilities at the Manzhouli railway port on the Russian border.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1990 as an agent for Hong Kong Management Service (Chemicals), part of the Landmark Chemicals trading group; he had earned a diploma in mechanical manufacturing from Beijing Open University (1984-87), per Winsway's IPO prospectus.
notes: Low profile; last on Hurun China list in 2021. No longer a director of the listed company; no published personal or press contacts found. Hurun calls the source 'Winsway Coking Coal'.

name: Chen Jinyue
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Ningbo Baosi Energy Equipment (Shenzhen: 300441)
profile: Born 1964 in Fenghua, Zhejiang, Chen ran small local alloy-materials and machinery workshops before founding Baosi in 2005. Baosi makes screw-compressor parts, compressors, vacuum pumps and hydraulic pumps and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2015; he controls roughly 40% of the company.
interesting_fact: Baosi is headquartered in Fenghua, Ningbo, which the company itself promotes as Chiang Kai-shek's ancestral home and a Maitreya Buddhist holy site, and it builds its corporate culture around Maitreya ideals of openness and harmony.
deep_cut_fact: Before Baosi he ran two small Fenghua workshops, the Fenghua Daqiao Chengli alloy-materials factory and Fenghua Jingda machinery factory; he also serves as a director of China's compressor industry association and a Fenghua district people's congress deputy.
notes: The IR email is the company's published securities-affairs contact (board secretary Xu Bin), not Chen personally. Very low international profile; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

The firm sells ERP, marketing and asset-management software to property developers and city operators (7,000+ clients) and now markets AI tools incl. its 'Qiming' large model.

name: Zhou Zhixu
current_role: Chairman (and core technical staff), 3PEAK Inc. / Sipu Microelectronics Technology (Suzhou), STAR Market 688536
profile: Zhou Zhixu (ZHIXU ZHOU, 周之栩), b. 1968 and a U.S. citizen, is an analog-chip engineer who co-founded Suzhou-based 3PEAK in 2008 after 13 years at Motorola/Freescale. 3PEAK designs signal-chain and power-management analog and mixed-signal ICs, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020, and has no controlling shareholder. He moved from general manager to chairman and holds ~9.46M shares.
interesting_fact: 3PEAK reports no controlling shareholder and no actual controller, which is unusual for a Chinese chip company; its founders and engineers each hold minority stakes.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BS, MS and PhD in electrical engineering all at Arizona State University. At Motorola/Freescale (1994-2007) he went from device and process R&D engineer to principal analog design engineer and senior member of the company's Science & Technology Advisory Board.
notes: Technical founder with a low media profile; English-speaking (U.S.-trained, U.S. citizen), which makes outreach easier. business@3peak.com is the company's general business inbox, not a press desk; the board secretary's office (Li Shuhuan) handles investor and media matters. Analog/power ICs are relevant to server power delivery.

profile: Leading figure in the Jiangyin-based Fasten group, historically a major Chinese maker of steel wire/steel cord and optical fiber/cable. current_role: Shareholder of Allwinner Technology (全志科技, SZSE ChiNext: 300458), per Hurun; title/role not confirmed
