name: Ji Xinhua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, UCloud Technology (优刻得, 688158.SH)
profile: Ji Xinhua (b. 1979), a noted Chinese white-hat hacker, ran security at Huawei, Tencent and Shanda before founding UCloud in 2012. UCloud's 2020 STAR Market IPO was China's first public-cloud listing and first dual-class A-share. He is now steering it toward AI compute and overseas expansion.
interesting_fact: In June 2026 UCloud opened an availability zone in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, its 36th worldwide across 28 regions. Ji's stated rule: 'we will build in every country with more than 30 million people,' as part of a 'Digital Silk Road' strategy.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, 'Ala Shanghai' (阿拉上海), launched in 1998 while he was an electrical-automation student at Tongji University. It was a local-life site that predated Dianping by years and failed for being too early. In 2012 he sold an apartment in Shenzhen to fund UCloud after more than 100 investors turned him down.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly: he gives frequent interviews to Chinese financial press. Strong fit for a data-center/AI-compute episode (UCloud runs large intelligent-computing centres, e.g. in Ulanqab). He was early in his career as Tencent Security Center deputy GM.

name: Li Shijun
current_role: Top-10 shareholder and long-time director/general manager (from 2011 per research reports) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, SZSE: 300724); current title not confirmed
profile: Li Shijun (李时俊) is an early partner in S.C New Energy, China's leading maker of solar-cell manufacturing equipment (wet benches, diffusion furnaces, PECVD, etching). He joined around 2008-2010 bringing a semiconductor-equipment team that moved the firm into dry-process tools; it listed in Shenzhen in 2018 and he remains a top-10 shareholder (2026).
interesting_fact: S.C rode the solar industry's shift from BSF to PERC cells to become China's top PV-cell equipment supplier, holding 196 patents by 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 22 years (1985-2007) at the Electronics Ministry's 48th Research Institute, a pioneer of Chinese semiconductor and PV equipment, rising from head of its Ion Beam Technology Lab to assistant director before joining S.C.
notes: 'S.C' = Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创); despite the 'semiconductor equipment' tag, its core business is solar PV cell equipment. Controllers are Liang Meizhen, Zuo Guojun and Yu Zhong; Li is a significant shareholder. Very low public profile; route via company board office.

name: Li Xiaodan
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and co-actual controller (with chairman Xing Meizheng) of Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics (SZSE ChiNext: 300303).
profile: Li Xiaodan is one of two actual controllers of Jufei Optoelectronics, a Shenzhen SMD LED packager (founded 2005) supplying phones, PCs, TVs, displays, auto electronics, sensing and optical comms. She holds ~3.05% and acts in concert with chairman Xing Meizheng (together ~10.8%), renewing their agreement on 27 Oct 2026.

notes: No personal biography published; she holds no disclosed executive post. Relationship to Xing Meizheng not stated in filings. Only route is Jufei securities/board office email.

name: Xing Meizheng
current_role: Chairman (company head) and co-controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics (聚飞光电, SZSE 300303)
profile: Co-controlling shareholder (with Li Xiaodan) and head of Shenzhen Jufei Optoelectronics, founded in 2005 and listed on ChiNext in March 2012. Jufei is one of China's leading makers of LED backlight components for phones, TVs and displays, and has expanded into lighting, automotive and optical-device products.
interesting_fact: Jufei grew from a 2005 Shenzhen start-up with RMB59.5m registered capital into what Chinese industry press calls the country's leading backlight-LED maker within seven years of founding.
notes: Low profile; no personal interviews found. Best route is Jufei's securities/IR office (jfzq@, tel 0755-29646311).

name: Corbin J Robertson Jr
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Natural Resource Partners L.P. (NYSE: NRP); director, Quintana Minerals and KLX Energy Services
profile: Houston-born (1947) grandson of oilman Hugh Roy Cullen, founder of Quintana Petroleum. He started in the family business at 15, inherited oil holdings and in the 1980s moved into coal royalties, amassing one of the largest private U.S. coal reserves. He leads NRP, a Houston partnership owning mineral and royalty interests (coal, soda ash, carbon-neutral initiatives).
interesting_fact: He was an All-American linebacker at the University of Texas who captained the Longhorns to victory in the 1969 Cotton Bowl Classic.
deep_cut_fact: Racing as 'Saron Stable', he bred Turkoman (by Alydar), voted 1986 Eclipse Award U.S. Champion Older Male, and raced Hall of Fame filly Bold 'n Determined (inducted 1997).
notes: Goes by 'Corby'. Serves on University of Houston Energy Advisory Board; UH has a Corbin J. Robertson Society. Major GOP donor and coal-industry figure: politically sensitive topics. NRP IR contact is the only published route.

name: Steven Ferguson
current_role: Principal of Linton Investments, the Ferguson family investment office (Aberdeenshire, Scotland)
profile: Aberdeenshire entrepreneur who built Kintore-based Ferguson Group (offshore containers, accommodation modules) into a global offshore rental business over three decades, selling it to Brambles in 2014 for ~£320m. Now invests via family office Linton Investments, incl. North Sea services firm Centrifuges Un-Limited (2020).
interesting_fact: Ferguson Group grew from a small North Sea container firm into a global business with a fleet of 16,000+ offshore containers, tanks and baskets, and in 2011 launched its own 220-berth accommodation service vessel, ASV Pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 the Ferguson family set up the Inverurie Youth Sports Foundation, which has funded 61 young athletes across 34 sports in the Garioch area - including freestyle skier Kirsty Muir (2022 Winter Olympian) and Tokyo Paralympic finalist swimmer Conner Morrison.
notes: Private family-office figure; best route is Linton Investments' published admin email. Sale-to-Brambles detail per Energy Voice (https://www.energyvoice.com/?p=64838, not directly fetchable here). Energy angle: North Sea services and decommissioning (Centrifuges).

name: Michael Gregory
profile: A UK businessman listed on Hurun Global (2015–2019) and the Sunday Times Rich List (about £295–320m) with wealth from engineering services and electric power. An East Midlands rich-list ranking places a Michael Gregory at £295m, but I couldn't confirm his company from public sources.
notes: Ambiguous common name. A Michael Gregory appears at £295m in an East Midlands rich-list ranking (https://www.hinckleytimes.net/news/local-news/triumph-rich-list-john-bloor-9151652), but no industry is given. name: Li Ruijie
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Power Leader Investment Holding (宝德集团); actual controller of Power Leader Computer Systems (server maker)
profile: Li Ruijie (b. 1967, Jieyang, Guangdong) co-founded server maker Power Leader (宝德) with his wife Zhang Yunxia in 1997, listed it in Hong Kong in 2002, and pushed it into online-game servers and games, which became Shenzhen-listed Zhongqingbao (中青宝). He has handed Zhongqingbao's chair to the next generation while controlling Power Leader Computing, a domestic server/PC maker.
interesting_fact: His Power Leader Computing, a Chinese server maker, unveiled a custom 'PowerStar' CPU in May 2023, produced by Intel specially for Power Leader and aimed at commercial branded PCs.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the early 1990s selling sound cards before moving into server after-sales and then manufacturing, riding Intel's rise; Power Leader went public in Hong Kong within about three years of being founded.
notes: No published contact found (powerleader.com.cn blocked automated fetch). Sensitive: in Mar 2025 Shenzhen CSRC bureau issued administrative penalties to Zhang Yunxia and Li Ruijie over disclosure violations; the 2023 PowerStar chip launch drew 'rebadged Intel' criticism. Avoid these in outreach.

name: Zhang Yunxia
current_role: Co-founder and co-controller of PowerLeader (宝德) group, Shenzhen; legal representative and head of Shenzhen Zhongqingbao Interactive Network (ZQGame, SZ:300052)
profile: Tianjin-born, Nankai University computer-software graduate who co-founded Shenzhen PowerLeader (宝德) in 1997, now a top domestic Chinese server/cloud-hardware brand. The group also controls listed online-game and cloud-services company Zhongqingbao (ZQGame), where she was GM 2008-2012 and is now legal representative. Wealth shared with co-controller Li Ruijie.
interesting_fact: PowerLeader, which she co-founded in 1997, describes itself as one of China's top 5 domestic server brands and No. 9 in the Asia-Pacific server market. It now builds AI/GPU servers and cloud solutions.

A Shenzhen CSRC penalty (Mar 2025) says she was detained on 29 Dec 2023 on suspicion of refusing to carry out a court judgment and released on bail the same day; disclosure was delayed. name: Steven Lamprell
current_role: Founder of Lamprell (UAE-based energy fabrication/rig services group); not involved in day-to-day management
profile: British-born (1950) entrepreneur who moved to the UAE with his family and in 1976 founded Lamprell, which grew from rig maintenance into fabrication of jack-up rigs, FPSO modules/turrets and offshore wind structures from yards in Sharjah, Hamriyah and Jebel Ali. He sold a majority stake when Lamprell floated on London's AIM in Oct 2006 (reported £265M); the company celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2026.
interesting_fact: For Lamprell's 50th anniversary (2026) he said: 'What I am most proud of is not the scale Lamprell has reached, but the culture that remains... It has been a privilege to pioneer Lamprell and witness its 50-year success story.'
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen polo player with his own entry in Horace Laffaye's 'The Polo Encyclopedia', and a racehorse owner.
notes: Private; Dubai/UAE-based. Lamprell is no longer London-listed. Energy-transition angle: Lamprell now builds offshore wind foundations as well as oil & gas structures. Approach via company communications.

name: Manish H Bhatia
current_role: President and Chief Operating Officer, Micron Technology (previously EVP Global Operations); Independent Director, Quantinuum
profile: Joined Micron in 2017 as EVP Global Operations; now President & COO, running its business units, fabs, supply chain, IT/AI and government affairs (the HBM/DRAM build-out behind the AI data-center boom). Previously led silicon operations at Western Digital and SanDisk after McKinsey and Matrix Semiconductor. Quantinuum board member.
interesting_fact: He was awarded Singapore's Public Service Medal (Friends of Singapore) in 2024 for contributions to the country's semiconductor industry, and sits on the Singapore Economic Development Board and the U.S.-Japan Business Council.
deep_cut_fact: An MIT mechanical engineer (BS and MS), he did his MBA at MIT Sloan as a Leaders for Manufacturing fellow, and early on worked at Matrix Semiconductor, the 3D one-time-programmable memory startup later bought by SanDisk.
notes: Title has changed: Micron's site now lists him as President & COO (input shows EVP Global Operations). Chairs Quantinuum's nominating & governance committee. Matrix Semiconductor detail: Micron bio confirms he worked there; the 3D-memory/SanDisk description is general background on that company. Route via Micron corporate communications (media contact Mark Plungy).

name: Thomas E Jorden
current_role: Non-Executive Chair of the Board, Devon Energy (since the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger)
profile: Geophysicist and shale-era E&P chief: he joined Key Production in 1993 as chief geophysicist, became CEO (2011) and chairman (2012) of Cimarex Energy, then led Coterra Energy (Cimarex + Cabot, 2021) as chairman, CEO and president. After Devon's all-stock ~$58bn combination with Coterra closed on 7 May 2026, he became Devon's non-executive board chair.
interesting_fact: He steered two big shale mergers in five years - Cimarex/Cabot into Coterra (2021) and Coterra into Devon (2026) - ending up chairing one of the largest US independent oil & gas producers.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both his bachelor's and master's in geophysics at the Colorado School of Mines, later chaired its Board of Trustees, and started his career at Superior Oil Company and Union Pacific Resources before joining Key Production as chief geophysicist in 1993. He is also a Tulane University trustee.
notes: SEC-derived wealth (~$316m). Devon media contact is Michelle Hindmarch (phone only published). Known as a thoughtful, technical speaker on shale and capital discipline - a good podcast guest candidate via Devon communications.

name: Jack A Fusco
current_role: Chairman (since May 2026), President and CEO (since May 2016), Cheniere Energy, Inc. (NYSE: LNG)
profile: A 40-year power and gas veteran, Fusco runs Cheniere, the largest US LNG exporter (Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi). Earlier he cofounded Goldman-backed Orion Power (CEO 1998-2002), ran Texas Genco to a 5x+ return on its 2006 merger with NRG, and as Calpine CEO (2008-14) led it out of bankruptcy to become America's largest gas-fired power generator.
interesting_fact: Named 2025 Chief Executive of the Year at the Platts Global Energy Awards and repeatedly Institutional Investor's best natural-gas CEO (2020, 2022-2025); in 2012 he was its best electric-industry CEO.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1984 as a mechanical engineer at Pacific Gas & Electric straight out of Cal State Sacramento; 13 years later he moved to Goldman Sachs as a VP trading wholesale electricity, which led to founding Orion Power. He sits on the board of the American-Italian Cancer Foundation.
notes: Very relevant: gas-to-power and LNG exports tie into data-center power demand; frequent CERAWeek/Gastech speaker, so conference-stage interviews are a realistic route. Media requests via Cheniere newsroom/IR.

name: Gyan M Swarup
current_role: Director (listed from 2012), Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd., Kolkata (role not confirmed as current)
profile: Gyan Mahendra Swarup is listed as a director of Paharpur Cooling Towers, a family-owned Kolkata maker of cooling towers, air-cooled condensers and heat exchangers incorporated in 1949. Hurun India listed him in 2018-19. Day-to-day leadership is held by Gaurav Swarup (Co-Chairman & MD) and Vikram Swarup (MD).
interesting_fact: Paharpur is one of the world's largest cooling-tower makers, with offices across India plus Europe and Turkey operations. Its heat-rejection technology matters for thermal power and, increasingly, data-center cooling.
notes: Almost no public biographical information; his relationship to Gaurav and Vikram Swarup is unverified. Whether he is alive and still on the board is unconfirmed; check MCA filings. The listed email is Paharpur's general company address, not a personal one. Gaurav Swarup is the more public family member.

name: Deming Xiao
current_role: EVP, Global Operations, Monolithic Power Systems (Nasdaq: MPWR)
profile: Process engineer turned operations chief who joined power-semiconductor maker MPS in May 2001 as Foundry Manager, led MPS Asia Operations from 2008, and now runs global operations. MPS power-management chips are key to AI server and data-centre power delivery. Earlier he worked at Chartered Semiconductor and Fairchild Imaging Sensors.
interesting_fact: An early MPS employee (joined 2001, three years before its 2004 IPO), he built out the fabless company's Asian foundry and manufacturing base as MPS grew into a major supplier of power chips for AI accelerators.
deep_cut_fact: He studied semiconductor physics at Sichuan University in Chengdu (B.S.), earned an MSEE at Wayne State University in Detroit, and spent six years managing process integration engineering at Fairchild Imaging Sensors before joining MPS.
notes: Low public profile operations executive (age 62 per the FY2024 10-K). Best route is MPS investor relations. Bio also on the MPS management page (https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/about-mps/managementteam.html), which is JS-rendered.

profile: Li Anmin founded the Anmin coking plant in Jiexiu, Shanxi in 1984 and from 1993 led Shanxi Antai Group as chairman and GM, expanding from a single coking plant into coal washing, coke, steel rolling, power and building materials; the company listed in Shanghai in 2003. He remains its controlling shareholder (~31.6%) per 2025-26 filings.

deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1984 as factory director of the Anmin Coking Plant he founded, the business that grew into Antai Group.
notes: Poor podcast fit: past exchange censure (2015) and CSRC penalty (2016) over related-party disclosures; his shares were frozen/pledged in a bank dispute settled Jan 2026. Fortune listing is dated (Hurun 2007-2015). Coal/coke rather than clean energy. Referenced as living controlling shareholder in Feb 2026 share-unfreezing filings.

current_role: Board chairman, Zonda Group (中大集团), Yancheng, Jiangsu (as of 2008; current status unconfirmed)
profile: Co-leader, with Xu Liankuan (group president), of Zonda Group, a private Jiangsu manufacturer founded in 1994 whose Zonda Bus unit makes coaches, city buses and commercial vehicles, later including new-energy buses, plus auto-maintenance equipment. name: Yang Jianzhong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and director-level family principal of Juli Sling Co. (巨力索具, SZSE: 002342) / Juli Group, Xushui, Baoding, Hebei; chaired the listed company through its 1st-6th boards (to ~2022)
profile: Born 1965, Yang Jianzhong has run the family rigging business in Xushui, Hebei since 1992, building Juli Group and its SZSE-listed unit Juli Sling (wire-rope slings, rigging and hoisting gear, incl. for energy projects). name: Susan Tobbell
current_role: Co-founder, SGN Retail (Essex forecourt operator; sale of 100% to Essar's EET Retail agreed Sept 2026); director, TG Convenience Stores and Starbridge Property Investment
profile: Susan Margaret Tobbell is a UK fuel-retail entrepreneur. name: Mike F Chang
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and EVP of Strategic Initiatives, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor (Nasdaq: AOSL)

name: Gary Hromadko
current_role: Independent Director, Equinix Inc. (since June 2003); private investor
profile: Silicon Valley investor (age 73) who has sat on the board of Equinix, the world's largest data-center/interconnection REIT, since June 2003. He was a venture partner at Crosslink Capital (2002-2017), has been a private investor since 1993, and formerly served on the board of Carbonite; his wealth comes largely from long-held Equinix stock.
interesting_fact: He is Equinix's longest-tenured current director, joining in 2003 when it was a post-dotcom recovery story; in 2025 he chaired both the Finance Committee and the Real Estate Committee overseeing data-center development capital spending.

notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Equinix's proxy says interested parties may write to the Board c/o the Corporate Secretary, Equinix Inc., One Lagoon Drive, Redwood City, CA 94065 (corporate address, not personal). Good fit for data-center episode as a 20+ year insider of the sector's bellwether.

name: Randall J Weisenburger
current_role: Managing Member, Mile 26 Capital LLC; Presiding Director and Senior Independent Director, Carnival Corp & plc; director of Valero Energy, MP Materials and Corsair Gaming
profile: Finance executive (age 67) who was EVP and CFO of advertising giant Omnicom Group from 1998 to 2014, after a decade (1988-98) as a founding member of boutique bank Wasserstein Perella, where he ran its merchant-banking arm Wasserstein & Co. deep_cut_fact: In 1988 he was a founding member of Bruce Wasserstein and Joseph Perella's boutique investment bank Wasserstein Perella, serving as president and CEO of its merchant-banking subsidiary Wasserstein & Co. and as an executive of several of its portfolio companies before joining Omnicom.

Only published route: letters to Carnival directors via Carnival Corporation & plc, Attention: Company Secretary, 3655 N.W. 87th Avenue, Miami, FL 33178 (per 2026 proxy). Valero/MP Materials board seats give energy/critical-minerals angle.

name: Gautam N Mehra
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Savita Oil Technologies Ltd (re-appointed MD to Sept 2028)
profile: Chemical engineer with a UC Berkeley MBA, Gautam N. Mehra leads Savita Oil Technologies, the Mumbai petroleum-specialties firm his father N.K. Mehra co-founded in 1961. Savita leads India in transformer oils, white oils and waxes, sells in 75+ countries, owns wind farms, and now markets data-center immersion-cooling and BESS fluids.
interesting_fact: Savita says it set up India's first private-sector R&D centre in the petroleum industry, was the first Indian private petroleum company to earn ISO 9001, and commissioned its first windmill in Maharashtra around 1999-2002 - an early oil-company move into renewables.
deep_cut_fact: Savita began in 1961 at Sakinaka, Mumbai, making liquid paraffin as an import substitute; in his chairman's message Mehra says founder N.K. Mehra 'drew inspiration from the sun' and coined the company motto 'Bonds Build Businesses'.
notes: legal@savita.com is the published registered-office (Nariman Point) email, likely routed via company secretary. Good podcast angle: Savita now sells 'Data Center Fluids' (immersion cooling) and transformer oils for grid/BESS.

name: Vijay S Nair

profile: Vijay S. Nair (registry name: Vijayasankaran A. Sivaraman Nair) is the founder and managing director of Visen Industries, an unlisted Mumbai-based chemicals/petrochemicals company incorporated in 1985. He appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2016-2017.
notes: Identity match rests on registry/aggregator data (tofler.in, Crunchbase), not an official bio; confirm before outreach. Private company with little press coverage. Low priority for the podcast.

name: Hemant Kamala Jalan
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Indigo Paints Ltd (NSE: INDIGOPNTS), Pune
profile: Founder of Indigo Paints (2000), which he grew from a small cement-paint maker into India's fifth-largest decorative paint company by revenue, with Sequoia Capital backing (2014, 2016). Indigo listed in Feb 2021 after an IPO oversubscribed ~117 times, and in 2023 moved into waterproofing/construction chemicals by buying 51% of Apple Chemie India.
interesting_fact: Indigo's January 2021 IPO was oversubscribed about 117 times, with anchor investors including the Government of Singapore, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs; MS Dhoni has been its brand ambassador since 2018, and actor Mohanlal fronts it in Kerala.

notes: Paints/chemicals, not energy - weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast (dataset tags him as petrochemicals). Gives media interviews on growth (e.g. Economic Times). No personal channels verified.

name: Richard J Hendrix
current_role: Chair of the Board, Navitas Semiconductor (Nasdaq: NVTS); operating executive, Crestview Advisors
profile: Richard Hendrix (60) was at FBR & Co. from 1999, its CEO 2009-2017 and chairman 2012-2017. Since 2017 he has been an operating executive at PE firm Crestview and ran the Live Oak SPACs, including Live Oak Acquisition Corp. II, which took GaN/SiC power-chip maker Navitas public in Oct 2021. He has chaired Navitas' board since April 2025.
interesting_fact: Hendrix sponsored a string of SPACs: Live Oak I merged with bioplastics maker Danimer Scientific, Live Oak II with Navitas, whose gallium-nitride and silicon-carbide chips now target AI data-center power supplies and 800V power distribution.
deep_cut_fact: Before FBR he was a managing director in PNC Capital Markets' investment banking group, where he headed PNC's asset-backed securities business; he holds a B.S. in Finance from Miami University (Ohio).

public_contacts.value: secretary@navitassemi.com (Navitas corporate secretary; published channel for communications to the Board chair; tel +1 844-654-2642)

name: Moshe Arkin
current_role: Executive Chairman, Sol-Gel Technologies (Nasdaq: SLGL); founder & chairman, Arkin Holdings/Arkin Capital; co-founder & chairman, Accelmed; director and 10% owner, Odysight.ai
profile: Israeli investor Mori Arkin (born 1952) took over his father's pharma importer Agis at 19 and built it into a listed generics maker, sold to Perrigo for about $818M in 2004-05. He now invests in life sciences and med-tech via Arkin Holdings and Accelmed, and chairs dermatology firm Sol-Gel, awaiting Phase 3 data for its Gorlin syndrome drug.
interesting_fact: Forbes dubbed him a 'pharma kingpin-turned-VC' when he joined the billionaires' club in 2012; he is also a backer of Odysight.ai, an AI visual-sensing company for predictive maintenance.
deep_cut_fact: As a Russian speaker he served in IDF intelligence Unit 848 (later Unit 8200) in Sinai, then began university studying Bible and archaeology before switching to psychology (BA with honours) and graduate work in physiological psychology and philosophy of science.
notes: Goes by Mori Arkin. Sol-Gel's SGT-610 top-line data were due late November 2026, a sensitive moment for the company. Arkin Capital's website appeared to redirect elsewhere, so it was not listed. Weak fit for energy/data-centre focus; the Odysight.ai stake is the AI angle.

name: Richard P. Wallace
current_role: President & CEO and Director, KLA Corporation; Director, Marvell Technology
profile: Rick Wallace has led KLA, the leading maker of semiconductor process-control and inspection equipment that is critical to AI-chip manufacturing, as CEO since 2006 after a 30+-year career inside the company. He also sits on Marvell's board and previously served on the boards of Splunk, Proofpoint and NetApp.
interesting_fact: He previously chaired the board of SEMI, the global semiconductor equipment and materials industry association.
deep_cut_fact: He joined KLA Instruments in 1988 as an applications engineer, after earlier stints at Ultratech Stepper and Cypress Semiconductor; he holds a BSEE from the University of Michigan and a master's in engineering management from Santa Clara University.
notes: Wealth estimate is from SEC insider holdings (~$142M), so below UHNW billionaire tier. Media route is KLA Corporate Communications (media@kla.com, Mike Dulin); IR is VP Kevin Kessel. Good AI-chip supply chain angle.

name: John Graham-Cumming
current_role: Member of the Board of Directors, Cloudflare (NYSE: NET); former Cloudflare CTO (to March 2025)
profile: British programmer and writer with an Oxford DPhil in secure-systems formal methods (1992). He co-founded Electric Cloud, joined Cloudflare as an early programmer, became its CTO and moved to the board in 2025. He wrote the POPFile machine-learning spam filter, The Geek Atlas and The GNU Make Book, and now maintains side projects like the Low-background Steel catalogue of pre-AI-era data.
interesting_fact: His 2009 online petition led UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown to issue a formal government apology for the persecution of Alan Turing. In 2010 he launched Plan 28, a project to build Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.
deep_cut_fact: On 10 April 2011 he launched GAGA-1, a homemade balloon capsule, from near Cambridge; it reached 32,086m, flew 2h12m and its camera took 1,856 photos, including the Thames estuary, the moon and the black sky, before landing in a field west of Cambridge.
notes: Very approachable and active online (blog, X @jgrahamc, GitHub). A strong podcast guest on internet infrastructure, AI-era data (lowbackgroundsteel.ai) and computing history. His own 2025 Cloudflare post 'Three Chapters at Cloudflare: Programmer to CTO to Board' is a good primer.

name: Yvonne McGill
current_role: Former CFO, Dell Technologies (resigned as CFO Sept 9, 2025); former director, Applied Materials (2019-Sept 2025). Current role not verified.
profile: Yvonne McGill joined Dell in 1997 and rose through its finance organisation to become CFO, overseeing accounting, FP&A, tax, treasury, IR and corporate development. She was an independent director of Applied Materials from 2019 to September 2025. She resigned as Dell's CFO in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Her whole corporate career was effectively at one company: she spent more than 27 years at Dell, from 1997 to 2025, before becoming its CFO, while also sitting on the board of chip-equipment leader Applied Materials.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Dell she worked at government-IT contractor ManTech International and at Price Waterhouse. She is a Certified Public Accountant (inactive).
notes: Dell's 8-K of Sept 8, 2025 records her resignation as CFO. It cites no disagreement over financial matters, and she stayed as an adviser through Oct 31, 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1571996/000157199625000104/dell-20250905.htm). Her net worth comes from Dell/AMAT insider holdings. Her next role is unknown, and LinkedIn is the likely channel but was not verified.

current_role: Chairman of the Board, One Liberty Properties (NYSE: OLP); Senior VP and director, BRT Apartments (NYSE: BRT); Chairman/CEO of Georgetown Partners (manager of Gould Investors L.P.)

name: Gregg J Felton
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Altus Power (Stamford, CT; now owned by TPG Rise Climate)
profile: Gregg Felton co-founded Altus Power, a developer, owner and operator of commercial-scale and community solar, storage and EV-charging assets, and has been with it since 2013. Altus went public via SPAC in December 2021 (NYSE: AMPS) and has since been taken private by TPG Rise Climate. He previously was a Goldman Sachs partner and CIO of GSAM's Credit Alternatives platform.
interesting_fact: Altus Power energized its first solar system in Bridgeport, Connecticut in 2010, took an initial investment from Blackstone in 2014, and grew into one of the largest US commercial-scale solar owners before teaming up with TPG Rise Climate.
deep_cut_fact: A Tufts economics graduate with both a J.D. (Georgetown Law) and an MBA (Georgetown business school), Felton started at Chase Manhattan Bank and, before Altus, ran Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Credit Alternatives platform overseeing more than $5B in hedge-fund and private-credit vehicles.

name: Jayendra H Kharawala
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jay Chemical Industries Pvt Ltd (JCIL), India (listed as chairman on the company website)
profile: Founder of Jay Chemical Industries, started in 1967 as a small dye and dye-intermediate unit. JCIL is now one of the world's top reactive-dye producers, with more than 15% of India's market, sales in over 40 countries and revenue above $200M. It has expanded into digital textile inks, construction chemicals and garments.
interesting_fact: JCIL makes more than half of its own raw-material inputs (over 50% backward integration). That is a deliberate self-reliance strategy that Kharawala built into a dye business started when international firms dominated Indian dyes.
deep_cut_fact: Jay Chemicals marked its 50th anniversary on 9 March 2017. The company credits its founding to Kharawala's vision 'to do business that would not only provide for his family but would better society as well'.
notes: Private company with a low profile. Day-to-day operations are run by Managing Director Greeven Kharawala. Alive status is not independently confirmed (the company site still lists him as chairman). The links are corporate, not personal. Industry is textile dyes, so the fit with energy and data centers is weak.

name: Ramesh Vinayak Vaze
current_role: Not on the current board of S H Kelkar and Company (Keva); current status unconfirmed
profile: Member of the Vaze promoter family behind S H Kelkar and Company (now branded Keva), a Mumbai fragrance, flavour and aroma-ingredients maker that began as an industrial perfume manufacturer in British India and is now one of India's largest fragrance companies. The family's third generation, Kedar Vaze, is Group CEO; Prabha Vaze is a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Keva started as S H Kelkar & Company, a maker of industrial perfumes in British India, and grew organically and via acquisitions into an Indian fragrance multinational.

name: Bharat Naresh Oberoi
current_role: Joint Managing Director and Promoter, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Bharat Oberoi is a promoter and Joint MD (since 2003) of Powerica, the Mumbai power-solutions firm his father Naresh Chander Oberoi founded in 1984. Powerica builds diesel generator sets and medium-speed large generators for standby/prime power (a key data-center backup market) and since 2008 has been a wind IPP and wind EPC/O&M contractor. He joined in 1994 and leads its marketing side.
interesting_fact: Powerica began as a diesel-generator business in 1984, added medium-speed large generators in 1996, and in 2008 moved into wind energy as an independent power producer, later adding wind EPC and O&M services.
notes: Low public profile; last on Hurun India in 2018. Backup-power gensets for Indian data centers plus wind IPP make a natural energy/data-center angle. Route via company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no sourced personal deep-cut.

name: Vasant Laxminarayan Rathi
current_role: Promoter and Non-Executive Director, Advanced Enzyme Technologies Ltd (NSE: ADVENZYMES); heads its US subsidiaries
profile: V. L. Rathi, a pharmacist turned enzyme entrepreneur, co-founded Rathi Papains (1978), set up Cal-India Foods in the US (1985) and has been with Advanced Enzyme Technologies since 1993. The Thane-based enzyme and probiotics maker listed in India in 2016; from the US he runs its American subsidiaries.
interesting_fact: Advanced Enzymes grew from a family papain business into one of India's largest enzyme makers, with US and European arms. It owns Germany's evoxx technologies in Monheim am Rhein.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Rathi Papains (1978), made enzymes from papain, the protein-digesting enzyme taken from papaya latex. He trained as a pharmacist (B.Pharm, Nagpur University) and earned an MS at the University of Hawaii.
notes: Categorized as Chemicals/Petrochemicals 'energy', but the business is industrial and nutritional enzymes, so the fit for an energy podcast is weak (enzymes are used in biofuel/biogas, which could be an angle). Low media profile; route via the US subsidiaries (Cal-India Foods / AST Enzymes in California) or the company's general email.

name: Suresh Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Chairman, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Samrat flour brand), Parakh Group, Pune
profile: Younger son of Parakh Group founder Harakchand K. Parakh (1930-2015), Suresh Parakh is a flour-milling veteran who chairs Parakh Agro Industries, maker of Samrat atta, besan and oil. The family's Parakh Foods built the Gemini edible-oil brand, sold to Cargill in 2004-05; the Pune group now spans FMCG, flexible packaging, real estate (Gemini Housing) and wind power.
interesting_fact: Parakh Group's energy arm, Parakh Energy, runs 8.3 MW of wind turbines (4 Suzlon, 2 Vestas) in Dhule, Maharashtra, feeding the western regional grid.
deep_cut_fact: He drove the adoption of Swiss Bühler milling technology in the group's flour mills, which combine traditional stone chakkis with Bühler machinery, and personally heads the bulk flour sales business, with some customers loyal for 25+ years. B.Com, Maharashtra Mandal College, Pune.
notes: Primarily a food/FMCG businessman; the energy link is the family's wind assets and former edible-oil refining (Gemini sold to Cargill: https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2011/03/29/Acquisition-boosts-Cargill-brand-portfolio-in-India). Elder brother Prakash Parakh led group expansion. Low-fit for energy podcast.

name: Sureshbhai Jayantibhai Patel
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Bodal Chemicals Ltd (NSE: BODALCHEM), Ahmedabad.
profile: Suresh J. Patel founded Bodal Chemicals in Ahmedabad around 1989-90 as a small vinyl sulphone maker and built it into a vertically integrated producer of dye intermediates, textile/leather/paper dyestuffs and basic chemicals (sulphuric acid etc.), exporting to 40+ countries. He has been chairman & MD since 2006, the year the company went public.
interesting_fact: Bodal is one of very few dye makers integrated from basic chemicals through intermediates to finished dyestuffs; by 2015 it ran eight Gujarat plants with ~2,500 staff and sales above Rs 1,000 crore, exporting 80% of its dyestuff output.
deep_cut_fact: Bodal began in 1989 as 'JK Pharma', a two-man partnership of Suresh Patel and Ramesh Patel with capacity of just 60 tonnes a year of vinyl sulphone; it became Bodal Chemicals Pvt Ltd in 1994.
notes: Chemicals, not energy/data-center; modest wealth (Hurun India 2017 only). Director Bhavin Patel runs the dyestuff division. Best route: company secretarial/info email.

name: Madan Mohan Dhanuka
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, I G Petrochemicals Ltd (Dhanuka Group), Mumbai (per Simply Wall St/Investing.com; some sites list Nikunj Dhanuka as chairman)
profile: Senior figure of the Dhanuka Group and a director of I G Petrochemicals since its incorporation in October 1988. IGPL, set up in technical collaboration with Germany's Lurgi, is India's largest maker of phthalic anhydride (used in plasticisers, paints and resins), with plants at Taloja, Maharashtra; he also sits on the board of Mysore Petro Chemicals.
interesting_fact: He has served on IGPL's board for more than 35 years, since the company's founding in 1988, as it grew into India's largest phthalic anhydride producer.

notes: Chairman title conflicts across data sites; confirm in latest IGPL annual report. Day-to-day leadership by younger family members (Nikunj, Mayank Dhanuka). Low public profile.

name: Abhay Vithaldas Udeshi
current_role: Chairman, Jayant Agro-Organics Ltd (Mumbai; BSE/NSE listed)
profile: Mumbai industrialist who succeeded his father Vithaldas Udeshi as chairman of Jayant Agro-Organics, a castor-oil and castor-derivatives company with an estimated 35-40% share of the global castor oil market. The group runs JVs with France's Arkema and a Japanese partner, plus hybrid castor seed and pharma-grade oil operations.
interesting_fact: He notes India produces nearly 90% of the world's castor oil; Jayant says it was the first company in India to process castor seeds into oil, starting in 1952.
deep_cut_fact: He helped create the Sustainable Castor Association (with Arkema, BASF and NGO Solidaridad), which runs a sustainable castor farming code and certification for Indian farmers and had grown to 31 global members by 2024.
notes: University of Baroda graduate; director of the Sustainable Castor Association. Energy relevance is modest (company has a power-generation segment; castor-based bio-chemicals). Family-run board.

name: Brij Bhushan Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (and subsidiary Shyam SEL and Power); President, Indian Chamber of Commerce
profile: Kolkata-based industrialist (B.Com, University of Calcutta) who has led Shyam Metalics since its inception in 2001, building it into an integrated metals producer (ferroalloys, iron and steel, aluminium foil) with captive power plants in West Bengal and Odisha; listed on NSE/BSE in 2021. He owns roughly 9.5% directly, with the promoter family holding the majority.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Shyam Metalics became India's largest producer of ferroalloys (per CRISIL, as of Feb 2021); its integrated plants run partly on captive power, hence 'Energy' in the name.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Indian Chamber of Commerce's National Expert Committee on Minerals and Metals in 2019 and that October won Zee Business's 'Inspirational Leader of the Year' award in the 'Dare to Dream' category, before rising to ICC Senior VP and then President.
notes: Hurun India figure ($132m, 2019) is stale; promoter-family stake is worth much more today. Head of IR Pankaj Harlalka appears on earnings calls; IR partner is EY (per call transcripts). ICC presidency gives a second route via Indian Chamber of Commerce, Kolkata.

name: Russell Craig Ellwanger
current_role: CEO (since May 2005) and director, Tower Semiconductor Ltd (Nasdaq/TASE: TSEM), Migdal HaEmek, Israel
profile: An American-born semiconductor veteran, Ellwanger spent 1980–92 at Philips Semiconductors and 1992–96 at Novellus. He then held senior roles at Applied Materials from 1996 to 2005, including running its Metal CVD, CMP/electroplating and global services units. Since 2005 he has turned Tower into a profitable specialty foundry; it now has big silicon-photonics and SiGe contracts for AI data-centre optical modules, including work with NVIDIA.
interesting_fact: Tower reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $460m (+24%), and Ellwanger raised the 2028 target to $3.6bn revenue and $1.2bn net profit. Growth is driven by silicon photonics for data-centre optics; Tower signed customer contracts for about $1.3bn of 2027 silicon-photonics revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He started wrestling at 11 and his family picked a Las Vegas high school for its wrestling programme. While studying physics at BYU he joined Philips Semiconductors' Utah site, partly because it was one of the few companies offering students health insurance, and was later sent to Philips' main lab in the Netherlands.
notes: Articulate and quotable: Globes says he quotes management gurus, William Faulkner and Alice in Wonderland. A strong data-centre/AI-optics guest. The IR contact is Liat Avraham (+972-4-6506154). A media contact (oritsha@towersemi.com) appears in some releases but I didn't verify it. The $1.3bn photonics-contracts figure comes from a Finviz headline.

JA Solar's 2007 Nasdaq IPO filing listed Mr. Huixian Wang with 9.58% of the BVI Jinglong Group (second-largest stake after Jin's 32.96%), which explains his single 2008 Hurun listing. No current role or public activity found since.
interesting_fact: He was one of 11 Ningjin co-owners of Jinglong Group (BVI) named in JA Solar's 2007 US IPO prospectus, a group of Hebei entrepreneurs whose wafer business seeded one of the world's largest solar-module makers.
notes: Very low profile; only on Hurun China 2008. Identity rests on the JA Solar F-1/A shareholder footnote. Jinglong moved out of PV into property, hotels and finance after JA Solar's 2019 Shenzhen relisting (Jiemian). No published contact; any approach would go via JA Solar (002459) or Jinglong Group. Not a strong outreach target.

name: Stefan A Dyckerhoff
current_role: Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures; independent director, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) since Nov 2019
profile: Networking executive turned VC. He ran Cisco's Edge Routing unit and Juniper's Platform Systems Division before joining Sutter Hill Ventures in 2012. An early backer and director of AI-connectivity chipmaker Astera Labs (IPO 2024), he also has board seats at SiFive and Enfabrica.
interesting_fact: His board seats cover much of the AI data-center 'plumbing' stack: Astera Labs (PCIe/CXL retimers and scale-up switches), Enfabrica (AI networking silicon) and SiFive (RISC-V processor IP).
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he ran routers himself. From 2007 to 2009 he was VP & GM of Cisco's Edge Routing Business Unit, and he then ran the Platform Systems Division at rival Juniper. He has a Duke BSE in electrical engineering and computer science and a Stanford MSEE.
notes: Low public profile. Sutter Hill is famously quiet, and its website is a placeholder with no contact details. The Astera Labs media contact reaches the company, not him. A warm intro through the Astera Labs or Sutter Hill network is likely the best route.

name: Jack Hartung
current_role: Independent director, Tesla (since 2025, Audit Committee); also on boards of The Honest Company, Portillo's, Wonder Group and ZocDoc. Retired from Chipotle March 2026
profile: John R. 'Jack' Hartung, 68, spent 18 years at McDonald's (ending as CFO of its Partner Brands Group, which included Chipotle) before joining Chipotle in 2002, serving as CFO for 20 years, then CFAO and President & Chief Strategy Officer as it grew past 3,500 restaurants. He stayed on after Brian Niccol left for Starbucks, then retired as senior advisor in March 2026; he now sits on Tesla's board among others.
interesting_fact: He was persuaded to delay his retirement when CEO Brian Niccol made a surprise move to Starbucks in 2024; he has been named 'CFO of the Year' by the Orange County Business Journal and 'Best CFO' (restaurants) by Institutional Investor.
deep_cut_fact: Portillo's 2026 proxy lists his favorite menu item as the Italian Beef with Hot Peppers. He holds a B.S. in accounting and economics and an MBA from Illinois State University, and is a (non-practicing) CPA and CMA.
notes: Tesla board seat gives an energy/AI angle (Tesla Energy, Megapacks). Low social-media profile; route via board/IR channels or Chipotle alumni network.

name: Theodore Blegen
current_role: Retired EVP & CFO (Feb 2026), Monolithic Power Systems; remains with MPS in a transition role
profile: T. Bernie Blegen joined power-chip maker Monolithic Power Systems in 2011 as corporate controller and served as CFO from 2016 until retiring after the FY2025 10-K in Feb 2026, a decade in which MPS grew into a major supplier of power-management chips for AI servers and data centers. Earlier he held finance roles at Xilinx and Credence Systems; UC Santa Barbara graduate.
interesting_fact: CEO Michael Hsing credited him with helping MPS grow 'consistently at an above-market growth rate' during his ten years as CFO, after joining in 2011 'when MPS was relatively small and only beginning to strategically diversify'.
deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he worked in publishing and software finance, including at Times Mirror's higher-education group, Shutterfly and Micro Focus, per his executive profile; his 10-K bio cites 25+ years across the semiconductor, software and publishing industries.
notes: Goes by 'Bernie'. Now retired as CFO, so the company IR route is indirect; Rob Dean is interim CFO. Specific employers Times Mirror/Shutterfly/Micro Focus come from MarketScreener profiles (not the 10-K, which confirms only the publishing/software background).

name: Joseph W Gorder
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Valero Energy (CEO 2014-June 2023, Executive Chairman until 31 Dec 2024)
profile: Joe Gorder ran Valero, the largest US independent refiner, as CEO (May 2014-June 2023) and chairman (from end-2014), then executive chairman until retiring at end-2024. He rose through Diamond Shamrock/Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (sales, treasury, IT, business development) before Valero's 2001 acquisition of UDS.
interesting_fact: When he became CEO, UMSL noted he was one of only two undergraduate alumni of the University of Missouri-St. Louis running a Fortune 500 top-20 company (with Express Scripts' George Paz) - a distinction otherwise shared only by Cornell.
deep_cut_fact: A Pattonville High School (Maryland Heights, Mo.) grad, he chose UMSL because he could work 30-40 hours a week and still graduate on time (BSBA, marketing, 1979). His leadership line: 'I believe that a leader is one who serves... give them the latitude to do their jobs without micromanaging them.'
notes: Retired from Valero's board at end-2024, so Valero IR is only an indirect route; no personal social accounts found. SEC-derived wealth (~$125m). UMSL alumni network is a possible warm connection.

name: Hu Yuxing
profile: Appeared once on the Hurun China Rich List (2006, ~US$125M) with wealth attributed to 'CNPC & Tafo Petro Corp' (胡玉兴). No public source could be found describing this person or the company 'Tafo Petro', so identity and current status are unconfirmed.
notes: English and Chinese searches (胡玉兴 + 石油/Tafo/CNPC) returned nothing relevant. Likely a private oil-services operator tied to CNPC in the mid-2000s; many such firms faded after 2006. Not worth pursuing without a Chinese company name.

name: Dan O Dinges
current_role: Former Chairman, President and CEO of Cabot Oil & Gas (2002-2021); Coterra Energy director until the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger
profile: Dan Dinges ran Cabot Oil & Gas for about 20 years. He took over in 2002 after more than 20 years at Noble Energy/Samedan and built Cabot into a leading Marcellus Shale gas producer. He led the 2021 merger with Cimarex that created Coterra Energy and then served on Coterra's board. Coterra merged into Devon Energy in May 2026, and Dinges was not named to the combined board.
interesting_fact: He chaired the American Exploration & Production Council, the trade group of the largest US independent oil and gas producers, from 2015. He has also served on the boards of U.S. Steel and the American Petroleum Institute.
deep_cut_fact: Dinges started out as a Mobil Oil landman covering Louisiana, Arkansas and the central Gulf of Mexico. He holds a BBA in Petroleum Land Management from the University of Texas, a niche degree. He is a member of the All-American Wildcatters and served on the executive committee of UT Austin's Kay Bailey Hutchison Center for Energy, Law and Business.
notes: Retired from executive roles and Houston-based, with no personal website or social accounts found. Coterra no longer exists independently (merged into Devon, May 2026), so there is no current corporate press route. Industry associations (AXPC, All-American Wildcatters) or UT's KBH Energy Center are possible intro paths.

name: Michael C Morgan
current_role: Co-founding partner & Chairman, Triangle Peak Partners; Lead Director, Kinder Morgan Inc.
profile: Former president of Kinder Morgan (pipelines and energy infrastructure) who co-founded Triangle Peak Partners, a venture/growth investor in energy and technology, and runs the Portcullis Partners investment partnership. He is lead director at Kinder Morgan and has served on the boards of residential-solar firm Sunnova and AI-driven storage company Stem.
interesting_fact: He spans both ends of the energy transition: lead director of one of North America's largest natural-gas pipeline operators while backing solar, storage and clean-tech companies through Triangle Peak.
deep_cut_fact: A 2022 Stanford Distinguished Careers Institute fellow (billed as 'Energy & Technology Geek/Investor'), he co-chaired the Precourt Institute for Energy's advisory council, won the Stanford Associates Governors' Award, and once taught as an adjunct professor at Rice's Jones School.
notes: Kinder Morgan contacts are corporate routes, not personal. No working Triangle Peak website found. Sunnova filed for Chapter 11 in 2025, so avoid that topic. Education: Stanford BA econ & MA sociology, Harvard MBA. Stanford energy-network ties could make a warm intro.

name: Xue Yongmin
current_role: Unknown; Hurun China (2008) listed him with Dongfang Ferro Alloy (iron ore, coal)
profile: Xue Yongmin appeared once, on the 2008 Hurun China Rich List, with an estimated $120m fortune from iron-ore, coal and ferroalloy business 'Dongfang Ferro Alloy'. No public source confirming his identity or current role was found.
notes: Single 2008 list appearance; not found in web searches. Not a viable outreach target without registry-level research.

name: Yang Huaijin
current_role: Unknown; formerly founder/CEO of JA Solar (2005-2009) and later CEO and largest shareholder of Hareon Solar
profile: Yang Huaijin (Samuel Yang) founded JA Solar in 2005 with partner Jinglong Group (Jin Baofang) and ran it as CEO until July 2009 through its Nasdaq IPO, which put him on Hurun's 2008 list. He then became CEO and top shareholder of Shanghai-listed Hareon Solar, later selling his stake (~6.6%) to Huajun Industrial; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: He founded JA Solar, now one of the world's largest solar cell and module makers, in 2005 and led it as CEO through its 2007 Nasdaq listing.
deep_cut_fact: Before JA Solar, he also helped found Suntech Power, the company that made Shi Zhengrong China's first solar billionaire (per JA Solar's own website, as cited by Reuters).
notes: Hard to reach; no current company role or published contact found. Hareon Solar later went through severe distress, so avoid that topic. Wealth figure (Hurun 2008) is very dated. Uses English name Samuel Yang.

name: Hari Krishna Chaudhary
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Vikram Solar Ltd (NSE/BSE); Director, Vikram (India) Ltd; chairman of the Kolkata-based Vikram Group
profile: Patriarch of the Kolkata Vikram Group, whose businesses began in 1974 with tea-processing machinery and spread into CTC tea, sponge iron and textiles. The group's solar arm, Vikram Solar (founded 2005 and led by MD Gyanesh Chaudhary), now has ~9.5 GW of module capacity and listed on the BSE/NSE on 26 Aug 2025 after a Rs 2,079 crore IPO; he serves as non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Vikram Solar commissioned India's first floating solar plant, a 10 kW pilot in Rajarhat, Kolkata, in 2013-14, and grew from 12 MW of module capacity in 2009 to about 9.5 GW by January 2026.
deep_cut_fact: The family's solar business grew out of tea: he is a director of Vikram (India) Ltd, a Kolkata company founded in 1974 that makes tea-processing machinery, the original business of the Vikram Group.
notes: Low public profile; the public face of Vikram Solar is MD Gyanesh Chaudhary. Only a sales@ address is published on the site; for formal contact use the company-secretary/investor channels listed on vikramsolar.com investors pages. Exact titles vary across sources (some call him Vikram Group chairman).

name: Jyotsna Gautam Kulkarni
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd (NSE: KIRLOSENG); no executive role found
profile: Jyotsna Gautam Kulkarni belongs to the Kirloskar promoter group of Pune-based Kirloskar Oil Engines (KOEL), which makes diesel and gas gensets, engines, and power and water-management equipment. A March 2023 SEBI takeover-regulation disclosure shows she held about 13 million KOEL shares (~8.97%) before that transaction. She has no public executive profile.
interesting_fact: Kirloskar Oil Engines is one of India's largest makers of diesel and gas generator sets, the backup-power equipment that data centres and industry depend on. That makes the family shareholding indirectly relevant to the energy and data-centre theme.

public_contacts.value: https://www.kirloskaroilengines.com (company; investor contacts via Company Secretary)

notes: She is a passive shareholder and I found no public profile or interviews. Alive status is inferred from her 2023 SEBI filing. The only route is via KOEL's Company Secretary (Farah Irani, per 2026 filings). Search results cite investors@kirloskar.com, but I could not verify it on a primary page. Executive family members (e.g. Gautam Kulkarni, former KOEL executive vice chairman) are more natural guests.

name: Atul Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Retired as Chairman of Kirloskar Oil Engines on 31 Mar 2026 (age 70); remains on boards incl. Kirloskar Industries and Kirloskar Pneumatic (non-executive)
profile: Fourth-generation member of Pune's Kirloskar industrial family. Joined the group in 1978 and led Kirloskar Oil Engines (diesel engines, gensets, pumps, power solutions) for decades as vice-chairman, chairman, CMD and executive chairman; brother Rahul Kirloskar succeeded him as KOEL chair in April 2026. Former MCCIA president and past chair of CII's National Committee on Defence.
interesting_fact: He stepped down from KOEL in a two-line letter citing only that he had reached 70, handing the chair to his brother Rahul, with Gauri Kirloskar as vice-chair.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1978 as a trainee at Kirloskar Cummins, and by December 1981 was Chief Executive of Cummins Diesel Sales and Services; he became EVP of Kirloskar Oil Engines in Nov 1984 and MD the following year.
notes: Now retired from KOEL chair; good elder-statesman voice on Indian engines/backup power (gensets relevant to data centers). Education sources conflict (COEP/IIM-C vs. other listings), so don't cite his degrees.

name: Rahul Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd (from April 2026); Chairman, Kirloskar Pneumatic Co.
profile: Rahul C. Kirloskar is a fourth-generation member of India's Kirloskar engineering family with 34+ years in the group. He became MD of Kirloskar Pneumatic in 1993 and its chairman in 1998, ran exports for Kirloskar Oil Engines 2001-2012, and succeeded his brother Atul as KOEL chairman when Atul retired on 31 March 2026.
interesting_fact: He took over the KOEL chair from his brother Atul Kirloskar, who retired at 70 in March 2026, with Gauri Kirloskar becoming vice-chairperson alongside her MD role; KOEL makes gensets and engines widely used for backup power.
deep_cut_fact: He personally founded Kirloskar Chillers (HVAC/refrigeration) and has chaired both the CII Pune Council and the Maharashtra State CII Council; from 2001-2012 he led KOEL's push to expand exports for the whole Kirloskar Group.
notes: Good energy/data-center angle: KOEL gensets are used for data-center backup power. Kirloskar Pneumatic (where he is chairman) is a separate listed company with its own IR. Route via KOEL corporate inbox.

name: Gaurav Swarup
current_role: Co-Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata); long-time Chairman, KSB Ltd (India)
profile: Third-generation leader (with brother Vikram Swarup, Chairman) of Paharpur Cooling Towers, India's market leader in industrial cooling towers and air-cooled heat exchangers for power, petrochemical and steel plants, which also has packaging and real-estate interests. He was its MD from 1993. In July 2024 Paharpur bought a controlling stake in thyssenkrupp Industries India, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: Paharpur took control of thyssenkrupp's Indian engineering arm (cement, mining, energy and sugar equipment) in 2024. He and Vikram called TKIL 'a highly successful and well-regarded entity'.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2016 he became President of the All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE), the FICCI-allied employers' body, at its 82nd AGM. He has also chaired pump maker KSB Ltd's Indian board since 2009.
notes: Paharpur also makes dry/air-cooled systems (SPG Dry Cooling), which fit the data-center cooling theme. The contact page lists only general and regional company inboxes, none specific to him. The KSB chairmanship dates from 2009 (marketscreener) and should be rechecked before citing.

name: Vikram Swarup
current_role: Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata)
profile: Vikram Swarup chairs family-owned Paharpur Cooling Towers (est. 1949, Kolkata), a major global maker of wet, dry and adiabatic cooling towers for power plants, HVAC, oil & gas, chemicals and heavy industry, alongside co-chairman Gaurav Swarup. A director since 1993, he has expanded the group into engineering; in 2024 Paharpur took majority control of thyssenkrupp's Indian unit, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: In 2024 Paharpur Cooling Towers became majority shareholder of thyssenkrupp Industries India, which was renamed TKIL Industries - a supplier of equipment for cement, mining, energy and sugar plants.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts or interviews found. Strong energy/data-center fit (industrial and power-plant cooling, dry/adiabatic coolers). Company HQ switchboard and support@paharpur.com are the published routes. Don't confuse with author/diplomat Vikas Swarup.

name: Lynn J Good
current_role: Retired Chair & CEO of Duke Energy (retired April 1, 2025); director of Morgan Stanley and Caterpillar
profile: Lynn Good, from Fairfield, Ohio, spent two decades at Arthur Andersen (one of its first female partners in the Midwest) before joining Cinergy/Duke, becoming Duke Energy CFO, then CEO in 2013 and chair in 2016. She steered Duke's coal-to-clean transition and grid and nuclear plans, retiring in April 2025 (succeeded by Harry Sideris).
interesting_fact: She has been a leading voice for the U.S. nuclear industry, serving on the board of the World Association of Nuclear Operators and as past chair of the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations; EEI gave her its Thomas A. Edison Legacy Award.
deep_cut_fact: Her math-teacher father sat with her over the college catalog and steered her to the equivalent of computer science; she told NPR she had 'never seen a computer' before college (she graduated from Miami University in systems analysis and accounting).
notes: Retired from Duke, so Duke corporate channels are no longer hers; no personal website/social accounts or published office contact found. Strong energy-transition/nuclear/load-growth guest; best route likely via board/industry networks (EEI, Morgan Stanley/Caterpillar corporate secretaries).

name: Neil Gagnon
current_role: Principal, Gagnon Securities LLC and Gagnon Advisors LLC (New York investment managers)
profile: New York small-cap investor whose firms, Gagnon Securities and Gagnon Advisors, take concentrated stakes in small public companies. He appears as an insider of engine and power-system maker Power Solutions International (PSIX) via a large shareholding, not as an operator; Gagnon Advisors still filed 13F reports in Nov 2026.
interesting_fact: His personal and firm holdings are frequently large enough to cross SEC 5-10% reporting thresholds; in 2025 he reported a ~5% stake in NYSE-listed Chinese lender CNFinance alongside his firms.
notes: Very private; almost no press profile. Only published contact found is the Gagnon Advisors office, 1370 Avenue of the Americas, New York (main line 212-554-5000 per its SEC 13F: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1599466/000101905626000153/primary_doc.xml). Firm sites did not load. Latest personal SEC filing: Mar 2025.

name: Jeffrey Clay Sell
current_role: CEO, X-Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: XE), Rockville, MD - advanced small modular reactors (Xe-100) and TRISO-X fuel
profile: J. Clay Sell (b. 1967, Texas) was U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy (2005-08), effectively DOE's COO, after years as an energy-policy staffer in Congress and the White House. After eight years running Hunt Energy Horizons, he became X-energy's CEO in 2019, leading it to a Dow SMR construction permit, an Amazon/AEP deal and a Nasdaq listing.
interesting_fact: X-energy's Xe-100 project with Dow on the Texas Gulf Coast won a construction permit for what X-energy calls a historic nuclear-powered industrial site; Sell credited the NRC for granting it earlier than expected.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career on the staff of Texas congressman Mac Thornberry (1995-99), led the Bush-Cheney transition's energy policy team, and holds an accounting BBA from Texas Tech and a JD from UT Austin; before X-energy he spent eight years building Hunt Energy Horizons' renewables portfolio.
notes: Excellent fit (nuclear SMRs powering data centers - Amazon is an investor/partner). Frequent conference speaker and policy voice; press releases name Robert McEntyre (Corporate Communications) as media contact via media@x-energy.com.

name: Shai Yeshayahu Weil
current_role: Independent Director (Compensation Committee), Enlight Renewable Energy (NASDAQ/TASE: ENLT); chairman of Har Tuv Group, Lumen Capital, Essence Partners and Minrav Group
profile: Dr. Shai Weil, an Israeli investor and executive, has sat on Enlight Renewable Energy's board since November 2009. He is an executive/partner in companies across industry, tech, real estate and services (Milgam, Pango, AllCloud, Minrav, Israel Post) and chairs Har Tuv Group, Lumen Capital, Essence Partners and Minrav.
interesting_fact: He joined Enlight's board in November 2009, making him one of the longest-serving directors of what is now one of Israel's largest renewable-energy companies.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a doctorate (D.P.S.) in International Business and Management from Pace University in New York, plus an M.S. from Boston University, and sits on the board of JGIVE, a nonprofit dedicated to cultivating a culture of philanthropy in Israel.
notes: Net worth here is from SEC insider holdings (~$85M), not a billionaire. Not a public-facing figure; best route is Enlight's corporate contact form or via the companies he chairs. The 20-F's only listed contact is the General Counsel (not used here as a press route).

name: Joshua Ian Weinstein
current_role: CEO, Carnival Corporation Ltd.; director, Chipotle Mexican Grill; Chairman, Cruise Lines International Association
profile: New York-born lawyer (Penn; NYU Law) who joined Carnival's legal department in 2002 and rose through treasurer (2007-17), president of Carnival UK (P&O Cruises, Cunard) and COO before becoming CEO in August 2022. He steered the post-COVID restart of a 90-plus-ship, eight-brand fleet carrying about 13.5M guests a year.
interesting_fact: He spent a decade as Carnival's treasurer, an unusual finance-and-legal route to running the world's largest cruise company, and now also chairs the cruise industry's trade body, CLIA.
deep_cut_fact: Before Carnival he was a corporate associate at Skadden, Arps (1999-2001) and Greenberg Traurig (2001-02); he is also a trustee of the Perez Art Museum Miami.
notes: Goes by Josh. The data-center/AI focus tag looks off: his wealth is Carnival stock, and the relevant link to the podcast is limited (possibly shipboard energy/LNG fuel). Route via Carnival Chief Communications Office (Jody Venturoni).

name: David Alan Kennedy
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Dell Technologies (interim from Sept 2025, permanent since Nov 24, 2025)
profile: David Kennedy (49) is a Dell lifer who joined in 1998 and rose through finance and sales operations: CFO of the Client Solutions Group (2017-20), COO of Global Sales (2020-23) and SVP Global Business Operations, Finance, before succeeding Yvonne McGill as CFO. He oversees finance, IR, corporate development and Dell Financial Services as AI servers drive record revenue.
interesting_fact: In his first full year as CFO, Dell posted record quarterly revenue of $47 billion in Q2 FY27 and raised guidance on accelerating AI-server demand.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CFO he spent three years running Dell's global sales operations as COO for Global Sales, an unusual operations-side path to the CFO chair; he has been at Dell since 1998, more than half his life.
notes: Low public profile outside earnings calls. Route via Dell media relations; same company contacts as Michael Dell's profile in lane 000.

name: April S Arnzen
current_role: EVP and Chief People Officer, Micron Technology; President of the Micron Foundation
profile: April Arnzen (55) leads Micron's global people strategy and also oversees its global communications and marketing organisation and the Micron Foundation's philanthropy. She joined Micron in 1996 and rose through HR roles to SVP HR (2017), Chief People Officer (2020) and EVP (2023). Her wealth reflects Micron stock held as an insider during the AI memory (HBM) boom.
interesting_fact: Because communications and marketing report into her people organisation, she oversees Micron's corporate communications team, which is the company's press desk.
deep_cut_fact: A Micron lifer: she joined the Boise memory maker in December 1996 and has spent ~30 years there. She earned a BS in HR management and marketing at the University of Idaho and completed the Stanford GSB Executive Program in 2018.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; reachable via Micron corporate communications (which sits in her organisation). Good angle: workforce for U.S. fab build-out (Idaho/New York) and AI memory demand.

name: Ricardo Alejandro Torres
current_role: Executive Vice President and Director, Pampa Energía (NYSE: PAM; board member since Nov 2005, mandate to end-2028)
profile: Argentine executive (b. 1958): IRSA financial director 1993-2001 and Darwin Inversiones partner before joining Pampa Energía, Argentina's largest integrated power company (generation, transmission, oil & gas, petrochemicals). He chaired distributor Edenor 2012-2021 (CEO 2015-2021) and is a partner in Todos Capital and Pop Argentina.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Pampa Energía's board since November 2005 and, as chairman and later CEO of Edenor until 2021, ran one of Argentina's largest electricity distributors.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy he is an education advocate: he chairs La Fundación Observatorio Argentinos por la Educación (an education-data NGO) and sits on the management board of Fundación Pampa Energía. He trained as a public accountant at the University of Buenos Aires and holds an MBA from Austral University.
notes: Wealth estimate is from SEC insider holdings (Form 4 as VP, Buenos Aires). Good angle: Argentine power/Vaca Muerta gas. No personal social accounts verified. Formal route via Pampa IR; education foundation is a warm hook.

name: Aman Joshi
current_role: Chief Commercial Officer, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), leading global sales and business development since Jan 2024
profile: Commercial chief at fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy, whose on-site solid-oxide power systems have become a go-to fast power source for AI data centers. He joined in 2024 after 20+ years at GE across GE Capital, Corporate, Aviation, Power and Vernova; his wealth figure reflects Bloom stock awards after the share price surge.
interesting_fact: From 2018 to 2024 he was global GM of GE's aeroderivative gas turbine business, working with utilities and policymakers; the same 'bring your own power' pitch now drives his fuel-cell sales to data-center developers.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an energy dealmaker he trained in finance and governance: he is a member of both the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, and held business-unit CFO roles at GE Vernova.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast since he sells Bloom's data-center power deals. Route via Bloom media relations (Katja Gagen). Did not verify a personal LinkedIn (search budget exhausted).

name: Dawn E Hudson
current_role: Independent director, NVIDIA (since 2013; chairs Compensation Committee); former CMO of the NFL
profile: Marketing executive (b. ~1957) who spent 13 years at ad agencies (D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles, Omnicom), then ran Pepsi-Cola North America as President (2002) and CEO (2005-07), was Vice Chairman of The Parthenon Group (2009-14) and NFL Chief Marketing Officer (2014-18). Her wealth stems largely from NVIDIA stock earned as a director since 2013; she also sat on IPG's board until its Omnicom merger.
interesting_fact: She joined NVIDIA's board in 2013, long before the AI boom, and now chairs the compensation committee that sets Jensen Huang's pay at one of the world's most valuable companies.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Pepsi-Cola North America she simultaneously led PepsiCo's foodservice division as CEO (2005-07), and earlier held board seats at Lowe's (2001-2015) and Allergan (2008-2014).

public_contacts.value: shareholdermeeting@nvidia.com (NVIDIA corporate secretary; official channel for communications to the board/named directors - intended for stockholders)

notes: Not to be confused with Dawn Hudson, former CEO of the Film Academy (different person). Wealth is from NVIDIA director equity (~$82M), not founder-level. Low public profile since NFL; no personal site/social found.

name: Adam Singolda
current_role: Founder and CEO, Taboola (Nasdaq: TBLA), New York
profile: Israeli-born founder of Taboola, which he started in Israel in 2007 and moved to New York; it grew into one of the largest open-web recommendation/advertising platforms (~$1.9B revenue in 2025) and listed via SPAC in 2021. He is now steering Taboola into AI products such as performance platform Realize and the gen-AI answer engine DeeperDive for publishers.
interesting_fact: By 2016 Taboola's recommendation widgets were embedded on 41 of the world's top 50 news sites, including The Guardian and CNN.
deep_cut_fact: Taboola did not start with articles: it began in 2007 as a recommendation engine for video content, raising a $1.5M first round that November, and only expanded to text articles and slideshows around 2010.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly CEO who speaks often about AI and the open web; his personal X/LinkedIn could not be verified (search quota exhausted). Net-worth figure ($82M) is SEC-reported holdings only. AI angle is ad-tech, not infrastructure.

name: Andrew R. Novotny
current_role: Special Advisor to the CEO and Executive Committee member, Constellation Energy (formerly President & CEO of Calpine)
profile: Andrew Novotny is a power trader turned power-generation executive. He joined Calpine in 2012 as VP of power trading, rose to EVP commercial operations (2018), COO (2021), president (2023) and CEO. After Constellation acquired Calpine in January 2026 he became SEVP of Constellation Power Operations and is now special advisor to CEO Joe Dominguez.
interesting_fact: His insider stake comes from the Calpine deal: on 7 Jan 2026 his Calpine shares converted into about 299,000 Constellation shares as Constellation, America's largest clean-power producer, absorbed Calpine's gas and geothermal fleet.
deep_cut_fact: Before Calpine he was VP of financial gas and power trading at BG Group and a VP at Duke Energy; he graduated magna cum laude in economics from Vanderbilt and was a Jones Scholar at Rice's MBA program. He sits on the board of the Greater Houston Partnership.
