interesting_fact: He led Atmos as CEO for about seven years (2010–2017), a period of heavy investment in pipeline-safety replacement that made it one of the best-performing US utility stocks. He has stayed on as chairman since then.
deep_cut_fact: Before running a utility he practised energy law, focused on utility rate and regulatory matters. He was general counsel at interstate gas-pipeline companies and then GC and chief compliance officer at Piedmont Natural Gas. He holds bachelor's and master's degrees from Wichita State and a law degree from Washburn University.
notes: boardofdirectors@atmosenergy.com is Atmos's published address for contacting the board (via lead director Nancy Quinn), not a personal or press line, so use it sparingly. Low public profile; for a podcast, current CEO Kevin Akers may be the more accessible Atmos voice.

name: Jeremy L. Goebel
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Commercial Officer, Plains All American Pipeline (PAA/PAGP), Houston
profile: Jeremy Goebel runs the commercial side of Plains All American, one of the largest US crude-oil and NGL midstream operators with a large Permian Basin footprint. He joined Plains in 2013 in M&A/business development, became SVP Strategic Planning & Acquisitions, EVP Commercial in 2019 and CCO in 2021; his wealth comes from Plains equity awards.
interesting_fact: He was groomed as successor to long-time Plains commercial chief Harry Pefanis: in 2018 he was promoted to the new role of Sr. Group VP, Commercial, reporting directly to Pefanis, with 'increasing responsibilities' for Plains' commercial activities.
deep_cut_fact: A Louisiana State University chemical engineer (MBA, UT Austin), he started in engineering and business management in Chevron's downstream operations, then was Director of Operations at Authentix (product authentication/fuel marking) and worked at energy investment bank Simmons & Company.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder); low public profile. Best route via Plains media relations. Good guest angle: Permian crude/NGL logistics and gas demand from data centres.

name: Lars Norell
current_role: Executive Chairman, Edly Inc. (NY education-finance fintech) since June 2024; Managing Member, Start Capital LLC; co-founder and former co-CEO of Altus Power
profile: Former lawyer (Cadwalader, UVA JD) turned structured-credit banker at Credit Suisse, Merrill Lynch (co-head US structured credit products) and Cohen & Co. He co-founded Altus Power, a commercial-scale solar and storage owner, taking it public via SPAC in 2021. Left as co-CEO in April 2024. TPG Rise Climate bought Altus for $2.2B in 2025, and he now invests through Start Capital.
interesting_fact: Altus Power, which he co-founded, became the largest US owner of commercial-scale solar and was taken private by TPG in a $2.2B all-cash deal, at a 66% premium to the unaffected price.
deep_cut_fact: His investment firm Start Capital describes its focus as 're-industrialization' across power, industry and education. Through it he was an early investor and board member of Edly, which pioneered income-based private student loans and NIL funding for college athletes (NILLY, co-founded by NBA champion Kendrick Perkins).
notes: His 'TenPercentOwner' AMPS holding is obsolete since TPG took Altus private in 2025. He started his career as an attorney at Cadwalader in 1998. Undergraduate degree from IUM (International University of Monaco). Best route is probably via Edly or LinkedIn (not verified).

name: William D. Watkins
current_role: Chairperson of the Board, Nextpower Inc. (formerly Nextracker, NASDAQ: NXT); director (reported chair since 2024) of Flex Ltd.
profile: Veteran hardware executive who ran Seagate's disk-drive operations and was its CEO 2004-2009, after joining via the 1996 Conner Peripherals merger. He then led LED maker Bridgelux (CEO 2010-13) and flow-battery company Imergy Power Systems (CEO 2013-16). He has been on Flex's board since 2009 and chairs Nextpower, the solar tracker and power-tech company spun out of Flex.
interesting_fact: As Seagate COO/CEO he pushed engineers to design drives around common parts (only ~2% of products shared components), starting with cutting the number of screws per drive and working up to read/write heads.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Maracaibo, Venezuela, into an oil-industry family that moved to Canada, Wyoming and then Pampa, Texas, he enlisted after high school (1971) as an Army medic caring for injured Vietnam veterans in Missouri. After graduating from UT he hitchhiked to California and got his first tech job at floppy-disk maker Xidex.
notes: Age 73 (2026 proxy). Good fit for solar/energy-storage/data-center power angle (Nextpower, Flex power businesses, Imergy flow batteries). Known for blunt, quotable interviews. Flex chair title per MarketScreener/Zonebourse; the Nextpower chair role is confirmed in its July 2026 DEF 14A.

name: Tanoira Santiago Martinez
current_role: Executive Vice President, LNG & Integrated Gas, and Alternate Director, YPF S.A. (Argentina)
profile: Santiago Martínez Tanoira is an industrial engineer (ITBA, Universidad Austral MBA) and a YPF veteran since 1998. He has worked across petrochemicals, chemicals and Mendoza upstream operations and served as upstream EVP (2016-17). Since May 2020 he has led YPF's LNG and integrated-gas business, central to the company's plan to export Vaca Muerta shale gas as LNG ('Argentina LNG').
interesting_fact: He oversees the gas side of Argentina's push to become an LNG exporter. YPF's CEO has described Argentina LNG as a multi-billion-dollar centerpiece of the company's strategy for monetising Vaca Muerta gas.
deep_cut_fact: He spent part of his career in Spain. From 2008 he was Basic Petrochemical and Intermediate Products Director at Repsol Química, then returned to Argentina as YPF's Chemistry Director (2011-12) and sat on the board of fertiliser maker Profertil before switching to upstream oil and gas in Mendoza.
notes: A corporate executive, not a founder; his wealth comes from SEC-reported YPF holdings. A relevant LNG and gas voice for an energy podcast. Route requests through YPF media relations. Emails were taken from a YPF release syndicated in April 2025; re-check them on ypf.com before use.

name: Corbin J Robertson Iii
current_role: Director, Natural Resource Partners (NRP); principal, co-owner and director of Quintana Minerals Corp.; owner of CIII Capital Management (Houston)

Robertson III, 55, is a Houston private-equity investor and part of the Quintana Minerals family (Cullen/Robertson) behind Natural Resource Partners, a coal/minerals royalty and soda-ash partnership. name: Gale E Klappa
current_role: Non-executive Chairman of the Board, WEC Energy Group; Director, Associated Banc-Corp
profile: Utility veteran (45+ years) who was CFO of Southern Company before joining Wisconsin Energy in 2003; as chairman/CEO he led the 2015 Integrys acquisition that created WEC Energy Group (≈4.7M electric and gas customers in WI, IL, MI, MN). He returned as CEO 2017-2024 after his successor's medical setback and is now non-executive chairman as WEC builds generation for Midwest data-center demand.

He returned to give UWM's December 2025 commencement address.

No published press email found; WEC media relations is reachable via company newsroom/phone hotline.

Grady Jolly of the US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit; at the Senate Intelligence Committee she focused on the law of intelligence collection and covert action. name: Douglas V Reynolds
current_role: President & CEO (since Dec 2012) and Director, Energy Services of America (Nasdaq: ESOA), Huntington WV; founder/managing director of HD Media
profile: Huntington-born (1976) attorney and businessman who runs Energy Services of America, a pipeline, utility and electrical contractor serving gas, water and power customers in Appalachia and beyond. name: Nitesh Sharan
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Quantinuum (QNT), Broomfield, Colorado (since 6 April 2026)

profile: Bill Parrett (b. 1945) is a CPA who joined Deloitte in 1967 out of St. Francis College in Brooklyn. He rose to lead Deloitte's US firm and then served as global CEO of Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu from 2003 to 2007. Since retiring he has been a career audit-committee chair, on the boards of Blackstone, Oracle, UBS, Thermo Fisher, Eastman Kodak and Thoughtworks.

name: Ronald J Tanski
current_role: Independent Director, National Fuel Gas Co (since 2014) and CMS Energy / Consumers Energy; retired President & CEO of National Fuel Gas (2013-2019)
profile: Buffalo, NY energy executive (age 73) who spent his whole career at National Fuel Gas, an integrated gas utility, pipeline/storage and Appalachian upstream (Seneca Resources) company, rising from staff attorney to Treasurer/PFO, President/COO and CEO before retiring in 2019. notes: Retired, low public profile; reachable only via corporate channels (NFG corporate secretary or CMS Energy). Good natural-gas/utility angle for data-center power demand in the Northeast and Michigan.

He joined in 2017 after a decade as GC of natural-gas compression firm Archrock and its predecessors (Exterran, Universal Compression); his wealth (~$31m) is Quanta stock from that tenure.

profile: Milton 'Tom' Tormey is one of five co-founders (with Richard Lowenthal, Harjinder Bhade, Praveen Mandal and Dave Baxter) of Coulomb Technologies, launched in 2007 in Campbell, California, to build networked EV charging before many EVs were on the road. current_role: Co-founder of Dagger (dagger.io), a programmable CI/CD and AI-agent workflow engine; Docker founder
profile: New York-born, France-raised engineer (b. 1983) who co-founded dotCloud in Paris in 2008, went through Y Combinator in 2010, and open-sourced Docker in 2013, popularising Linux containers that now underpin cloud and data-center software. current_role: Fujitsu Professor of Computer Science and AI at MIT (EECS/CSAIL); co-founder, CTO and board chairman, Cambridge Mobile Telematics

notes: An academic and approachable through MIT; hari@csail.mit.edu is his MIT address as published on his MIT CSAIL and EECS profile pages. The CMT website blocked automated access, so no CMT press contact was captured. His expertise in congestion control and networking is relevant to data centers.

profile: Machine-learning engineer (Tsinghua BS, Yale CS PhD per profiles) who worked at Yahoo, Google and Airbnb before co-founding Moveworks in 2016 with Bhavin Shah, Varun Singh and Vaibhav Nivargi. Moveworks built an LLM-powered enterprise AI assistant and was bought by ServiceNow for about $2.85bn, ServiceNow's largest acquisition.

It launched in 2014 and went on to power a large share of direct answers in Google Search and Google Home. He then worked on booking-recommendation algorithms at Airbnb before co-founding Moveworks.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Bhavin Shah is Moveworks' public face. His post-acquisition title comes from a single low-quality profile. 'Jiang Chen' is a common name, so confirm through Moveworks or ServiceNow before outreach. ServiceNow's press office is the only published route.

current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Moveworks (acquired by ServiceNow, deal closed 15 Dec 2025); current title inside ServiceNow not confirmed

Press now likely routed via ServiceNow communications.

name: Hannu Valtonen
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, Avrea (GitHub Actions CI/CD infrastructure startup); co-founder and former CPO of Aiven
profile: Finnish engineer who co-founded Helsinki-based Aiven, the managed open-source data platform (PostgreSQL, Kafka, ClickHouse, etc.) valued at ~$3bn, and served as its Chief Product Officer. He has since stepped back from Aiven operations and now leads Avrea, which sells fast GitHub Actions runners, sandboxes and CI tooling for engineers and AI agents.

deep_cut_fact: Aiven's founders met at antivirus maker F-Secure, where Valtonen was a senior engineer/lead architect; he, Oskari Saarenmaa and Mika Eloranta left to run a PostgreSQL consultancy (Ohmu) for Nordic firms before pivoting in 2015 to productize that expertise as a multi-cloud data platform.

name: Oskari Saarenmaa
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Aiven (Helsinki)
profile: Finnish software architect who, with fellow F-Secure alumni (Hannu Valtonen, Heikki Nousiainen, Mika Eloranta), ran the open-source database consultancy Ohmu before founding Aiven in 2015. Aiven runs managed open-source data infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Kafka, etc.) across clouds and became a $3B unicorn. name: Christopher Hopper
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Aurora Solar (San Francisco); CEO until 2026, when Charlie Herche took over
profile: Munich-born engineer Christopher Hopper (Imperial College MEng 2011, Stanford MBA) co-founded Aurora Solar in 2013 with fellow GSB student Samuel Adeyemo after a Kenya solar project showed how painful PV system design was. Aurora's cloud software for solar design and sales reached a ~$4bn valuation; Hopper led it as CEO for over a decade and is now executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Aurora began when Hopper and Adeyemo, as first-year Stanford MBAs, spent seven months designing a solar system for a school in Nairobi that took just two weeks to install - so they built software to make design as easy as installation.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up spending hours after school in his parents' engineering firm in Germany; at Imperial he co-founded the student humanitarian energy group e.quinox and helped launch off-grid solar start-up BBOXX, and won Imperial's Alumni Entrepreneur Award in 2023.
notes: Aurora PR & communications director is Karen DeVincent-Reinbold (press@aurorasolar.com). Accessible, media-friendly founder. Executive Chairman title is from a March 2026 release; verify before citing.

name: Samuel Adeyemo
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Duranta (Seattle applied geospatial-AI lab/landscaping software); co-founder of Aurora Solar
profile: Nairobi-born Sam Adeyemo (UChicago economics, ex-JPMorgan, Stanford MBA and MS in Earth Sciences) co-founded Aurora Solar in 2013 with Chris Hopper. Aurora's remote solar-design and sales software became a ~$4B-valued unicorn; he served as COO/director until about 2023. In 2024 he co-founded Duranta, which raised a $7M seed (Base10) in 2025 to build 'Aidan', a vision model that measures properties from aerial imagery.
interesting_fact: Aurora started with a 2012 side gig: as Stanford MBA students, he and Hopper installed a 220-panel solar system for a school in Nairobi and found designing it harder than installing it, which inspired remote solar-design software.
deep_cut_fact: He attended the University of Chicago on scholarship (AB Economics, 2004), where he was Phi Beta Kappa, a student marshal and chairman of the Council on University Programming, before starting his career as a JPMorgan analyst.

public_contacts.value: Previously interviewed on the SunCast podcast (Episode 536, with Chris Hopper)

notes: Accessible, podcast-friendly founder and a good energy-to-AI story (solar software to geospatial AI). Also ran Vituo Technologies, installing small solar systems in emerging markets, before Aurora. Duranta is a small startup, so hello@ likely reaches the founders.

name: Sherry Wei
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Bumblebee Networks (cloud-managed intelligent edge networking, founded 2023); founder of Aviatrix

Aviatrix, bootstrapped at first, reached a ~$2.5B valuation; she served as CTO/CPO before stepping back (Doug Merritt became CEO) and in 2023 co-founded Bumblebee Networks.

deep_cut_fact: She named the company Aviatrix, a word meaning 'female pilot', and recruited Cisco colleagues to join the bootstrapped startup in 2014.
notes: No longer runs Aviatrix; route via Bumblebee Networks. Speaks at telecom events (International Telecoms Week). Cloud-networking expertise relevant to data-center topics.

Enpal expanded into batteries, heat pumps, EV charging and energy supply, and in Jan 2026 reported its first year above EUR1bn revenue with positive free cash flow.

notes: Media-friendly founder (many interviews with EU-Startups, OMR, pv-magazine, McKinsey case study). Strausberg birthplace from gruender.de (https://www.gruender.de/gruendung/enpal-gruender-mario-kohle/); 2008 student-to-CEO detail from KfW (https://www.kfw.de/stories/economy/start-ups/enpal/). name: Yunsup Lee
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Technology Officer, SiFive
profile: Yunsup Lee co-created the open RISC-V instruction set and the first RISC-V processors as a UC Berkeley PhD student, then co-founded SiFive in 2015 with Andrew Waterman and Krste Asanovic to commercialize RISC-V core IP. SiFive's cores ship in 2B+ devices; it raised a $400M Series G in 2026 (~$3.65B valuation) to push into AI data centres, including NVIDIA NVLink Fusion support.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original authors of the RISC-V spec 'from Day 1' and co-designed the first RISC-V microprocessors at Berkeley; SiFive is now targeting AI data-centre CPUs.
deep_cut_fact: His 2016 Berkeley PhD thesis introduced the Hwacha 'decoupled vector-fetch' architecture (committee included David Patterson), and at Hot Chips 2015 he presented Raven3, a 28nm RISC-V vector chip with on-die switched-capacitor DC-DC converters.
notes: Strong data-center fit (RISC-V for AI data centres, $400M 2026 round). Press email is SiFive Corporate Communications (David Miller) as listed on 2026 press releases. Hot Chips slides: https://old.hotchips.org/wp-content/uploads/hc_archives/hc27/HC27.25-Tuesday-Epub/HC27.25.70-Processors-Epub/HC27.25.731-RISC-V-Lee-UCB-V4.with-backup.pdf

name: Avi Baum

notes: Accessible technical leader who regularly blogs and gives interviews (hailo.ai/blog). LinkedIn is linked from Hailo's own leadership page. Edge-AI counterpoint to data-center AI; good on power-efficiency and memory-bandwidth topics.

current_role: Co-Founder & President, Chipper Cash
profile: Maijid Moujaled co-founded Chipper Cash with CEO Ham Serunjogi. Chipper Cash is a fintech app for cross-border payments across Africa, with operations in markets including Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda and the US. It was valued at over $1B, and he serves as its president.

name: Gerald Yao
current_role: Co-founder and Class II Director, FiscalNote Holdings (OTCID: NOTE); Chief Strategy Officer 2014-April 2025
profile: Co-founded FiscalNote in 2013 with high-school friends Tim Hwang and Jonathan Chen. The D.C. company sells AI-driven policy and regulatory intelligence and went public via SPAC in 2022. name: Jonathan Chen
current_role: Co-founder of FiscalNote; current role not confirmed (not in FiscalNote management as of its 2022 listing)
profile: One of three co-founders (with Tim Hwang and Gerald Yao) of FiscalNote, the Washington, D.C. policy/legislative-intelligence software company founded in 2013 that uses AI to analyze and predict legislation and regulation. FiscalNote reached unicorn status and listed on the NYSE via SPAC (Duddell Street) in 2022.

name: Tim Hwang
current_role: Co-founder of FiscalNote; executive chairman since Jan 2025 (role after FiscalNote's March 2026 NYSE delisting not confirmed)
profile: Tim Hwang (b. 1992, East Lansing; raised in Potomac, MD) launched FiscalNote in 2013 while finishing at Princeton, deferring Harvard Business School, with two high-school friends. The Washington, D.C. company uses AI to track and predict legislation and regulation, bought CQ Roll Call in 2018 and listed on the NYSE via SPAC in 2022. name: Amir Husain
current_role: Founder and board member, Avathon (formerly SparkCognition); Chairman, WorldQuant Foundry venture studio
profile: Amir Husain, an Austin AI entrepreneur and author, founded SparkCognition in 2013 (now Avathon, industrial AI; valued at more than $1B) and was CEO until the end of 2023; he stays on its board. He also founded SkyGrid (a Boeing JV, later acquired by Boeing) and SGS, and now chairs the venture studio WorldQuant Foundry.

deep_cut_fact: A prolific inventor-author: he holds 62 U.S. patents in AI, autonomy and distributed systems. Beyond 'The Sentient Machine' he has written books on generative art and a 2026 book, 'Algorithms from Scratch', and he runs a YouTube channel, 'Deep Tech with Amir'.

public_contacts.value: https://amirhusain.com/contact/ (for speaking, media and business enquiries)

name: Qian Jun
current_role: Founder & CEO, Vastai Technologies (瀚博半导体 / Vastaitec), Shanghai
profile: Qian Jun (钱军), a ~30-year chip designer (LSI, Cisco, AMD), founded Vastai Technologies in Dec 2018 with ex-AMD Fellow Zhang Lei. Vastai makes data-center GPUs and AI inference chips (SV102, 7nm SG100); backers include Alibaba, Kuaishou and MediaTek. It began A-share IPO tutoring in 2025 at a ~RMB 10.5bn valuation.

deep_cut_fact: An SJTU alum with a 1995 master's from the University of Iowa, he started as a design engineer at LSI Logic, then spent 11 years at Cisco (1998-2009, leaving as senior director of hardware engineering) before running GPU SoC design for AMD in Shanghai.
notes: 'Vastaitec' = Vastai Technologies (瀚博半导体). Strong data-center/AI-chip angle; pre-IPO, so may be in a quiet period. Co-founder/CTO Zhang Lei (Louis Zhang) is co-controller.

name: Huang Xiangdong
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Greater Bay Technology (GBT, 巨湾技研), Guangzhou.
profile: Ex-GAC Group VP/chief engineer who ran GAC's R&D Center 2006-2016 (e.g. GS4 SUV) and a South China University of Technology professor. After retiring he co-founded GAC-incubated Greater Bay Technology in 2020 with CEO Pei Feng; it makes extreme-fast-charge Phoenix cells and began all-solid-state cell production in Oct 2026.

deep_cut_fact: He studied automotive engineering in Italy in the 1980s and spent five years as a postdoc at Fiat's research centre before returning to China in 1991 to teach; he then came out of retirement at GAC to start GBT.
notes: Strong battery/energy-storage angle (fast-charge and solid-state). No published personal or press email found; company site was unreachable from here. Some sources call him CTO rather than chairman.

name: Liu Jiping
current_role: Founder and legal representative, Shenzhen Hangshun Chip Technology (航顺芯片, HK32 MCUs)
profile: Jiangxi-born (1982) entrepreneur who sold MCUs, made his first money as a chip distributor, then moved to Shenzhen in 2013 to found Hangshun Chip, a general-purpose 32-bit MCU/SoC designer. Starting with lower-risk LDOs, LCD drivers and memory, Hangshun now ships 300+ ARM Cortex-M0/M3/M4 MCUs and raised a record-setting RMB1bn Series D in Jan 2022.

profile: Chip architect and former director of the CAS Institute of Automation. name: David Golan
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Viz.ai (former CTO); current operating role not found
profile: Israeli machine-learning researcher (PhD in statistics & ML, Tel Aviv University) who, as a Fulbright postdoc at Stanford applying deep learning to medical imaging and genetics, co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and served as CTO. Viz.ai built the first FDA-cleared AI triage system for stroke (2018), now installed in 800+ hospitals in the US and Europe; he remains on the board.

name: Manoj Ramachandran
current_role: Co-founder of Viz.ai; Consultant Orthopaedic & Trauma Surgeon (and reported Director of Innovation) at Barts Health NHS Trust, London; CEO & co-founder of halfloop (per profiles)
profile: London paediatric/young-adult orthopaedic surgeon who co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and David Golan; its FDA-cleared AI care-coordination tools (stroke first, now cardio, vascular, oncology) made it a ~$1bn+ unicorn. He combines NHS practice at Barts with ventures, most recently halfloop (patient data for implant recipients).

name: Fangjin Yang
current_role: Cofounder and CEO, Imply Data (Apache Druid-based real-time analytics / observability warehouse)
profile: Canadian engineer (Waterloo BASc EE, MASc CompE) who worked at Cisco and was a lead engineer at adtech startup Metamarkets, where he co-created open-source real-time database Apache Druid. In 2015 he cofounded Imply with Gian Merlino and Vadim Ogievetsky; it now sells Imply Lumi, an 'observability warehouse' for security and log data.

current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Imply Data
profile: Gian Merlino is an original author of Apache Druid, the open-source real-time analytics database built at Metamarkets, where he led data ingestion after senior roles at Yahoo. In 2015 he co-founded Imply with Fangjin Yang and Vadim Ogievetsky to commercialise Druid (a16z-backed, about $1bn valuation) and remains its CTO.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
current_role: Founder, The Network School; founder, Balaji Fund; author of 'The Network State'

Srinivasan (b. 1980; Stanford EE PhD) co-founded Counsyl (sold to Myriad for $375m), was an a16z general partner, co-founded 21 Inc/Earn.com (sold to Coinbase in 2018, where he became first CTO) and relocation start-up Teleport (2014, sold to Topia). name: Sten Tamkivi
current_role: Partner, Plural (European founder-led VC platform); Founding Partner, Creative Destruction Lab Estonia
profile: Estonian entrepreneur and investor who spent 8+ years as an early Skype executive through its $8.5B sale to Microsoft. notes: Very accessible and public: active on X and LinkedIn, gives interviews (ERR, Estonian World, Seedcamp). Founders Pledge member. Hurun lists him via Teleport, but his wealth is mainly from Skype/Teleport exits. Good podcast guest candidate.
